As exploration in the scope of generalized NLP is much more advanced, it implies the tremendous gap that is still to be addressed amongst all feasible tasks where an opinion, taste, or feelings are inherent, thus creating a need for a solution, where a data fusion could take place.

title: Hausdorff measure for the singularity set of the 3D chemotaxis-Navier-Stokes equations
creator: Xiaomeng Chen, Shuai Li, Lili Wang, Wendong Wang
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Xiaomeng Chen, Shuai Li, Lili Wang, Wendong Wang. Suspensions of aerobic bacteria often develop flows from the interplay of chemotaxis and buoyancy, which is so-called the chemotaxis-Navier-Stokes flow. In 2004, Dombrowski et al. observed that Bacterial flow in a sessile drop related to those in the Boycott effect of sedimentation can carry bioconvective plumes, viewed from below through the bottom of a petri dish, and the horizontal “turbulence” white line near the top is the air-water-plastic contact line.

title: Preprint INR-TH-2023-016
creator: A New Solution to the Strong CP Problem
description: Abstract We suggest a new solution to the strong CP problem. The solution is based on the proper use of the boundary conditions for the QCD generating functional integral. We expand the perturbative boundary conditions to both perturbative and nonperturbative fields integrated in the QCD generating functional integral.

title: Weak localization as a probe of intervalley coherence in graphene multilayers
creator: Nemin Wei, Yongxin Zeng, A. H. MacDonald
description: Abstract Spontaneous intervalley coherence is suspected in several different graphene multilayer systems, but is difficult to confirm because of a paucity of convenient experimental signatures. Here we suggest that magneto-conductance features associated with quantum corrections to Drude conductivity can serve as a smoking gun for intervalley coherence that does not break time-reversal symmetry.

title: Active flux for triangular meshes for compressible flows problems
creator: Rémi Abgrall, Jianfang Lin, Yongle Liu
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Rémi Abgrall, Jianfang Lin, Yongle Liu. In this article, we show how to construct a numerical method for solving hyperbolic problems, whether linear or non-linear, using a continuous representation of the variables and their mean value in each triangular element. This type of approach has already been introduced by Roe, and others, in the multi-dimensional framework under the name of Active Flux, see [ 11 , 12 , 10 , 16 , 7 ] .

title: Institut für Theoretische Physik, Leibniz Universität Hannover
creator: Appelstraße 2, 30167 Hannover, Germany
description: Abstract Scaling limit of the staggered six-vertex model with U_{q}\big(\mathfrak{sl}(2)\big) invariant boundary conditions Holger Frahm \star , Sascha Gehrmann \dagger and Gleb A. Kotousov \ddagger Abstract We study the scaling limit of a statistical system, which is a special case of the integrable inhomogeneous six-vertex model. It possesses U_{q}\big(\mathfrak{sl}(2)\big) invariance due to the choice of open boundary conditions imposed.

title: Topic Shifts as a Proxy for Assessing Politicization in Social Media
creator: Marcelo Sartori Locatelli, Pedro Calais, Matheus Prado Miranda, João Pedro Junho, Tomas Lacerda Muniz, Wagner Meira Jr, Virgilio Almeida
description: Abstract Politicization is a social phenomenon studied by political science characterized by the extent to which ideas and facts are given a political tone. A range of topics, such as climate change, religion and vaccines has been subject to increasing politicization in the media and social media platforms.

title: Proximal algorithm and calibrated cycles
creator: Ryohei Chihara
description: Abstract . We sketch an application of proximal algorithms to the deformation of de Rham currents into cycles, which is presented as a convex optimization problem. Emphasis is placed on the use of total variation denoising for differential forms, specifically in constructing calibrated cycles in calibrated manifolds. 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification 53C38, 90C25, 49J40 1.

title: CaRe-CNN: Cascading Refinement CNN for Myocardial Infarct Segmentation with Microvascular Obstructions
creator: Franz Thaler 1,2 , Matthias A.F. Gsell 1 , Gernot Plank 1 and Martin Urschler 3 1 Gottfried Schatz Research Center: Medical Physics and Biophysics, Medical University of Graz, Graz, Austria 2 Institute of Computer Graphics and Vision, Graz University of Technology, Graz, Austria 3 Institute for Medi
description: Abstract Late gadolinium enhanced (LGE) magnetic resonance (MR) imaging is widely established to assess the viability of myocardial tissue of patients after acute myocardial infarction (MI). We propose the Cascading Refinement CNN (CaRe-CNN), which is a fully 3D, end-to-end trained, 3-stage CNN cascade that exploits the hierarchical structure of such labeled cardiac data.

title: Physics Informed Neural Networks for an Inverse Problem in Peridynamic Models
creator: Fabio V. Difonzo, Luciano Lopez, Sabrina F. Pellegrino
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Fabio V. Difonzo, Luciano Lopez, Sabrina F. Pellegrino. Deep learning is a powerful tool for solving data driven differential problems and has come out to have successful applications in solving direct and inverse problems described by PDEs, even in presence of integral terms.

title: Simultaneous minijets and QGP evolution
creator: \firstname Charles \lastname Gale, \firstname Sangyong \lastname Jeon, \firstname Daniel \lastname Pablos, \firstname Mayank \lastname Singh \fnsep
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by \firstname Charles \lastname Gale, \firstname Sangyong \lastname Jeon, \firstname Daniel \lastname Pablos, \firstname Mayank \lastname Singh \fnsep. Minijets traversing through the QGP formed in heavy-ion collisions deposit significant amount of energy in the bulk medium. They also create gradients in temperatures which alter the flow profile and enhance entropy production. We study the effects of minijets in a simultaneous hydro + jet framework and find that inclusion of minijets requires recalibration of transport properties extracted from the model-to-data comparisons.

title: Uncertainty as a Fairness Measure
creator: Selim Kuzucu selim.kuzucu@metu.edu.tr, Jiaee Cheong jc2208@cam.ac.uk, Hatice Gunes hg410@cam.ac.uk, Sinan Kalkan skalkan@metu.edu.tr
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Selim Kuzucu selim.kuzucu@metu.edu.tr, Jiaee Cheong jc2208@cam.ac.uk, Hatice Gunes hg410@cam.ac.uk, Sinan Kalkan skalkan@metu.edu.tr. Unfair predictions of machine learning (ML) models impede their broad acceptance in real-world settings. Tackling this arduous challenge first necessitates defining what it means for an ML model to be fair. This has been addressed by the ML community with various measures of fairness that depend on the prediction outcomes of the ML models, either at the group-level or the individual-level.

title: Full three-loop Renormalisation of an abelian chiral Gauge Theory with non-anticommuting γ 5 \gamma_{5} in the BMHV Scheme
creator: Dominik Stöckinger, Matthias Weißwange, [2em] Institut für Kern- und Teilchenphysik, TU DresdenZellescher Weg 19, DE-01069 Dresden, Germany
description: Abstract In this work we present a complete three-loop renormalisation of an abelian chiral gauge theory within the Breitenlohner-Maison/’t Hooft-Veltman (BMHV) scheme of dimensional regularisation (DReg). In this scheme the γ 5 \gamma_{5} -matrix appearing in gauge interactions is a non-anticommuting object, leading to a breaking of gauge and BRST invariance.

title: Epidemic models on homogeneous networks : some analytical results
creator: Louis Bremaud, Olivier Giraud, Denis Ullmo
description: Abstract The ability to actually implement epidemic models is a crucial stake for public institutions, as they may be overtaken by the increasing complexity of current models and sometimes tend to revert to less elaborate models such as the SIR.

title: Short-term memory effects in the phototactic behavior of microalgae
creator: Taha Laroussi, Mojtaba Jarrahi, Gabriel Amselem
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Taha Laroussi, Mojtaba Jarrahi, Gabriel Amselem. Phototaxis, the directed motion in response to a light stimulus, is crucial for motile microorganisms that rely on photosynthesis, such as the unicellular microalga Chlamydomonas reinhardtii . It is well known that microalgae adapt to ambient light stimuli. On time scales of several dozen minutes, when stimulated long enough, the response of the microalga evolves as if the light intensity were decreasing [Mayer, Nature (1968)].

title: Phantom-Powered Nested Sampling
creator: Joshua G. Albert
description: Abstract We introduce a novel technique within the Nested Sampling framework to enhance efficiency of the computation of Bayesian evidence, a critical component in scientific data analysis. In higher dimensions, Nested Sampling relies on Markov Chain-based likelihood-constrained prior samplers, which generate numerous ’phantom points’ during parameter space exploration.

title: Machine Vision-Enabled Sports Performance Analysis
creator: Timilehin B. Aderinola, Hananeh Younesian, Cathy Goulding, Darragh Whelan, Brian Caulfield, Georgiana Ifrim
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Timilehin B. Aderinola, Hananeh Younesian, Cathy Goulding, Darragh Whelan, Brian Caulfield, Georgiana Ifrim. Goal: This study investigates the feasibility of monocular 2D markerless motion capture (MMC) using a single smartphone to measure jump height, velocity, flight time, contact time, and range of motion (ROM) during motor tasks. Methods: Sixteen healthy adults performed three repetitions of selected tests while their body movements were recorded using force plates, optical motion capture (OMC), and a smartphone camera.

title: A hierarchy of Plateau problems and the approximation of Plateau’s laws via the Allen–Cahn equation
creator: Francesco Maggi, Michael Novack, Daniel Restrepo
description: Abstract . We introduce a diffused interface formulation of the Plateau problem, where the Allen–Cahn energy 𝒜 ​ 𝒞 ε \mathcal{AC}_{\varepsilon} is minimized under a volume constraint v v and a spanning condition on the level sets of the densities.

title: Muted : Multilingual Targeted Offensive Speech Identification and Visualization
creator: Christoph Tillmann, Aashka Trivedi, Sara Rosenthal, Santosh Borse
description: Abstract Offensive language such as hate, abuse, and profanity (HAP) occurs in various content on the web. While previous work has mostly dealt with sentence level annotations, there have been a few recent attempts to identify offensive spans as well.

title: Combining Game Design and Data Visualization to Inform Plastics Policy: Fostering Collaboration between Science, Decision-Makers, and Artificial Intelligence
creator: A Samuel Pottinger, Nivedita Biyani, Roland Geyer, Douglas J McCauley, Magali de Bruyn, Molly R Morse, Neil Nathan, Kevin Koy, Ciera Martinez
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by A Samuel Pottinger, Nivedita Biyani, Roland Geyer, Douglas J McCauley, Magali de Bruyn, Molly R Morse, Neil Nathan, Kevin Koy, Ciera Martinez. Abstract : This multi-disciplinary case study details how a public web application combines information and game design to visualize effects of user-defined policies intended to reduce plastic waste.

title: 1PN effective binary Lagrangian for the gravity-Kalb-Ramond sector in the conservative regime
creator: Vegard Undheim, Alex B. Nielsen, Eirik Eik Svanes
description: Abstract Within the framework of string theory, a number of new fields are possible correcting the Einstein-Hilbert action, including a Kalb-Ramond two-form field. In this work we derive explicitly first order relativistic corrections to conservative dynamics with a Kalb-Ramond field, using the effective field theory approach. The resulting additional terms in the Lagrangian governing conservative binary dynamics are presented explicitly.

title: The full version of this paper appeared in proceedings of ECAI 2023 The Problem of Coherence in Natural Language Explanations of Recommendations
creator: Jakub Raczyński, Mateusz Lango, Jerzy Stefanowski
description: Abstract Providing natural language explanations for recommendations is particularly useful from the perspective of a non-expert user. Although several methods for providing such explanations have recently been proposed, we argue that an important aspect of explanation quality has been overlooked in their experimental evaluation.

title: Baryon-to-Meson Ratios in Jets from Au+Au and p p + p p Collisions at s NN = 200 \sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=200 GeV
description: Abstract Measurements at RHIC and the LHC show strongly enhanced baryon-to-meson yield ratios at intermediate transverse momenta ( p T p_{\rm{T}} ) in high-energy nuclear collisions compared to p p + p p baseline. This enhancement is attributed to the following QGP effects: strong hydrodynamic flow and parton recombination.

title: AFDM-SCMA: A Promising Waveform for Massive Connectivity over High Mobility Channels Thanks: Qu Luo and Pei Xiao are with the 5G & 6G Innovation Centre, University of Surrey, U. K. (email: {q.u.luo, p.xiao}@surrey.ac.uk). Zilong Liu and Thomos, Nikolaos are with the School of Computer Science and El
creator: Qu Luo, Pei Xiao, Zilong Liu
description: Abstract This paper studies the affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM)-empowered sparse code multiple access (SCMA) system, referred to as AFDM-SCMA, for supporting massive connectivity in high-mobility environments. First, by placing the sparse codewords on the AFDM chirp subcarriers, the input-output (I/O) relation of AFDM-SCMA systems is presented.

title: Density Descent for Diversity Optimization Conference: Genetic and Evolutionary Computation Conference; July 14–18, 2024; Melbourne, VIC, Australia Genetic and Evolutionary Computation Conference (GECCO ’24), July 14–18, 2024, Melbourne, VIC, Australia DOI: 10.1145/3638529.3654001 ISBN: 979-8-4007-0
creator: David H. Lee, Anishalakshmi V. Palaparthi, Matthew C. Fontaine, Bryon Tjanaka, Stefanos Nikolaidis
description: Abstract . Diversity optimization seeks to discover a set of solutions that elicit diverse features. Prior work has proposed Novelty Search (NS), which, given a current set of solutions, seeks to expand the set by finding points in areas of low density in the feature space.

title: Convergence guarantees for adaptive model predictive control with kinky inference
creator: Riccardo Zuliani, Raffaele Soloperto, John Lygeros
description:
A 2023 arXiv research paper by Riccardo Zuliani, Raffaele Soloperto, John Lygeros. We analyze the convergence properties of a robust adaptive model predictive control algorithm used to control an unknown nonlinear system. We show that by employing a standard quadratic stabilizing cost function, and by recursively updating the nominal model through kinky inference , the resulting controller ensures convergence of the true system to the origin, despite the presence of model uncertainty. We illustrate our theoretical findings through a numerical simulation. keywords

Adaptive model predictive control, adaptive control, kinky inference.

title: Memoryless Chemotaxis with Discrete Cues
creator: Jacob Knight, Paula García-Galindo, Johannes Pausch, Gunnar Pruessner
description: Abstract A wide array of biological systems can navigate in shallow gradients of chemoattractant with remarkable precision. Whilst previous approaches model such systems using coarse-grained chemical density profiles, we construct a dynamical model consisting of a chemotactic cell responding to discrete cue particles.

title: “ Knowing When You Don’t Know ”: A Multilingual Relevance Assessment Dataset for Robust Retrieval-Augmented Generation
creator: Nandan Thakur, Luiz Bonifacio, Xinyu Zhang, Odunayo Ogundepo, Ehsan Kamalloo, David Alfonso-Hermelo, Xiaoguang Li, Qun Liu, Boxing Chen, Mehdi Rezagholizadeh, Jimmy Lin, [1ex] David R. Cheriton School of Computer Science, University of Waterloo, Canada
description: Abstract Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) grounds Large Language Model (LLM) output by leveraging external knowledge sources to reduce factual hallucinations. However, prior work lacks a comprehensive evaluation of different language families, making it challenging to evaluate LLM robustness against errors in external retrieved knowledge.

title: Safety verification of Neural-Network-based controllers: a set invariance approach
creator: Louis Jouret, Adnane Saoud, Sorin Olaru
description: Abstract This paper presents a novel approach to ensure the safety of continuous-time linear dynamical systems controlled by a neural network (NN) based state-feedback. Our method capitalizes on the use of continuous piece-wise affine (PWA) activation functions (e.g. ReLU) which render the NN a PWA continuous function.

title: Fluxes of Courant bracket twisted at the same time by B B and θ \theta Thanks: Work supported in part by the Serbian Ministry of Science, Technological Development and Innovation
creator: Lj. Davidović, I. Ivanišević, B. Sazdović
description: Abstract This paper investigates the simultaneous twisting of the Courant bracket by a 2-form B B and a bi-vector θ \theta , exploring the generalized fluxes obtained in Courant algebroid relations. We define the twisted Lie bracket and demonstrate that the generalized H H -flux can be expressed as the field strength defined on this Lie algebroid.

title: Target detection using underwater acoustic communication links
creator: Lu Shen 1 , Yuriy Zakharov 1 , Benjamin Henson 1 , Nils Morozs 1 , Benoît Parrein 2 , Paul D. Mitchell 1
description: Abstract Underwater monitoring and surveillance systems are essential for underwater target detection, localization and classification. The aim of this work is to investigate the possibility of target detection by using data transmission between communication nodes in an underwater acoustic (UWA) network, i.e, re-using acoustic communication signals for target detection.

title: Precision Mass Measurement of Proton-Dripline Halo Candidate 22 Al
creator: S. E. Campbell, G. Bollen, B. A. Brown, A. Dockery, K. Fossez, C. M. Ireland, K. Minamisono, D. Puentes, A. Ortiz-Cortes, B. J. Rickey, R. Ringle, S. Schwarz, C. S. Sumithrarachchi, A. C. C. Villari, I. T. Yandow
description: Abstract We report the first mass measurement of the proton-halo candidate 22 Al performed with the LEBIT facility’s 9.4 T Penning trap mass spectrometer at FRIB. This measurement completes the mass information for the lightest remaining proton-dripline nucleus achievable with Penning traps.

title: Mastering Stacking of Diverse Shapes with Large-Scale Iterative Reinforcement Learning on Real Robots
creator: Thomas Lampe, Abbas Abdolmaleki, Sarah Bechtle, Sandy H. Huang, Jost Tobias SpringenbergMichael Bloesch, Oliver Groth, Roland Hafner, Tim Hertweck, Michael Neunert, Markus Wulfmeier, Jingwei Zhang, Francesco Nori, Nicolas Heess, Martin Riedmiller
description: Abstract Reinforcement learning solely from an agent’s self-generated data is often believed to be infeasible for learning on real robots, due to the amount of data needed. However, if done right, agents learning from real data can be surprisingly efficient through re-using previously collected sub-optimal data.

title: Performance of two-level sampling for the glueball spectrum in pure gauge theory
creator: Juan Andrés Urrea-Niño
description: Abstract The computation of the glueball spectrum is particularly challenging due to the rapid decay of the signal-to-noise ratio of the correlation functions. To address this issue, advanced techniques such as gauge link smearing and the variational method are commonly employed to identify the spectrum before the signal diminishes significantly.

title: Multiple Beads-on-a-string: Dark Matter-Deficient Galaxy Formation in a Mini-bullet Satellite-satellite Galaxy Collision yt ( Turk et al. 2011 ) , dice ( Perret 2016 ) , enzo ( Bryan et al. 2014 ; Brummel-Smith et al. 2019 ) , the grackle chemistry and cooling library ( Smith et al. 2017 ) , Rebound
creator: Joohyun Lee, Eun-jin Shin, Ji-hoon Kim, Paul R. Shapiro, Eunwoo Chung
description: Abstract Dark matter-deficient galaxies (DMDGs) discovered in the survey of ultra-diffuse galaxies (UDGs), in apparent conflict with standard CDM, may be produced by high-velocity galaxy-galaxy collisions, the Mini-bullet scenario. Recent observations of an aligned trail of 7 − 11 7-11 UDGs near NGC1052, including DMDGs DF2 and DF4, suggesting a common formation event, ∼ 8.9 ± 1.5 \sim 8.9\pm 1.

title: BioSpark : An End-to-End Generative System for Biological-Analogical Inspirations and Ideation
creator: Hyeonsu B. Kang, David Chuan-En Lin, Nikolas Martelaro, Aniket Kittur, Yan-Ying Chen, Matthew K. Hong, [1ex] Human-Computer Interaction Institute, Carnegie Mellon University, Pittsburgh, PA 15213, [.5ex] Toyota Research Institute, Los Altos, CA 94022, [1ex] {hyeonsuk,chuanenl,nikmart,nkittur}@cs.cmu
description: Abstract Nature is often used to inspire solutions for complex engineering problems, but achieving its full potential is challenging due to difficulties in discovering relevant analogies and synthesizing from them. Here, we present an end-to-end system, BioSpark , that generates biological-analogical mechanisms and provides an interactive interface to comprehend and synthesize from them.

title: News Signals: An NLP Library for Text and Time Series
creator: Chris Hokamp*, Demian Gholipour Ghalandari*, Parsa Ghaffari
description: Abstract We present an open-source Python library for building and using datasets where inputs are clusters of textual data, and outputs are sequences of real values representing one or more time series signals. The news-signals library supports diverse data science and NLP problem settings related to the prediction of time series behaviour using textual data feeds.

title: Online Vertical Federated Learning for Cooperative Spectrum Sensing
creator: Heqiang Wang 1 , Jie Xu 1
description: Abstract The increasing demand for wireless communication underscores the need to optimize radio frequency spectrum utilization. An effective strategy for leveraging underutilized licensed frequency bands is cooperative spectrum sensing (CSS), which enable multiple secondary users (SUs) to collaboratively detect the spectrum usage of primary users (PUs) prior to accessing the licensed spectrum.

title: Relativistic Jet Motion in the Radio-quiet LINER Galaxy KISSR872 Facilities: VLBA, SDSS
creator: Preeti Kharb, Eric G. Blackman, Eric Clausen-Brown, Mousumi Das, Daniel A. Schwartz, Aneta Siemiginowska, Smitha Subramanian, Sravani Vaddi
description: Abstract We report superluminal jet motion with an apparent speed of β app = 1.65 ± 0.57 \beta_{\mathrm{app}}=1.65\pm 0.57 in the radio-quiet (RQ) low ionisation nuclear emission line region (LINER) galaxy, KISSR872. This result comes from two epoch phase-referenced very long baseline interferometry (VLBI) observations at 5 GHz.

title: Lyapunov Exponents of Linear Switched Systems
creator: Andrei A. Agrachev, Michele Motta
description: Abstract We explicitly compute the maximal Lyapunov exponent for a switched system on SL 2 ​ ( ℝ ) \mathrm{SL}_{2}(\mathbb{R}) . This computation is reduced to the characterization of optimal trajectories for an optimal control problem on the Lie group. Keywords. Control Theory, Optimal Control, Switched system, Dynamical Systems, Lyapunov Exponents 1 Introduction Let \dot{y}=A(t)y,\quad y\in\mathbb{R}^{n}, (1.

title: Renormalization: general theory
creator: Vieri Mastropietro
description: Abstract . We review the theory of renormalization, including perturbative renormalization, regularized functional integrals, Renormalization Group and rigorous renormalization. 1. Introduction The notion of Renormalization was introduced originally by Bethe, Schwinger, Feynman, Tomonaga, Dyson and others in the 1950’s (see e.g.

title: The Animal-AI Environment: A Virtual Laboratory For Comparative Cognition and Artificial Intelligence Research Thanks: Corresponding Author: Konstantinos Voudouris (kv301@srcf.net)
creator: Konstantinos Voudouris, Ben Slater, Lucy G. Cheke, Wout Schellaert, José Hernández-Orallo, Marta Halina, Matishalin Patel, Ibrahim Alhas, Matteo G. Mecattaf, John Burden, Joel Holmes, Niharika Chaubey, Niall Donnelly, Matthew Crosby
description: Abstract The Animal-AI Environment is a unique game-based research platform designed to facilitate collaboration between the artificial intelligence and comparative cognition research communities. In this paper, we present the latest version of the Animal-AI Environment, outlining several major features that make the game more engaging for humans and more complex for AI systems.

title: Universal behavior of the BCS energy gap
creator: Joscha Henheik and Asbjørn Bækgaard Lauritsen IST Austria, Am Campus 1, 3400 Klosterneuburg, Austria
description: Abstract We consider the BCS energy gap Ξ ⁡ ( T ) \Xi(T) (essentially given by Ξ ⁡ ( T ) ≈ Δ ⁡ ( T , μ ) \Xi(T)\approx\Delta(T,\sqrt{\mu}) , the BCS order parameter) at all temperatures 0 ≤ T ≤ T c 0\leq T\leq T_{c} up to the critical one, T c T_{c} , and show that, in

title: DiffTune-MPC: Closed-Loop Learning for Model Predictive Control
creator: Ran Tao, Sheng Cheng, Xiaofeng Wang, Shenlong Wang, Naira Hovakimyan
description: Abstract Model predictive control (MPC) has been applied to many platforms in robotics and autonomous systems for its capability to predict a system’s future behavior while incorporating constraints that a system may have. To enhance the performance of a system with an MPC controller, one can manually tune the MPC’s cost function.

title: Frequency analysis and filter design for directed graphs with polar decomposition
creator: Semin Kwak, Laura Shimabukuro, Antonio Ortega
description: Abstract In this study, we challenge the traditional approach of frequency analysis on directed graphs, which typically relies on a single measure of signal variation such as total variation. We argue that the inherent directionality in directed graphs necessitates a multifaceted analytical approach that incorporates multiple signal variations definitions.

title: Irreducible representation of Plesken Lie algebras
creator: S. N. Arjun, P. G. Romeo
description: Abstract In [ 4 ] , Cohen and Taylor introduced Plesken Lie algebra as certain Lie algebra constructed using finite groups. Arjun and Romeo described the linear representation of these Lie algebras induced from group representation in [ 1 ] .

title: Warping the Residuals for Image Editing with StyleGAN
creator: Ahmet Burak Yildirim, Hamza Pehlivan, Aysegul Dundar
description: Abstract StyleGAN models show editing capabilities via their semantically interpretable latent organizations which require successful GAN inversion methods to edit real images. Many works have been proposed for inverting images into StyleGAN’s latent space. However, their results either suffer from low fidelity to the input image or poor editing qualities, especially for edits that require large transformations.

title: Rheological Analysis and Evaluation of Measurement Techniques for the Curing Polymethylmethacrylate Bone Cement in Vertebroplasty
creator: Zubin Trivedi, Jacek K. Wychowaniec, Dominic Gehweiler, Christoph M. Sprecher, Andreas Boger, Boyko Gueorguiev, Matteo D’Este, Tim Ricken, Oliver Röhrle
description: Abstract Vertebroplasty is a minimally invasive surgical procedure used to treat vertebral fractures, which conventionally involves injecting polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA) bone cement into the fractured vertebra. A common risk associated with vertebroplasty is cement leaking out of the vertebra during the injection, which may occur due to a lack of understanding of the bone cement’s complex flow behavior.

title: On the origin of the spectral features observed in the cosmic ray spectrum
creator: S. Recchia ,, S. Gabici
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by S. Recchia ,, S. Gabici. Recent measurements revealed the presence of several features in the cosmic ray spectrum. In particular, the proton and helium spectra exhibit a spectral hardening at ≈ 300 ​ GV \approx 300\,\mathrm{GV} and a spectral steeping at ≈ 15 ​ TV \approx 15\,\mathrm{TV} , followed by the well known knee -like feature at ≈ 3 ​ TV \approx 3\mathrm{TV} .

Sloan Foundation under grant G-2021-16778, while the author was in residence at the Simons

description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Jeanne N. Clelland. Let T ∗ = { P 1 ∗ , … , P N ∗ } T^{*}=\{P^{*}_{1},\ldots,P^{*}_{N}\} be a polygonal tiling of a simply connected region R ∗ R^{*} in the plane, and let T = { P 1 , … , P N } T=\{P_{1},\ldots,P_{N}\} be a noisy version of T ∗ T^{*} obtained by making small perturbations to the coordinates of the vertices of the polygons in T ∗ T^{*} .

title: Unstable Instantons in 𝑨 A -model Localization
creator: Emil Hakan Leeb-Lundberg
description: Abstract We apply localization techniques to A A -twisted 𝒩 = ( 2 , 2 ) \mathcal{N}=(2,2) theories of vector multiplets on S 2 S^{2} . We derive formulae for A A -model partition functions and correlators as integrals along a real contour, as opposed to a complex one.

title: Asymptotics of polynomials orthogonal with respect to a generalized Freud weight with application to special function solutions of Painlevé-IV Thanks: The author was supported by the European Research Council (ERC) Grant Agreement No. 101002013
creator: Ahmad Barhoumi
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Ahmad Barhoumi. We obtain asymptotics of polynomials satisfying the orthogonality relations ∫ ℝ z k ​ P n ​ ( z , t , N ) ​ e − N ⁡ ( 1 4 ​ z 4 + t 2 ​ z 2 ) ​ 𝑑 z = 0 for k = 0 , 1 , … , n − 1 , \int_{{\mathbb{R}}}z^{k}P_{n}(z;t,N){\mathrm{e}}^{-N\left(\frac{1}{4}z^{4}+\frac{t}{2}z^{2}\right)}{\mathrm{d}}z=0\quad\text{for}\quad k=0,1,...,n-1, where the complex parameter t t is in the so-called two-cut region.

title: DeRDaVa: Deletion-Robust Data Valuation for Machine Learning
creator: Xiao Tian, Rachael Hwee Ling Sim, Jue Fan, Bryan Kian Hsiang Low
description: Abstract Data valuation is concerned with determining a fair valuation of data from data sources to compensate them or to identify training examples that are the most or least useful for predictions. With the rising interest in personal data ownership and data protection regulations, model owners will likely have to fulfil more data deletion requests.

title: Foliated structure of weak nearly Sasakian manifolds
creator: Vladimir Rovenski
description: Abstract Weak contact metric manifolds, i.e., the linear complex structure on the contact distribution is replaced by a nonsingular skew-symmetric tensor, defined by the author and R. Wolak, allowed a new look at the theory of contact manifolds. In this paper we study the new structure of this type, called the weak nearly Sasakian structure.

title: Layerwise complexity-matched learning yields an improved model of cortical area V2
creator: Nikhil Parthasarathy np1742@nyu.edu, Olivier J. Hénaff henaff@google.com, Eero P. Simoncelli eero.simoncelli@nyu.edu
description: Abstract Human ability to recognize complex visual patterns arises through transformations performed by successive areas in the ventral visual cortex. Deep neural networks trained end-to-end for object recognition approach human capabilities, and offer the best descriptions to date of neural responses in the late stages of the hierarchy.

title: Fast multi-component cat generation under resonant or strong dressing Rydberg Kerr interaction
creator: Mohammadsadegh Khazali
description: Abstract Cat states are maximally entangled states with applications in metrology and fault-tolerant quantum computation. The experiments have revealed that Rydberg collective avalanche decoherence acts as the bottleneck for cat creation with Rydberg atoms. This process initiates after the black body radiation (BBR-)induced decay of Rydberg atoms and sets a strong limit on the cat creation time.

title: One size fits all: Insights on Extrinsic Thermal Absorption from Similarity of Supernova Remnant Radio Continuum Spectra
creator: Mario G. Abadi, Gabriela Castelletti, Leonardo Supan, Namir E. Kassim, Joseph W. Lazio
description: Abstract Typically, integrated radio frequency continuum spectra of supernova remnants (SNRs) exhibit a power-law form due to their synchrotron emission. In numerous cases, these spectra show an exponential turnover, long assumed due to thermal free-free absorption in the interstellar medium.

title: On locally finite ordered rooted trees and their rooted subtrees
creator: Geir Agnarsson, Elie Alhajjar, Aleyah Dawkins
description: Abstract . In this article we compare the known dynamical polynomial time algorithm for the game-over attack strategy, to that of the brute force approach; of checking all the ordered rooted subtrees of a given tree that represents a given computer network. Our approach is purely enumerative and combinatorial in nature.

title: Glioblastoma Tumor Segmentation using an Ensemble of Vision Transformers
creator: Huafeng Liu 1 , Benjamin Dowdell 1 , Todd Engelder 1 , Zarah Pulmano 1 , Nicolas Osa 1 , and Arko Barman 2
description: Abstract Glioblastoma is one of the most aggressive and deadliest types of brain cancer, with low survival rates compared to other types of cancer. Analysis of Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) scans is one of the most effective methods for the diagnosis and treatment of brain cancers such as glioblastoma.

title: Assessing Estimation Uncertainty under Model Misspecification
creator: Rong Li 1 , Yichen Qin 2 , Yang Li 1∗ 1: School of Statistics, Renmin University of China, Beijing, China. 2: Department of Operations, Business Analytics, and Information Systems, University of Cincinnati, Cincinnati, Ohio, USA
description: Abstract Abstract: Model misspecification is ubiquitous in data analysis because the data-generating process is often complex and mathematically intractable. Therefore, assessing estimation uncertainty and conducting statistical inference under a possibly misspecified working model is unavoidable. In such a case, classical methods such as bootstrap and asymptotic theory-based inference frequently fail since they rely heavily on the model assumptions.

title: Learning Temporal Properties is 𝖭𝖯 \mathsf{NP} -hard
creator: Benjamin Bordais, Daniel Neider, Rajarshi Roy
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Benjamin Bordais, Daniel Neider, Rajarshi Roy. 1 Introduction Temporal logics are probably the most popular specification languages employed to specify the temporal behavior of computing systems. Originally introduced in the context of program verification, temporal logics such as Linear Temporal Logic (LTL) [ 18 ] and Computation Tree Logic (CTL) [ 10 ] now find applications in a wide variety of topics, including reinforcement learning [ 13 , 25 , 15 , 5 ] , motion planning [ 14 , 11 ] , formal

title: Symmetry Enforced Fermi Surface Degeneracies Observed in Time-Reversal Symmetry-Breaking Superconductor LaNiGa 2
creator: Matthew Staab, Robert Prater, Sudheer Sreedhar, Journey Byland, Eliana Mann, Davis Zackaria, Yunshu Shi, Henry J. Bowman, Andrew L. Stephens, Myung-Chul Jung, Antia S. Botana, Warren E. Pickett, Valentin Taufour, Inna Vishik
description: Abstract LaNiGa 2 is superconductor that breaks time-reversal symmetry in the superconducting state without any known nearby magnetism. Recently, single crystals of LaNiGa 2 have been synthesized, revealing a nonsymmorphic Cmcm space group. Here, we report measurements of the electronic structure of LaNiGa 2 throughout the three-dimensional Brillouin zone (BZ) using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES).

title: Fractional Topological Charges in 2D Magnets
creator: Nina del Ser, Imane El Achchi, Achim Rosch
description: Abstract Magnetic skyrmions and antiskyrmions are characterised by an integer topological charge 𝒬 = ∓ 1 \mathcal{Q}=\mp 1 , describing the winding of the magnetic orientation. Half-integer winding numbers, 𝒬 = ± 1 2 \mathcal{Q}=\pm\frac{1}{2} , can be obtained for magnetic vortices (merons). Here, we discuss the physics of magnets with fractional topological charge which is neither integer nor half-integer.

title: Cascade Speculative Drafting for Even Faster LLM Inference
creator: Ziyi Chen, Xiaocong Yang, Jiacheng Lin, Chenkai Sun, Kevin Chen-Chuan Chang, Jie Huang
description: Abstract Introduced to enhance the efficiency of large language model (LLM) inference, speculative decoding operates by having a smaller model generate a draft. A larger target model then reviews this draft to align with its output, and any acceptance by the target model results in a reduction of the number of the target model runs, ultimately improving efficiency.

title: Explore 3D Dance Generation via Reward Model from Automatically-Ranked Demonstrations
creator: Zilin Wang, Haolin Zhuang, Lu Li, Yinmin Zhang, Junjie Zhong, Jun Chen, Yu Yang, Boshi Tang, Zhiyong Wu
description: Abstract This paper presents an Exploratory 3D Dance generation framework, E3D2, designed to address the exploration capability deficiency in existing music-conditioned 3D dance generation models. Current models often generate monotonous and simplistic dance sequences that misalign with human preferences because they lack exploration capabilities.

title: Precise Fourier parameters of Cepheid Radial Velocity Curves Thanks: Full Tables • ‣ 0.A , 6 , 7 , 8 , 9 and 10 are only available at the CDS via anonymous ftp to cdsarc.u-strasbg.fr (130.79.128.5) or via http://cdsarc.u-strasbg.fr/viz-bin/cat/J/A+A/
creator: V. Hocdé, P. Moskalik, N. A. Gorynya, R. Smolec, R. Singh Rathour, O. Ziółkowska
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by V. Hocdé, P. Moskalik, N. A. Gorynya, R. Smolec, R. Singh Rathour, O. Ziółkowska. Radial velocity (RV) curves of Classical Cepheids are indispensable in studying resonances between their pulsation modes. They allow precise determination of the resonant periods, which in turn helps to constrain fundamental parameters of these stars. The RV curves of Cepheids are also needed to identify their pulsation modes, which is essential for accurate calibration of the Cepheid period-luminosity (PL) relation.

title: Bias-Reduced Neural Networks for Parameter Estimation in Quantitative MRI Publication type: PRE-PRINT – SUBMITTED TO MAGNETIC RESONANCE IN MEDICINE
creator: Andrew Mao, Sebastian Flassbeck, Jakob Assländer
description: Abstract 1 Purpose To develop neural network (NN)-based quantitative MRI parameter estimators with minimal bias and a variance close to the Cramér-Rao bound. 2 Theory and Methods We generalize the mean squared error loss to control the bias and variance of the NN’s estimates, which involves averaging over multiple noise realizations of the same measurements during training.

title: Adaptive Smooth Activation for Improved Disease Diagnosis and Organ Segmentation from Radiology Scans
creator: Koushik Biswas, Debesh Jha, Nikhil Kumar Tomar, Gorkem Durak, Alpay Medetalibeyoglu
description: Abstract In this study, we propose a new activation function, called Adaptive Smooth Activation Unit (ASAU), tailored for optimized gradient propagation, thereby enhancing the proficiency of convolutional networks in medical image analysis. We apply this new activation function to two important and commonly used general tasks in medical image analysis: automatic disease diagnosis and organ segmentation in CT and MRI.

title: Bifurcation tracking on moving meshes and with consideration of azimuthal symmetry breaking instabilities Journal: Journal of Computational Physics
creator: Christian Diddens, Duarte Rocha
description: Abstract We present a black-box method to numerically investigate the linear stability of arbitrary multi-physics problems. While the user just has to enter the system’s residual in weak formulation, i.e. by a finite element method, all required discretized matrices are automatically assembled based on just-in-time generated and compiled highly performant C code.

title: Coffea-Casa: Building composable analysis facilities for the HL-LHC
creator: \firstname Sam \lastname Albin, \firstname Garhan \lastname Attebury, \firstname Kenneth \lastname Bloom, \firstname Brian \lastname Bockelman, \firstname Carl \lastname Lundstedt, \firstname Oksana \lastname Shadura \fnsep, \firstname John \lastname Thiltges
description: Abstract The large data volumes expected from the High Luminosity LHC (HL-LHC) present challenges to existing paradigms and facilities for end-user data analysis. Modern cyberinfrastructure tools provide a diverse set of services that can be composed into a system that provides physicists with powerful tools that give them straightforward access to large computing resources, with low barriers to entry.

title: Preference and Concurrence Aware Bayesian Graph Neural Networks for Recommender Systems
creator: Hongjian Gu, Yaochen Hu, Yingxue Zhang
description: Abstract Graph-based collaborative filtering methods have prevailing performance for recommender systems since they can capture high-order information between users and items, in which the graphs are constructed from the observed user-item interactions that might miss links or contain spurious positive interactions in industrial scenarios. The Bayesian Graph Neural Network framework approaches this issue with generative models for the interaction graphs.

title: Appearance-Based Refinement for Object-Centric Motion Segmentation
creator: Junyu Xie, Weidi Xie, Andrew Zisserman
description: Abstract The goal of this paper is to discover, segment, and track independently moving objects in complex visual scenes. Previous approaches have explored the use of optical flow for motion segmentation, leading to imperfect predictions due to partial motion, background distraction, and object articulations and interactions.

title: Enhanced contribution of the pairing gap to the QCD equation of state at large isospin chemical potential
creator: Yuki Fujimoto
description: Abstract I study QCD at large isospin density, which is known to be in the superfluid state with Cooper pairs carrying the same quantum number as pions. I solve the gap equation derived from the perturbation theory up to the next-to-leading order corrections.

title: Synthetic Shifts to Initial Seed Vector Exposes the Brittle Nature of Latent-Based Diffusion Models
creator: Mao Po-Yuan, Shashank KotyanTham Yik FoongDanilo Vasconcellos VargasLaboratory of Intelligent SystemsKyushu University, Fukuoka, Japan
description: Abstract Recent advances in Conditional Diffusion Models have led to substantial capabilities in various domains. However, understanding the impact of variations in the initial seed vector remains an underexplored area of concern. Particularly, latent-based diffusion models display inconsistencies in image generation under standard conditions when initialized with suboptimal initial seed vectors.

title: Symbolic Learning for Material Discovery
creator: Dan Cunnington, Flaviu Cipcigan, Rodrigo Neumann Barros Ferreira, Jonathan Booth
description: Abstract Discovering new materials is essential to solve challenges in climate change, sustainability and healthcare. A typical task in materials discovery is to search for a material in a database which maximises the value of a function. That function is often expensive to evaluate, and can rely upon a simulation or an experiment.

title: Cosmic Recombination in the Presence of Primordial Magnetic Fields
creator: Karsten Jedamzik, Tom Abel, Yacine Ali-Haïmoud
description: Abstract Primordial magnetic fields (PMFs) may explain observations of magnetic fields on extragalactic scales. They are most cleanly constrained by measurements of cosmic microwave background radiation (CMB) anisotropies. Their effects on cosmic recombination may even be at the heart of the resolution of the Hubble tension.

title: Heuristic for Optimisation of Dark Store Facility Locations for Quick Commerce Businesses
creator: Prithvi Dinesh Kewalramani, Harshad Khadilkar
description: Abstract We present a fast, flexible heuristic for setting up warehouse locations for quick commerce businesses, with the goal of serving the largest number of customers under the constraints of delivery radius and maximum daily deliveries per warehouse. Quick commerce or direct-to-customer delivery businesses guarantee delivery within a specified time.

title: Collective excitation of bosonic quantum Hall state
creator: Moumita Indra & Sandip Mondal
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Moumita Indra & Sandip Mondal. The recent developments in the theory of rapidly rotating Bose atoms have been reviewed in this article. Rotation leads to the development of quantized-vortices, that cluster into a vortex array, exactly to how superfluid helium behaves. Theoretically, a number of strongly correlated phases are projected to exist in this domain, which might be thought of as bosonic counterparts of fractional quantum Hall effect (FQHE).

title: Graded multiplicities in the Kostant-Rallis setting
creator: Andrew Frohmader
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Andrew Frohmader. This paper contains two main results. First, we provide combinatorial branching rules for GL n ↓ O n \GL_{n}\downarrow\Or_{n} and GL 2 ​ n ↓ Sp 2 ​ n \GL_{2n}\downarrow\Sp_{2n} extending the Littlewood restriction rules.

title: The Public Algorithms Survey in Allegheny County
description: Abstract 1 Overview Algorithms are increasingly used in public domains to assist in human decision-making {}^{\mbox{1}} Karen Levy, Kyla E Chasalow, and Sarah Riley. Algorithms and decision-making in the public sector. Annual Review of Law and Social Science, 17:309-334, 2021. .

title: Rethinking the Instruction Quality: L IFT is What You Need
creator: Yang Xu, Yongqiang Yao, Yufan Huang, Mengnan Qi, Maoquan Wang, Bin Gu, Neel Sundaresan
description: Abstract Instruction tuning, a specialized technique to enhance large language model (LLM) performance via instruction datasets, relies heavily on the quality of employed data. Existing quality improvement methods alter instruction data through dataset expansion or curation. However, the expansion method risks data redundancy, potentially compromising LLM performance, while the curation approach confines the LLM’s potential to the original dataset.

title: Recommending Influencers to Merchants using Matching Game Algorithm
creator: Gomes, J.M, Dias, L.A.V
description: Abstract Abstract The goal of this work was to apply the “ Gale-Shapley ” algorithm to a real-world problem. We analyzed the pairing of influencers with merchants, and after a detailed specification of the variables involved, we conducted experiments to observe the validity of the approach.

title: A Red Teaming Framework for Securing AI in Maritime Autonomous Systems
creator: Mathew J. Walter 1 , Aaron Barrett 1 and Kimberly Tam 1,2
description: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is being ubiquitously adopted to automate processes in science and industry. However, due to its often intricate and opaque nature, AI has been shown to possess inherent vulnerabilities which can be maliciously exploited with adversarial AI, potentially putting AI users and developers at both cyber and physical risk.

title: Protoclusters as Drivers of Stellar Mass Growth in the Early Universe, a Case Study: Taralay - a Massive Protocluster at z ∼ \sim 4.57 2023 Protoclusters as Drivers of Stellar Mass Growth in the Early Universe, a Case Study: Taralay - a Massive Protocluster at z ∼ \sim 4.57 – 14
creator: Priti Staab, Brian C. Lemaux, Ben Forrest, Ekta Shah, Olga Cucciati, Lori Lubin, Roy R. Gal, Denise Hung Lu Shen Finn Giddings, Yana Khusanova, Giovanni Zamorani, Sandro Bardelli, Letizia Pasqua Cassara, Paolo Cassata, Yi-Kuan Chiang, Yoshinobu Fudamoto, Shuma Fukushima, Bianca Garilli, Mauro Giaval
description: Abstract Simulations predict that the galaxy populations inhabiting protoclusters may contribute considerably to the total amount of stellar mass growth of galaxies in the early universe. In this study, we test these predictions observationally, focusing on the Taralay protocluster (formerly PCl J1001+0220) at z ∼ 4.57 z\sim 4.57 in the COSMOS field.

title: Labrador: Exploring the limits of masked language modeling for laboratory data
creator: David R. Bellamy, Bhawesh Kumar, Cindy Wang, Andrew Beam
description: Abstract In this work we introduce Labrador \xspace , a pre-trained Transformer model for laboratory data. Labrador \xspace and BERT were pre-trained on a corpus of 100 million lab test results from electronic health records (EHRs) and evaluated on various downstream outcome prediction tasks.

title: Essay: Where Can Quantum Geometry Lead Us?
creator: Päivi Törmä
description: Abstract Quantum geometry defines the phase and amplitude distances between quantum states. The phase distance is characterized by the Berry curvature and thus relates to topological phenomena. The significance of the full quantum geometry, including the amplitude distance characterized by the quantum metric, has started to receive attention in the last few years.

title: Toward a Reinforcement-Learning-Based System for Adjusting Medication to Minimize Speech Disfluency
creator: Pavlos Constas, Vikram Rawal, Matthew Honorio Oliveira, Andreas Constas, Aditya Khan, Kaison Cheung, Najma Sultani, Carrie Chen, Micol Altomare, Michael Akzam, Jiacheng Chen, Vhea He, Lauren Altomare, Heraa Muqri, Asad Khan, Nimit Amikumar Bhanshali, Youssef Rachad, Michael Guerzhoy
description: Abstract We propose a reinforcement learning (RL)-based system that would automatically prescribe a hypothetical patient medication that may help the patient with their mental health-related speech disfluency, and adjust the medication and the dosages in response to zero-cost frequent measurement of the fluency of the patient.

title: Assessing GPT4-V on Structured Reasoning Tasks
creator: Mukul Singh, Jose Cambronero, Sumit Gulwani, Vu Le, Gust Verbruggen
description: Abstract Multi-modality promises to unlock further uses for large language models. Recently, the state-of-the-art language model GPT-4 was enhanced with vision capabilities. We carry out a prompting evaluation of GPT-4V and five other baselines on structured reasoning tasks, such as mathematical reasoning, visual data analysis, and code generation.

title: Unlocking Musculoskeletal Disorder Risk Factors: NLP-Based Classification and Mode-Based Ranking Journal: Decision Analytics Journal
creator: Md Abrar Jahin, Subrata Talapatra
description: Abstract This research delves into the intricate landscape of Musculoskeletal Disorder (MSD) risk factors, employing a novel fusion of Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques and mode-based ranking methodologies. The primary objective is to advance the comprehension of MSD risk factors, their classification, and their relative severity, facilitating more targeted preventive and management interventions.

title: Nudging Nutrition: Lessons from the Danish “Fat Tax”
creator: Christian M. Dahl Nadja van ’t Hoff Giovanni Mellace Sinne Smed
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Christian M. Dahl Nadja van ’t Hoff Giovanni Mellace Sinne Smed. In October 2011, Denmark introduced the world’s first and, to date, only tax targeting saturated fat. However, this tax was subsequently abolished in January 2013. Leveraging exogenous variation from untaxed Northern-German consumers, we employ a difference-in-differences approach to estimate the causal effects of both the implementation and repeal of the tax on consumption and expenditure behavior across eight product categories targeted by the tax.

title: Assessing SATNet’s Ability to Solve the Symbol Grounding Problem
creator: Oscar Chang, Lampros Flokas, Hod Lipson, Michael Spranger
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Oscar Chang, Lampros Flokas, Hod Lipson, Michael Spranger. SATNet is an award-winning MAXSAT solver that can be used to infer logical rules and integrated as a differentiable layer in a deep neural network [ 1 ] . It had been shown to solve Sudoku puzzles visually from examples of puzzle digit images, and was heralded as an impressive achievement towards the longstanding AI goal of combining pattern recognition with logical reasoning.

title: LLM in a flash : Efficient Large Language Model Inference with Limited Memory Thanks: {kalizadehvahid, imirzadeh, d_belenko, skhatamifard, minsik, cdelmundo, mrastegari, farajtabar}@apple.com
creator: Keivan Alizadeh, Iman Mirzadeh, Dmitry Belenko, S. Karen Khatamifard
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Keivan Alizadeh, Iman Mirzadeh, Dmitry Belenko, S. Karen Khatamifard. Large language models (LLMs) are central to modern natural language processing, delivering exceptional performance in various tasks. However, their substantial computational and memory requirements present challenges, especially for devices with limited DRAM capacity. This paper tackles the challenge of efficiently running LLMs that exceed the available DRAM capacity by storing the model parameters in flash memory, but bringing them on demand to DRAM.

title: An Algebraic Approach to The Longest Path Problem
creator: Omar Al - Khazali, b00088673@aus.edu
description: Abstract The Longest Path Problem is a question of finding the maximum length between pairs of vertices of a graph. In the general case, the problem is 𝒩 ​ 𝒫 \mathcal{NP} -complete. However, there is a small collection of graph classes for which there exists an efficient solution. Current approaches involve either approximation or computational enumeration.

title: Multiobjective Simulated Annealing Algorithm for Minimum Weight Minimum Connected Dominating Set Problem
creator: 1 st Hayet Dahmri, 2 nd Salim Bouamama
description: Abstract Minimum connected dominating set problem is an NP-hard combinatorial optimization problem in graph theory. Finding connected dominating set is of high interest in various domains such as wireless sensor networks, optical networks and systems biology. Its weighted variant named minimum weight connected dominating set is also useful in such applications.

title: CLIPSyntel : CLIP and LLM Synergy for Multimodal Question Summarization in Healthcare
creator: Akash Ghosh, Arkadeep Acharya, Raghav Jain, Sriparna Saha, Aman Chadha, Setu Sinha
description: Abstract In the era of modern healthcare, swiftly generating medical question summaries is crucial for informed and timely patient care. Despite the increasing complexity and volume of medical data, existing studies have focused solely on text-based summarization, neglecting the integration of visual information.

title: FastSR-NeRF: Improving NeRF Efficiency on Consumer Devices with A Simple Super-Resolution Pipeline
creator: Chien-Yu Lin, Qichen Fu, Thomas Merth, Karren Yang, Anurag Ranjan
description: Abstract Super-resolution (SR) techniques have recently been proposed to upscale the outputs of neural radiance fields (NeRF) and generate high-quality images with enhanced inference speeds. However, existing NeRF+SR methods increase training overhead by using extra input features, loss functions, and/or expensive training procedures such as knowledge distillation.

title: Iterative Motion Editing with Natural Language 607 Conference: Special Interest Group on Computer Graphics and Interactive Techniques Conference Conference Papers ’24; July 27-August 1, 2024; Denver, CO, USA Special Interest Group on Computer Graphics and Interactive Techniques Conference Conference
creator: Purvi Goel, Kuan-Chieh Wang, C. Karen Liu, Kayvon Fatahalian
description: Abstract . Text-to-motion diffusion models can generate realistic animations from text prompts, but do not support fine-grained motion editing controls. In this paper, we present a method for using natural language to iteratively specify local edits to existing character animations, a task that is common in most computer animation workflows.

title: COPD-FlowNet: Elevating Non-invasive COPD Diagnosis with CFD Simulations (Student Abstract)
creator: Aryan Tyagi, Aryaman Rao, Shubhanshu Rao, Raj Kumar Singh
description: Abstract Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disorder (COPD) is a prevalent respiratory disease that significantly impacts the quality of life of affected individuals. This paper presents COPD-FlowNet, a novel deep-learning framework that leverages a custom Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) to generate synthetic Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) velocity flow field images specific to the trachea of COPD patients.

title: Towards AI-driven Integrative Emissions Monitoring & Management for Nature-Based Climate Solutions
creator: Olamide Oladeji, Seyed Shahabeddin Mousavi
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Olamide Oladeji, Seyed Shahabeddin Mousavi. AI has been proposed as an important tool to support several efforts related to nature-based climate solutions such as the detection of wildfires that affect forests and vegetation-based offsets. While this and other use-cases provide important demonstrative value of the power of AI in climate change mitigation, such efforts have typically been undertaken in silos, without awareness of the integrative nature of real-world climate policy-making.

title: Fast Decision Boundary based Out-of-Distribution Detector
creator: Litian Liu, Yao Qin
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Litian Liu, Yao Qin. Efficient and effective Out-of-Distribution (OOD) detection is essential for the safe deployment of AI systems. Existing feature space methods, while effective, often incur significant computational overhead due to their reliance on auxiliary models built from training features. In this paper, we propose a computationally-efficient OOD detector without using auxiliary models while still leveraging the rich information embedded in the feature space. Specifically, we detect OOD samples based on their feature distances to decision boundaries.

title: QuadAttac K K : A Quadratic Programming Approach to Learning Ordered Top- K K Adversarial Attacks
creator: Thomas Paniagua, Ryan Grainger, Tianfu Wu
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Thomas Paniagua, Ryan Grainger, Tianfu Wu. The adversarial vulnerability of Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) has been well-known and widely concerned, often under the context of learning top- 1 1 attacks (e.g., fooling a DNN to classify a cat image as dog). This paper shows that the concern is much more serious by learning significantly more aggressive ordered top- K K clear-box 1 1 1 This is often referred to as white/black-box attacks in the literature.

title: The Decidability of the Riemann Hypothesis
creator: Kevin Broughan
description: Abstract Using first order predicate logic and results of the complex analysis of Takeuti which is based on a type theory and the work of Kreisel, and which gives a conservative extension of first order Peano arithmetic (PA), it is shown, assuming all critical zeros of the Riemann zeta function are simple, that the Riemann hypothesis is decidable in PA.

title: Deciphering Compatibility Relationships with Textual Descriptions via Extraction and Explanation
creator: Yu Wang, Zexue He, Zhankui He, Hao Xu, Julian McAuley
description: Abstract Understanding and accurately explaining compatibility relationships between fashion items is a challenging problem in the burgeoning domain of AI-driven outfit recommendations. Present models, while making strides in this area, still occasionally fall short, offering explanations that can be elementary and repetitive.

title: Set Theory is interpretable in Class Ordering Theory
creator: Zuhair Al-Johar
description:
A 2023 arXiv research paper by Zuhair Al-Johar. 1
Abstract

Here it is shown that standard set theory can be interpreted in a theory about order. The ordering here is about non-extensional flat classes, i.e. classes that are not elements of classes. So, stipulating a nearly well order over all those classes coupled together with indexing that order by elements of those classes, thereby having those elements serve as ordinals; this together with infinity and a replacement like axiom would be shown to interpret
\sf ZFC
.

title: SAI3D: Segment Any Instance in 3D Scenes
creator: Yingda Yin, Yuzheng Liu, Yang Xiao, Daniel Cohen-Or, Jingwei Huang, Baoquan Chen
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Yingda Yin, Yuzheng Liu, Yang Xiao, Daniel Cohen-Or, Jingwei Huang, Baoquan Chen. Advancements in 3D instance segmentation have traditionally been tethered to the availability of annotated datasets, limiting their application to a narrow spectrum of object categories. Recent efforts have sought to harness vision-language models like CLIP for open-set semantic reasoning, yet these methods struggle to distinguish between objects of the same categories and rely on specific prompts that are not universally applicable.

title: SeGA: Preference-Aware Self-Contrastive Learning with Prompts for Anomalous User Detection on Twitter
creator: Ying-Ying Chang, Wei-Yao Wang, Wen-Chih Peng
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Ying-Ying Chang, Wei-Yao Wang, Wen-Chih Peng. In the dynamic and rapidly evolving world of social media, detecting anomalous users has become a crucial task to address malicious activities such as misinformation and cyberbullying. As the increasing number of anomalous users improves the ability to mimic normal users and evade detection, existing methods only focusing on bot detection are ineffective in terms of capturing subtle distinctions between users.

title: Demographics of co-aging complex systems: from sickly worms to chess engines
creator: Cagatay Eskin, Dervis Can Vural
description: Abstract Aging, as defined in terms of the slope of the probability of death versus time (hazard curve), is a generic phenomenon observed in nearly all complex systems. Theoretical models of aging predict hazard curves that monotonically increase in time, in discrepancy with the peculiar ups and downs observed in empirically.

title: NORA-Surge: A storm surge hindcast for the Norwegian Sea, the North Sea and the Barents Sea
creator: Nils Melsom Kristensen, Paulina Tedesco, Jean Rabault, Ole Johan Aarnes, Øyvind Saetra, Øyvind Breivik
description: Abstract Knowledge about statistics for water level variations along the coast due to storm surge is important for the utilization of the coastal zone. An open and freely available storm surge hindcast archive covering the coast of Norway and adjacent sea areas spanning the time period 1979-2022 is presented.

title: Prime number theorems for polynomials from homogeneous dynamics
creator: Giorgos Kotsovolis, Katharine Woo
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Giorgos Kotsovolis, Katharine Woo. We establish a new class of examples of the multivariate Bateman-Horn conjecture by using tools from dynamics. These cases include the determinant polynomial on the space of n × n n\times n matrices, the Pfaffian on the space of skew-symmetric 2 ​ n × 2 ​ n 2n\times 2n matrices, and the determinant polynomial on the space of symmetric n × n n\times n matrices.

title: Zero distribution of finite order Bank–Laine functions Thanks: The author is supported by the Fundamental Research Funds for the Central Universities (FRF-TP-19-055A1) and a Project supported by the National Natural Science Foundation of China (12301091)
creator: Yueyang Zhang
description: Abstract . It is known that a Bank–Laine function E E is a product of two normalized solutions of the second order differential equation f ′′ + A ​ f = 0 f^{\prime\prime}+Af=0 ( † ) ({\dagger}) , where A = A ⁡ ( z ) A=A(z) is an entire function.

title: StarVector: Generating Scalable Vector Graphics Code from Images and Text
creator: Juan A. Rodriguez Abhay Puri Shubham Agarwal Issam H. Laradji Pau Rodriguez, Sai Rajeswar David Vazquez Christopher Pal Marco Pedersoli
description: Abstract Scalable Vector Graphics (SVGs) are vital for modern image rendering due to their scalability and versatility. Previous SVG generation methods have focused on curve-based vectorization, lacking semantic understanding, often producing artifacts, and struggling with SVG primitives beyond path curves. To address these issues, we introduce StarVector, a multimodal large language model for SVG generation.

title: Diffusion-Based Particle-DETR for BEV Perception
creator: Asen Nachkov, Martin Danelljan, Danda Pani Paudel, Luc Van Gool
description: Abstract The Bird-Eye-View (BEV) is one of the most widely-used scene representations for visual perception in Autonomous Vehicles (AVs) due to its well suited compatibility to downstream tasks. For the enhanced safety of AVs, modeling perception uncertainty in BEV is crucial.

title: Searching for the first radial excitation of the Δ ⁡ ( 1232 ) \Delta(1232) in lattice QCD
creator: Liam Hockley, Waseem Kamleh, Derek Leinweber, Anthony Thomas
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Liam Hockley, Waseem Kamleh, Derek Leinweber, Anthony Thomas. We present a lattice QCD analysis of the Δ \Delta -baryon spectrum, with the goal of finding the position of the 2 ​ s 2s radial excitation of the Δ ⁡ ( 1232 ) \Delta(1232) ground state.

title: An intermediate case of exponential multivalued forbidden matrix configurations
creator: Wallace Peaslee, Attila Sali, Jun Yan
description: Abstract The forbidden number forb ⁡ ( m , F ) \forb(m,F) , which denotes the maximum number of distinct columns in an m m -rowed ( 0 , 1 ) (0,1) -matrix with no submatrix that is a row and column permutation of F F , has been widely studied in extremal set theory.

title: Classifying toposes for non-geometric theories Thanks: The author is supported by the EPSRC grant EP/X018997/1.
creator: Mark Kamsma
description: Abstract . The classifying topos of a geometric theory is a topos such that geometric morphisms into it correspond to models of that theory. We study classifying toposes for different infinitary logics: first-order, sub-first-order (i.e. geometric logic plus implication) and classical.

title: Shortcut-to-Adiabatic Controlled-Phase Gate in Rydberg atoms
creator: Luis S. Yagüe Bosch, Tim Ehret, Francesco Petiziol, Ennio Arimondo, Sandro Wimberger
description: Abstract A shortcut-to-adiabatic protocol for the realization of a fast and high-fidelity controlled-phase gate in Rydberg atoms is developed. The adiabatic state transfer, driven in the high-blockade limit, is sped up by compensating nonadiabatic transitions via oscillating fields that mimic a counterdiabatic Hamiltonian. High fidelities are obtained in wide parameter regions.

title: Efficient and Scalable Graph Generation through Iterative Local Expansion
creator: Andreas Bergmeister, Karolis Martinkus, Nathanaël Perraudin, Roger Wattenhofer
description: Abstract In the realm of generative models for graphs, extensive research has been conducted. However, most existing methods struggle with large graphs due to the complexity of representing the entire joint distribution across all node pairs and capturing both global and local graph structures simultaneously.

title: Reinforcement Learning Based Quantum Circuit Optimization via ZX-Calculus
creator: Jordi Riu, Jan Nogué, Gerard Vilaplana, Artur Garcia-Saez, Marta P. Estarellas
description: Abstract We propose a novel Reinforcement Learning (RL) method for optimizing quantum circuits using graph-theoretic simplification rules of ZX-diagrams. The agent, trained using the Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithm, employs Graph Neural Networks to approximate the policy and value functions.

title: An operational definition of quantum information scrambling
creator: Gabriele Lo Monaco, Luca Innocenti, Dario Cilluffo, Diana A. Chisholm, Salvatore Lorenzo, G. Massimo Palma
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Gabriele Lo Monaco, Luca Innocenti, Dario Cilluffo, Diana A. Chisholm, Salvatore Lorenzo, G. Massimo Palma. Quantum information scrambling (QIS) is a characteristic feature of several quantum systems, ranging from black holes to quantum communication networks. While accurately quantifying QIS is crucial to understanding many such phenomena, common approaches based on the tripartite information have limitations due to the accessibility issues of quantum mutual information, and do not always properly take into consideration the dependence on the encoding input basis.

title: ( g − 2 ) e , μ (g-2)_{e,\mu} anomalies and decays h → e a ​ e b h\to e_{a}e_{b} , Z → e a ​ e b Z\to e_{a}e_{b} , and e b → e a ​ γ e_{b}\to e_{a}\gamma in a two Higgs doublet model with inverse seesaw neutrinos
creator: T.T. Hong, Q.Duyet Tran, T.Phong Nguyen, L.T. Hue, N.H.T. Nha
description: Abstract The lepton flavor violating decays h → e b ± ​ e a ∓ h\to e_{b}^{\pm}e_{a}^{\mp} , Z → e b ± ​ e a ∓ Z\to e_{b}^{\pm}e_{a}^{\mp} , and e b → e a ​ γ e_{b}\to e_{a}\gamma will be discussed in the framework of the Two Higgs doublet model with presence of new inverse seesaw neutrinos and

title: Error-corrected Hadamard gate simulated at the circuit level
creator: György P. Gehér, Campbell McLauchlan, Earl T. Campbell, Alexandra E. Moylett, Ophelia Crawford
description: Abstract We simulate the logical Hadamard gate in the surface code under a circuit-level noise model, compiling it to a physical circuit on square-grid connectivity hardware. Our paper is the first to do this for a logical unitary gate on a quantum error-correction code. We consider two proposals, both via patch-deformation: one that applies a transversal Hadamard gate (i.e.

title: Anomaly detection with flow-based fast calorimeter simulators
creator: Claudius Krause, Benjamin Nachman, Ian Pang, David Shih, Yunhao Zhu
description: Abstract Recently, several normalizing flow-based deep generative models have been proposed to accelerate the simulation of calorimeter showers. Using CaloFlow as an example, we show that these models can simultaneously perform unsupervised anomaly detection with no additional training cost. As a demonstration, we consider electromagnetic showers initiated by one (background) or multiple (signal) photons.

title: JWST’s PEARLS: 119 multiply imaged galaxies behind MACS0416, lensing properties of caustic crossing galaxies, and the relation between halo mass and number of globular clusters at z = 0.4 z=0.4
creator: Jose M. Diego , ,, Nathan J. Adams, S. P. Willner, Tom Harvey, Tom Broadhurst, Seth H. Cohen, Rolf A. Jansen, Jake Summers, Rogier A. Windhorst, Jordan C. J. D’Silva, Anton M. Koekemoer, Dan Coe, Christopher J. Conselice, Simon P. Driver, Brenda Frye, Norman A. Grogin, Madeline A. Marshall, Mario No
description: Abstract We present a new lens model for the z = 0.396 z=0.396 galaxy cluster MACS J0416.1 − - 2403 based on a previously known set of 77 spectroscopically confirmed, multiply imaged galaxies plus an additional set of 42 candidate multiply imaged galaxies from past HST and new JWST data.

title: Exploring Low-Mass Black Holes through Tidal Disruption Events in the Early Universe: Perspectives in the Era of JWST, RST, and LSST Surveys
creator: Kohei Inayoshi, Kazumi Kashiyama, Wenxiu Li, Yuichi Harikane, Kohei Ichikawa, Masafusa Onoue
description: Abstract The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) has recently uncovered the presence of low-luminosity active galactic nuclei (AGNs) at z = 4 − 11 z=4-11 . Spectroscopic observations have provided estimates of the nuclear black hole (BH) masses for these sources, extending the low-mass boundary down to M ∙ ∼ 10 6 − 7 ​ M ⊙ M_{\bullet}\sim 10^{6-7}~M_{\odot} .

title: Residual ANODE
creator: Ranit Das, Gregor Kasieczka, David Shih
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Ranit Das, Gregor Kasieczka, David Shih. We present R-Anode , a new method for data-driven, model-agnostic resonant anomaly detection that raises the bar for both performance and interpretability. The key to R-Anode is to enhance the inductive bias of the anomaly detection task by fitting a normalizing flow directly to the small and unknown signal component, while holding fixed a background model (also a normalizing flow) learned from sidebands.

title: Gravitational Waves from the Pulsar Magnetosphere Gravitational Waves from the Pulsar Magnetosphere – 2023
creator: Ioannis Contopoulos, Demosthenes Kazanas, Demetrios B. Papadopoulos
description: Abstract We investigate the generation of gravitational waves from the rotation of an orthogonal pulsar magnetosphere in flat space time. We calculate the first order metric perturbation due to the rotation of the non-axisymmetric distribution of electromagnetic energy density around the central star.

title: A Study of Systematics on the Cosmological Inference of the Hubble Constant from Gravitational Wave Standard Sirens Preprint: Short-author PP
creator: Grégoire Pierra, Simone Mastrogiovanni, Stéphane Perriès, Michela Mapelli
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Grégoire Pierra, Simone Mastrogiovanni, Stéphane Perriès, Michela Mapelli. Gravitational waves (GWs) from compact binary coalescences (CBCs) can constrain the cosmic expansion of the universe. In the absence of an associated electromagnetic counterpart, the spectral sirens method exploits the relation between the detector frame and the source frame masses to jointly infer the parameters of the mass distribution of black holes (BH) and the cosmic expansion parameter H 0 H_{0} .

title: Pseudospectrum of de Sitter black holes
creator: Kyriakos Destounis 1,2 , Valentin Boyanov 3 , Rodrigo Panosso Macedo 4
description: Abstract Pseudospectral analyses have broadened our understanding of ringdown waveforms from binary remnants, by providing insight into both the stability of their characteristic frequencies under environmental perturbations, as well as the underlying transient and non-modal phenomenology that a mode analysis may miss. In this work we present the pseudospectrum of scalar perturbations on spherically-symmetric black holes in de Sitter spacetimes.

title: Universal structure of measurement-induced information in many-body ground states
creator: Zihan Cheng, Rui Wen, Sarang Gopalakrishnan, Romain Vasseur, Andrew C. Potter
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Zihan Cheng, Rui Wen, Sarang Gopalakrishnan, Romain Vasseur, Andrew C. Potter. Unlike unitary dynamics, measurements of a subsystem can induce long-range entanglement via quantum teleportation. The amount of measurement-induced entanglement or mutual information depends jointly on the measurement basis and the entanglement structure of the state (before measurement), and has operational significance for whether the state is a resource for measurement-based quantum computing, as well as for the computational complexity of simulating the state using quantum or classical computers.

title: Experimentally tunable QED in dipolar-octupolar quantum spin ice
creator: Alaric Sanders, Han Yan (闫寒), Claudio Castelnovo, Andriy H. Nevidomskyy
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Alaric Sanders, Han Yan (闫寒), Claudio Castelnovo, Andriy H. Nevidomskyy. We propose a readily achievable experimental setting where an external magnetic field is used to tune the emergent quantum electrodynamics (eQED) of dipolar-octupolar quantum spin ice (DO-QSI).

title: Classification and transformations of quantum circuit decompositions for permutation operations
creator: Ankit Khandelwal †, Handy Kurniawan †, Shraddha Aangiras, Özlem Salehi, Adam Glos
description: Abstract Efficient decomposition of permutation unitaries is vital as they frequently appear in quantum computing. In this paper, we identify the key properties that impact the decomposition process of permutation unitaries. Then, we classify these decompositions based on the identified properties, establishing a comprehensive framework for analysis.

title: Bridging Logic and Learning: A Neural-Symbolic Approach for Enhanced Reasoning in Neural Models (ASPER)
creator: Fadi Al Machot
description: Abstract Neural-symbolic learning, an intersection of neural networks and symbolic reasoning, aims to blend neural networks’ learning capabilities with symbolic AI’s interpretability and reasoning. This paper introduces an approach designed to improve the performance of neural models in learning reasoning tasks.

title: Pauli Spectrum and Non-stabilizerness of Typical Quantum Many-Body States
creator: Xhek Turkeshi, Anatoly Dymarsky, Piotr Sierant
description: Abstract An important question of quantum information is to characterize genuinely quantum (beyond-Clifford) resources necessary for universal quantum computing. Here, we use the Pauli spectrum to quantify how “magic”, beyond Clifford, typical many-qubit states are. We first present a phenomenological picture of the Pauli spectrum based on quantum typicality and then confirm it for Haar random states.

title: Spread complexity for measurement-induced non-unitary dynamics and Zeno effect
creator: Aranya Bhattacharya, Rathindra Nath Das, Bidyut Dey, and Johanna Erdmenger
description: Abstract Using spread complexity and spread entropy, we study non-unitary quantum dynamics. For non-hermitian Hamiltonians, we extend the bi-Lanczos construction for the Krylov basis to the Schrödinger picture. Moreover, we implement an algorithm adapted to complex symmetric Hamiltonians. This reduces the computational memory requirements by half compared to the bi-Lanczos construction.

title: Fluid Mixing during Phase Separation in Crystallizing White Dwarfs
creator: M. H. Montgomery, Bart H. Dunlap
description: Abstract Accurate models of cooling white dwarfs must treat the energy released as their cores crystallize. This phase transition slows the cooling by releasing latent heat and also gravitational energy, which results from phase separation: liquid C is released from the solid C/O core, driving an outward carbon flux.

title: The Challenge of Measuring Asteroid Masses with Gaia DR2 astrometry Journal: PSJ
creator: Zachary Murray
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Zachary Murray. The Gaia second data release contains high-accuracy astrometric measurements of thousands of solar system bodies. These measurements raise the possibility of determining asteroid masses by modeling scattering events between massive objects observed by Gaia. In this paper, we identify promising encounters between small asteroids that occur during the second data release and quantify the various errors involved in mass determination.

title: Transformation-Dependent Performance-Enhancement of Digital Annealer for 3-SAT
creator: Christian Münch, Fritz Schinkel, Sebastian Zielinski, Stefan Walter
description: Abstract Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) problems are NP-hard problems and many real-world problems can be formulated as QUBO. Currently there are no algorithms known that can solve arbitrary instances of NP-hard problems efficiently. Therefore special-purpose hardware such as Digital Annealer, other Ising machines, as well as quantum annealers might lead to benefits in solving such problems.

title: Hunting for Hydrated Minerals on Trans-Neptunian Objects Journal: PSJ Astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2013 ) , Astroscrappy ( van Dokkum 2001 ; McCully et al. 2018 ) , Gemini IRAF ( Tody 1986 ; Tody 1993 ; Green 2012 ) , Matplotlib ( Hunter 2007 ) , NumPy ( Harris et al. 2020 ) , SciPy ( Virt
creator: Tom Seccull, Wesley C. Fraser, Dominik A. Kiersz, Thomas H. Puzia
description: Abstract We present new optical reflectance spectra of three potentially silicate-rich trans-Neptunian objects (TNOs).
