creator: Sahana Ramnath, Brihi Joshi, Skyler Hallinan, Ximing Lu, Liunian Harold Li, Aaron Chan, Jack Hessel, Yejin Choi, Xiang Ren
description: Abstract Large language models (LMs) are capable of generating free-text rationales to aid question answering. However, prior work 1) suggests that useful self-rationalization is emergent only at significant scales (e.g., 175B parameter GPT-3); and 2) focuses largely on downstream performance, ignoring the semantics of the rationales themselves, e.g., are they faithful, true, and helpful for humans?

title: Institutional Screening and the Sustainability of Conditional Cooperation
creator: Ethan Holdahl, Jiabin Wu
description: Abstract This paper studies a preference evolution model in which a population of agents are matched to play a sequential prisoner’s dilemma in an incomplete information environment. An institution can design an incentive-compatible screening scheme, such as a special zone that requires an entry fee, or a costly label for purchase, to segregate the conditional cooperators from the non-cooperators.

title: An invariant feature extraction for multi-modal images matching.
creator: Chenzhong Gao, Wei Li
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Chenzhong Gao, Wei Li. This paper aims at providing an effective multi-modal images invariant feature extraction and matching algorithm for the application of multi-source data analysis. Focusing on the differences and correlation of multi-modal images, a feature-based matching algorithm is implemented. The key technologies include phase congruency (PC) and Shi-Tomasi feature point for keypoints detection, LogGabor filter and a weighted partial main orientation map (WPMOM) for feature extraction, and a multi-scale process to deal with scale differences and optimize matching results.

title: Trace and Index of Dirac-Schrödinger Operators on Open Space with Operator Potentials
creator: Oliver Fürst
description: Abstract We develop a principal trace and generalized index formula for a Dirac-Schrödinger operator D D on open space of odd dimension d ≥ 3 d\geq 3 with a potential given by a family of self-adjoint unbounded operators acting on a infinite dimensional Hilbert space H H .

title: Three-dimensional checkerboard spin structure on a breathing pyrochlore lattice
creator: Margarita G. Dronova, Václav Petříček, Zachary Morgan, Feng Ye, Daniel M. Silevitch, Yejun Feng
description: Abstract The standard approach to realize a spin liquid state is through magnetically frustrated states, relying on ingredients such as the lattice geometry, dimensionality, and magnetic interaction type of the spins. While Heisenberg spins on a pyrochlore lattice with only antiferromagnetic nearest-neighbors interactions are theoretically proven disordered, spins in real systems generally include longer-range interactions.

title: Electroweak baryogenesis, dark matter, and dark CP-symmetry
creator: Jinghong Ma, Jie Wang, Lei Wang ∗
description: Abstract With the motivation of explaining the dark matter and achieving the electroweak baryogenesis via the spontaneous CP-violation at high temperature, we propose a complex singlet scalar ( S = χ + i ​ η s 2 S=\frac{\chi+i\eta_{s}}{\sqrt{2}} ) extension of the two-Higgs-doublet model respecting a discrete dark CP-symmetry: S → − S ∗ S\to-S^{*} .

title: Co-training and Co-distillation for Quality Improvement and Compression of Language Models
creator: Hayeon Lee Rui Hou Jongpil Kim, Davis Liang Hongbo Zhang Sung Ju Hwang Alexander Min, Meta AI Abridge AI KAIST hayeonlee@meta.com rayhou@meta.com jongpil@meta.comdavis@abridge.com hbzhang@meta.com sjhwang82@kaist.ac.kr alexmin@meta.com
description: Abstract Knowledge Distillation (KD) compresses computationally expensive pre-trained language models (PLMs) by transferring their knowledge to smaller models, allowing their use in resource-constrained or real-time settings. However, most smaller models fail to surpass the performance of the original larger model, resulting in sacrificing performance to improve inference speed.

title: The nature and nurture of network evolution
creator: Bin Zhou, Petter Holme, Zaiwu Gong, Choujun Zhan, Yao Huang, Xin Lu, Xiangyi Meng
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Bin Zhou, Petter Holme, Zaiwu Gong, Choujun Zhan, Yao Huang, Xin Lu, Xiangyi Meng. Although the origin of the fat-tail characteristic of the degree distribution in complex networks has been extensively researched, the underlying cause of the degree distribution characteristic across the complete range of degrees remains obscure. Here, we propose an evolution model that incorporates only two factors: the node’s weight, reflecting its innate attractiveness (nature), and the node’s degree, reflecting the external influences (nurture).

title: Consistent4D: Consistent 360° Dynamic Object Generation from Monocular Video
creator: Yanqin Jiang, Li Zhang, Jin Gao, Weimin Hu, Yao Yao
description: Abstract In this paper, we present Consistent4D, a novel approach for generating 4D dynamic objects from uncalibrated monocular videos. Uniquely, we cast the 360-degree dynamic object reconstruction as a 4D generation problem, eliminating the need for tedious multi-view data collection and camera calibration.

title: Nonparametric Estimation of Conditional Copula using Smoothed Checkerboard Bernstein Sieves
creator: Lu Lu, Sujit K. Ghosh
description: Abstract Conditional copulas are useful tools for modeling the dependence between multiple response variables that may vary with a given set of predictor variables. Conditional dependence measures such as conditional Kendall’s tau and Spearman’s rho that can be expressed as functionals of the conditional copula are often used to evaluate the strength of dependence conditioning on the covariates.

title: Constraints on the Neutron-Star Structure from the Clocked X-Ray Burster 1RXS J180408.9 − - 342058
creator: A. Dohi (土肥明), W. B. Iwakiri (岩切渉), N. Nishimura (西村信哉), T. Noda (野田常雄), S. Nagataki (長瀧重博), M. Hashimoto (橋本正章)
description: Abstract Type-I X-ray bursts are rapid-brightening transient phenomena on the surfaces of accreting neutron stars (NSs). Some X-ray bursts, called clocked bursters , exhibit regular behavior with similar light curve profiles in their burst sequences. The periodic nature of clocked bursters has the advantage of constraining X-ray binary parameters and physics inside the NS.

title: Signed graphs and inverses of their incidence matrices
creator: Abdullah Alazemi, Milica Anđelić, Sudipta Mallik
description: Abstract . The Laplacian matrix L L of a signed graph G G may or may not be invertible. We present a combinatorial formula of the Moore-Penrose inverse of L L . This is achieved by finding a combinatorial formula for the Moore-Penrose inverse of an incidence matrix of G G .

title: Cavity Induced Topology in Graphene
creator: Ceren B. Dag, Vasil Rokaj
description: Abstract Strongly coupling materials to cavity fields can affect their electronic properties altering the phases of matter. We study the monolayer graphene whose electrons are coupled to both left and right circularly polarized photons, and time-reversal symmetry is broken due to a phase shift between the two polarizations. We develop a many-body perturbative theory, and derive cavity mediated electronic interactions.

title: On subbagging Boosted Probit Model Trees
creator: Tian Qin, Wei-Min Huang
description: Abstract With the insight of variance-bias decomposition, we design a new hybrid bagging-boosting algorithm named SBPMT for classification problems. For the boosting part of SBPMT, we propose a new tree model called Probit Model Tree (PMT) as base classifiers in AdaBoost procedure.

title: Last fall degree of semi-local polynomial systems
creator: Ming-Deh A. Huang (USC, mdhuang@usc.edu)
description: Abstract . We study the last fall degrees of semi-local polynomial systems, and the computational complexity of solving such systems for closed-point and rational-point solutions, where the systems are defined over a finite field. A semi-local polynomial system specifies an algebraic set which is the image of a global linear transformation of a direct product of local affine algebraic sets.

title: Hilbert coefficients of quadratic algebras
creator: Ralf Fröberg
description: Abstract If R = k ⁡ [ x 1 , … , x n ] / I R=k[x_{1},\ldots,x_{n}]/I is a graded artinian algebra, then the length of k ⁡ [ x 1 , … , x n ] / I s k[x_{1},\ldots,x_{n}]/I^{s} becomes a polynomial in s s of degree n n for large s s .

title: A distributed multi-GPU ab initio density matrix renormalization group algorithm with applications to the P-cluster of nitrogenase
creator: Chunyang Xiang, Weile Jia, Wei-Hai Fang, Zhendong Li
description: Abstract The presence of many degenerate d / f d/f orbitals makes polynuclear transition metal compounds such as iron-sulfur clusters in nitrogenase challenging for state-of-the-art quantum chemistry methods. To address this challenge, we present the first distributed multi-GPU (Graphics Processing Unit) ab initio density matrix renormalization (DMRG) algorithm, suitable for modern high-performance computing (HPC) infrastructures.

title: Non-uniform Mixing of Quantum Walks on the Symmetric Group
creator: Avah Banerjee banerjeeav@mst.edu Missouri S&T
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Avah Banerjee banerjeeav@mst.edu Missouri S&T. It is well-known that classical random walks on regular graphs converge to the uniform distribution. Quantum walks, in their various forms, are quantizations of their corresponding classical random walk processes. Gerhardt and Watrous (2003) demonstrated that continuous-time quantum walks do not converge to the uniform distribution on certain Cayley graphs of the Symmetric group, which by definition are all regular.

title: Nef vector bundles on a quadric surface with first Chern class ( 2 , 2 ) (2,2) Thanks: This work was partially supported by JSPS KAKENHI (C) Grant Number 21K03158.
creator: Masahiro Ohno
description: Abstract . We classify nef vector bundles on a smooth quadric surface with first Chern class ( 2 , 2 ) (2,2) over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification Primary 14J60; Secondary 14F08, 14J45, 14F06 1. Introduction In [ SW90 , Sect. 3] and [ PSW92 , Sect.

title: Channel Attention for Quantum Convolutional Neural Networks
creator: Gekko Budiutama, Shunsuke Daimon, Hirofumi Nishi, Ryui Kaneko, Tomi Ohtsuki, Yu-ichiro Matsushita
description: Abstract Quantum convolutional neural networks (QCNNs) have gathered attention as one of the most promising algorithms for quantum machine learning. Reduction in the cost of training as well as improvement in performance is required for practical implementation of these models.

title: Application of some L 2 L_{2} optimization to a discrete distribution
creator: Jiwoong Kim
description: Abstract This paper proposes the novel method to estimate the success probability of the binomial distribution. To that end, we use the Cramer-von Mises type optimization which has been commonly used in estimating parameters of continuous distributions. Upon obtaining the estimator through the proposed method, its desirable properties such as asymptotic distribution and robustness are rigorously investigated.

title: Optimal Construction of N-bit-delay Almost Instantaneous Fixed-to-Variable-Length Codes
creator: Ryosuke Sugiura, Masaaki Nishino, Norihito Yasuda, Yutaka Kamamoto, and Takehiro Moriya
description: Abstract This paper presents an optimal construction of N N -bit-delay almost instantaneous fixed-to-variable-length (AIFV) codes, the general form of binary codes we can make when finite bits of decoding delay are allowed. The presented method enables us to optimize lossless codes among a broader class of codes compared to the conventional FV and AIFV codes.

title: FocusTune: Tuning Visual Localization through Focus-Guided Sampling
creator: Son Tung Nguyen, Alejandro Fontan, Michael Milford, Tobias Fischer
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Son Tung Nguyen, Alejandro Fontan, Michael Milford, Tobias Fischer. We propose FocusTune, a focus-guided sampling technique to improve the performance of visual localization algorithms. FocusTune directs a scene coordinate regression model towards regions critical for 3D point triangulation by exploiting key geometric constraints. Specifically, rather than uniformly sampling points across the image for training the scene coordinate regression model, we instead re-project 3D scene coordinates onto the 2D image plane and sample within a local neighborhood of the re-projected points.

title: Solvable limit of ETH matrix model for double-scaled SYK
creator: Kazumi Okuyama, and Takao Suyama
description: Abstract We study the two-matrix model for double-scaled SYK model, called ETH matrix model introduced by Jafferis et al [arXiv:2209.02131]. If we set the parameters q A , q B q_{A},q_{B} of this model to zero, the potential of this two-matrix model is given by the Gaussian terms and the q q -commutator squared interaction.

title: OVIR-3D: Open-Vocabulary 3D Instance Retrieval Without Training on 3D Data
creator: Shiyang Lu Haonan Chang Eric Pu Jing Abdeslam Boularias Kostas Bekris
description: Abstract This work presents OVIR-3D, a straightforward yet effective method for open-vocabulary 3D object instance retrieval without using any 3D data for training. Given a language query, the proposed method is able to return a ranked set of 3D object instance segments based on the feature similarity of the instance and the text query.

title: Dynamic Neural Fields for Learning Atlases of 4D Fetal MRI Time-series
creator: Zeen Chi, Zhongxiao Cong, Clinton J. Wang, Yingcheng Liu, Esra Abaci Turk, P. Ellen Grant, S. Mazdak Abulnaga, Polina Golland, Neel Dey
description: Abstract We present a method for fast biomedical image atlas construction using neural fields. Atlases are key to biomedical image analysis tasks, yet conventional and deep network estimation methods remain time-intensive. In this preliminary work, we frame subject-specific atlas building as learning a neural field of deformable spatiotemporal observations.

title: Bottomonia in quark-antiquark confining potential
creator: Ritu Garg, K.K Vishwakarma, Alka Upadhyay
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Ritu Garg, K.K Vishwakarma, Alka Upadhyay. In this paper, we comprehensively explore bottomonia mass spectra and their decay properties by solving the non-relativistic Schrodinger wave equation numerically with approximate quark-antiquark potential form. We also incorporate spin-dependent terms - spin-spin, spin-orbit, and tensor terms to remove mass degeneracy and to obtain excited states ( n ​ S , n ​ P , n ​ D , n ​ F , n = 1 , 2 , 3 , 4 , 5 nS,nP,nD,nF,n=1,2,3,4,5 ) mass spectra.

title: Stacked Autoencoder Based Feature Extraction and Superpixel Generation for Multifrequency PolSAR Image Classification
creator: Tushar Gadhiya, Sumanth Tangirala, and Anil K. Roy
description: Abstract In this paper we are proposing classification algorithm for multifrequency Polarimetric Synthetic Aperture Radar (PolSAR) image. Using PolSAR decomposition algorithms 33 features are extracted from each frequency band of the given image. Then, a two-layer autoencoder is used to reduce the dimensionality of input feature vector while retaining useful features of the input.

title: Inner-IoU: More Effective Intersection over Union Loss with Auxiliary Bounding Box
creator: Hao Zhang, Cong Xu, Shuaijie Zhang
description: Abstract With the rapid development of detectors, Bounding Box Regression (BBR) loss function has constantly updated and optimized. However, the existing IoU-based BBR still focus on accelerating convergence by adding new loss terms, ignoring the limitations of IoU loss term itself.

title: Human as Points: Explicit Point-based 3D Human Reconstruction from Single-view RGB Images
creator: Yingzhi Tang, Qijian Zhang, Yebin Liu, Junhui Hou
description: Abstract The latest trends in the research field of single-view human reconstruction are devoted to learning deep implicit functions constrained by explicit body shape priors. Despite the remarkable performance improvements compared with traditional processing pipelines, existing learning approaches still exhibit limitations in terms of flexibility , generalizability , robustness , and/or representation capability .

title: A generalized theory of expansions and collapses with applications to 𝒵 \mathcal{Z} -compactification Thanks: This research was supported in part by Simons Foundation Grant 427244, CRG
creator: Craig R. Guilbault, Daniel Gulbrandsen
description: Abstract . We generalize the dual notions of “expansion” and “collapse” so they can be applied to arbitrary metric spaces. We also expand the theory to allow for infinitely many such moves. Those tools are then employed to prove a variety of compactification theorems.

title: Actions on the quiver – Discrete quotients on the Coulomb branch
creator: Amihay Hanany, Guhesh Kumaran, Chunhao Li, Deshuo Liu, Marcus Sperling
description: Abstract This paper introduces two operations in quiver gauge theories. The first operation takes a quiver with a permutation symmetry 𝔖 n \mathfrak{S}_{n} and gives a quiver with adjoint loops. The corresponding 3d 𝒩 = 4 {\cal N}=4 Coulomb branches are related by an orbifold of 𝔖 n \mathfrak{S}_{n} .

title: Runs of extremes of observables on dynamical systems and applications. Thanks: MN thanks the NSF for support from NSF-DMS 2009923.
creator: Meagan Carney, Mark Holland, Matthew Nicol, Phuong Tran
description: Abstract . We use extreme value theory to estimate the probability of successive exceedances of a threshold value of a time-series of an observable on several classes of chaotic dynamical systems. The observables have either a Fréchet (fat-tailed) or Weibull (bounded) distribution.

title: Inflation and Reheating through an Independent Affine Connection
creator: Alberto Salvio
description: Abstract This paper is based on a talk in which I discussed how a component of the dynamical affine connection, that is independent of the metric, can drive inflation in agreement with observations. This provides a geometrical origin for the inflaton.

title: Microphysical Parameter Variation in GRB Stratified Afterglows and Closure Relations: from sub-GeV to TeV Observations 2015 Microphysical Parameter Variation in GRB Stratified Afterglows and Closure Relations: from sub-GeV to TeV Observations – 11
creator: Nissim Fraija, Maria G. Dainotti, Boris Betancourt Kamenetskaia, Antonio Galván-Gámez, Edilberto Aguilar-Ruiz
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Nissim Fraija, Maria G. Dainotti, Boris Betancourt Kamenetskaia, Antonio Galván-Gámez, Edilberto Aguilar-Ruiz. Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) are one of the most exciting sources that offer valuable opportunities for investigating the evolution of energy fraction given to magnetic fields and particles through microphysical parameters during relativistic shocks. The delayed onset of GeV-TeV radiation from bursts detected by the Fermi Large Area Telescope ( Fermi -LAT) and Cherenkov Telescopes provide crucial information in favor of the external-shock model.

title: A Novel Catalyst Scheme for Stochastic Minimax Optimization
creator: Guanghui Lan, Yan Li
description: Abstract This paper presents a proximal-point-based catalyst scheme for simple first-order methods applied to convex minimization and convex-concave minimax problems. In particular, for smooth and (strongly)-convex minimization problems, the proposed catalyst scheme, instantiated with a simple variant of stochastic gradient method, attains the optimal rate of convergence in terms of both deterministic and stochastic errors.

title: Sample Complexity Bounds for Estimating Probability Divergences under Invariances
creator: Behrooz Tahmasebi, Stefanie Jegelka
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Behrooz Tahmasebi, Stefanie Jegelka. Group-invariant probability distributions appear in many data-generative models in machine learning, such as graphs, point clouds, and images. In practice, one often needs to estimate divergences between such distributions. In this work, we study how the inherent invariances, with respect to any smooth action of a Lie group on a manifold, improve sample complexity when estimating the 1-Wasserstein distance, the Sobolev Integral Probability Metrics (Sobolev IPMs), the Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD), and also the complexity of the density estimation problem

title: Online Supplementary Appendices to
creator: “Estimation and Inference for
description: Abstract In this paper, we consider estimation and inference for the unknown parameters and function involved in a class of generalized hierarchical models. Such models are of great interest in the literature of neural networks (such as Bauer and Kohler 2019 ).

title: Improvement of response bandwidth and sensitivity of Rydberg Receiver using multi-channel excitations
creator: Jinlian Hu, Yuechun Jiao, Yunhui He, Hao Zhang, Linjie Zhang, Jianming Zhao, Suotang Jia
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Jinlian Hu, Yuechun Jiao, Yunhui He, Hao Zhang, Linjie Zhang, Jianming Zhao, Suotang Jia. We investigate the response bandwidth of a superheterodyne Rydberg receiver at a room-temperature vapor cell, and present an architecture of multi-channel lasers excitation to increase the response bandwidth and keep sensitivity, simultaneously.

title: Hemisphere-averaged Hellings-Downs curve between pulsar pairs for a gravitational wave source
creator: Tatsuya Sasaki, Kohei Yamauchi, Shun Yamamoto, Hideki Asada
description: Abstract The Hellings-Downs (HD) curve plays a crucial role in search for nano-hertz gravitational waves (GWs) with pulsar timing arrays. We discuss the angular pattern of correlations for pulsar pairs within a celestial hemisphere. The hemisphere-averaged correlation curve depends upon the sky location of a GW compact source like a binary of supermassive black holes.

title: An Iwahori theoretic mod p p Local Langlands Correspondence
creator: Anand Chitrao
description: Abstract We extend a comparison theorem of Anandavardhanan-Borisagar between the quotient of the induction of a mod p p character by the image of an Iwahori-Hecke operator and compact induction of a weight to the case of the trivial character. This involves studying the corresponding non-commutative Iwahori-Hecke algebra.

title: Stability in the homology of configuration spaces of high dimensional manifolds
creator: by
description: Abstract Consider the configuration spaces of manifold (closed or open). An influential theorem of McDuff and Segal shows that the (co)homology of unordered configuration spaces of open manifold is independent of number of configuration points in a range of degree called the stable range. Church prove that the homological stability is also present in the closed background manifold.

title: Multi-band analysis of strong gravitationally lensed post-blue nugget candidates from the Kilo-Degree Survey
creator: Rui Li, Nicola R. Napolitano, Linghua, Xie, Ran Li, Xiaotong Guo, Alexey Sergeyev, Crescenzo Tortora, Chiara Spiniello, Alessandro Sonnenfeld, Léon V. E. Koopmans, Diana Scognamiglio
description: Abstract During the early stages of galaxy evolution, a significant fraction of galaxies undergo a transitional phase between the “blue nugget” systems, which arise from the compaction of large, active star-forming disks, and the “red nuggets”, which are red and passive compact galaxies.

title: Manageable to unmanageable transition in a fractal model of project networks
creator: Alexei Vazquez
description: Abstract Project networks are characterized by power law degree distributions, a property that is known to promote spreading. In contrast, the longest path length of project networks scales algebraically with the network size, which improves the impact of random interventions. Using the duplication-split model of project networks, I provide convincing evidence that project networks are fractal networks.

title: Optimization of RIS Placement for Satellite-to-Ground Coverage Enhancement
creator: Xingchen Liu, Liuxun Xue, Shu Sun, and Meixia Tao
description: Abstract In satellite-to-ground communication, ensuring reliable and efficient connectivity poses significant challenges. The reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) offers a promising solution due to its ability to manipulate wireless propagation environments and thus enhance communication performance. In this paper, we propose a method for optimizing the placement of RISs on building facets to improve satellite-to-ground communication coverage.

title: Truly Scale-Equivariant Deep Nets with Fourier Layers
creator: Md Ashiqur Rahman, Raymond A. Yeh
description: Abstract In computer vision, models must be able to adapt to changes in image resolution to effectively carry out tasks such as image segmentation; This is known as scale-equivariance. Recent works have made progress in developing scale-equivariant convolutional neural networks, e.g., through weight-sharing and kernel resizing. However, these networks are not truly scale-equivariant in practice.

title: SoK: Evaluations in Industrial Intrusion Detection Research
creator: Olav Lamberts RWTH Aachen Universitylamberts@comsys.rwth-aachen.de, Konrad Wolsing Fraunhofer FKIERWTH Aachen Universitywolsing@comsys.rwth-aachen.de Eric Wagner Fraunhofer FKIERWTH Aachen Universityeric.wagner@fkie.fraunhofer.de Jan Pennekamp RWTH Aachen Universitypennekamp@comsys.rwth-aachen.de Ja
description: Abstract Industrial systems are increasingly threatened by cyberattacks with potentially disastrous consequences. To counter such attacks, industrial intrusion detection systems strive to timely uncover even the most sophisticated breaches. Due to its criticality for society, this fast-growing field attracts researchers from diverse backgrounds, resulting in 130 130 new detection approaches in 2021 alone.

title: Adapting Pre-trained Generative Models for Extractive Question Answering
creator: Prabir Mallick, Tapas Nayak, Indrajit Bhattacharya
description: Abstract Pre-trained Generative models such as BART, T5, etc. have gained prominence as a preferred method for text generation in various natural language processing tasks, including abstractive long-form question answering (QA) and summarization. However, the potential of generative models in extractive QA tasks, where discriminative models are commonly employed, remains largely unexplored.

title: Rotational phase dependent J-H colour of the dwarf planet Eris Thanks: Visiting Astronomer at the Infrared Telescope Facility, which is operated by the University of Hawaii under contract 80HQTR19D0030 with the National Aeronautics and Space Administration.” astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 20
creator: Róbert Szakáts, Csaba Kiss
description: Abstract The largest bodies – or dwarf planets – constitute a different class among Kuiper belt objects and are characterised by bright surfaces and volatile compositions remarkably different from that of smaller trans-Neptunian objects. These compositional differences are also reflected in the visible and near-infrared colours, and variegations across the surface can cause broadband colours to vary with rotational phase.

title: Nef vector bundles on a quadric threefold with first Chern class two Thanks: This work was partially supported by JSPS KAKENHI (C) Grant Number 21K03158.
creator: Masahiro Ohno
description: Abstract . We classify nef vector bundles on a smooth hyperquadric of dimension three with first Chern class two over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. In particular, we see that they are globally generated. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification Primary 14J60; Secondary 14J45, 14F08, 1.

title: Stochastic Pairwise Preference Convergence in Bayesian Agents
creator: Jordan Kemp 1, Max-Olivier Hongler 2, Olivier Gallay 3
description: Abstract Beliefs inform the behavior of forward-thinking agents in complex environments. Recently, sequential Bayesian inference has emerged as a mechanism to study belief formation among agents adapting to dynamical conditions. However, we lack critical theory to explain how preferences evolve in cases of simple agent interactions.

title: Constraining (anti)nuclei measurements relevant for astrophysics with ALICE
creator: \firstname Chiara \lastname Pinto \fnsep \firstname \lastname for the ALICE Collaboration
description: Abstract Antinuclei can be produced in space either by collisions of high-energy cosmic rays with the interstellar medium or from the annihilation of dark matter particles stemming into standard model particles. High-energy hadronic collisions at accelerators create a suitable environment for producing light (anti)nuclei.

title: Gravitational analogue of radiation reaction in STVG Journal: Physics of the Dark Universe
creator: Bobur Turimov, Abdurakhmon Nosirov, Ahmadjon Abdujabbarov
description: Abstract We have studied influence of STVG in circular motion of massive particle around the Schwarzschild-MOG black hole and discussed the Innermost Stable Circular Orbit (ISCO) and Marginally Bound Orbit (MBO) position of massive test particle. This research explores dynamics of massive particles within the framework of Scalar-Tensor-Vector Gravity (STVG) when navigating the vicinity of Schwarzschild-MOG black holes.

title: Surface Enhanced Infrared Absorption mechanism and modification of the plasmonic response
creator: Tanguy Colleu, Adam Fekete, Xavier Gonze, Alexandre Cloots, Vincent Liégeois, Gian-Marco Rignanese, Luc Henrard
description: Abstract Surface Enhanced Infrared Absorption (SEIRA) is an experimental method where trace amount of a compound can be detected with high sensibility. This high detection sensibility is the result of the interaction of the molecules with a localized plasmon, usually from a metallic nano-particle.

title: Modeling blazar broadband emission with convolutional neural networks - I. Synchrotron self-Compton model
creator: D. Bégué, N. Sahakyan, H. Dereli Bégué, P. Giommi, S. Gasparyan, M. Khachatryan, A. Casotto, A. Pe’er
description: Abstract Modeling the multiwavelength spectral energy distributions (SEDs) of blazars provides key insights into the underlying physical processes responsible for the emission. While SED modeling with self-consistent models is computationally demanding, it is essential for a comprehensive understanding of these astrophysical objects.

title: Multiple blowing-up solutions for asymptotically critical Lane-Emden systems on Riemannian manifolds
creator: Wenjing Chen, Zexi Wang
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Wenjing Chen, Zexi Wang. Let ( ℳ , g ) (\mathcal{M},g) be a smooth compact Riemannian manifold of dimension N ≥ 8 N\geq 8 . We are concerned with the following elliptic system { − Δ g ​ u + h ⁡ ( x ) ​ u = v p − α ​ ε , in ​ ℳ , − Δ g ​ v + h ⁡ ( x ) ​ v = u q − β ​ ε , in ​ ℳ ,

title: Magnetic moments of decuplet baryons in asymmetric strange hadronic matter at finite temperature
creator: Arvind Kumar, Suneel Dutt, Harleen Dahiya
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Arvind Kumar, Suneel Dutt, Harleen Dahiya. In the present work we study the masses and magnetic moments of decuplet baryons in isospin asymmetric strange hadronic medium at finite temperature using chiral SU(3) quark mean field model. In the strange isospin asymmetric medium, the properties of baryons in chiral SU(3) mean field model are modified through the exchange of scalar fields σ \sigma , ζ \zeta and δ \delta and the vector fields ω \omega , ρ \rho and ϕ \phi .

title: Self-Driven Configurational Dynamics in Frustrated Spring-Mass Systems
creator: Ori Saporta-Katz, Avraham Moriel
description: Abstract Various physical systems relax mechanical frustration through configurational rearrangements. We examine such rearrangements via Hamiltonian dynamics of simple internally-stressed harmonic 4-mass systems. We demonstrate theoretically and numerically how mechanical frustration controls the underlying potential energy landscape. Then, we examine the harmonic 4-mass systems’ Hamiltonian dynamics and relate the onset of chaotic motion to self-driven rearrangements.

title: Nonlinear stationary differential equations with fractional order 1 < α < 2 1<\alpha<2 on metric star graphs
creator: K.K.Sabirov
description: Abstract In this paper we consider nonlinear stationary fractional-in-space differential equations with order 1 < α < 2 1<\alpha<2 on the metric star graph with three finite bonds. At the branched point of the star graph we put the weight continuity and the generalized Kirchhoff rule.

title: Bayesian Time-Lapse Full Waveform Inversion using Hamiltonian Monte Carlo
creator: P. D. S. de Lima, M. S. Ferreira, G. Corso, J. M. de Araújo
description: Abstract Time-lapse images carry out important information about dynamic changes in Earth’s interior which can be inferred using different Full Waveform Inversion (FWI) schemes. The estimation process is performed by manipulating more than one seismic dataset, associated with the baseline and monitors surveys.

title: TabRepo: A Large Scale Repository of Tabular Model Evaluations and its AutoML Applications
creator: David Salinas, Nick Erickson
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by David Salinas, Nick Erickson. We introduce TabRepo, a new dataset of tabular model evaluations and predictions. TabRepo contains the predictions and metrics of 1310 models evaluated on 200 classification and regression datasets. We illustrate the benefit of our dataset in multiple ways. First, we show that it allows to perform analysis such as comparing Hyperparameter Optimization against current AutoML systems while also considering ensembling at marginal cost by using precomputed model predictions.

title: Light-scattering reconstruction of transparent shapes using neural networks
creator: Tymoteusz Miara, Draga Pihler-Puzović, Matthias Heil, Anne Juel
description: Abstract We propose a cheap non-intrusive high-resolution method of visualising transparent or translucent objects which may translate, rotate and change their shape. We propose a method of reconstructing a strongly deformed time-evolving surface from a time-series of noisy clouds of points using a lightweight neural network.

title: Exploring the Capability of Text-to-Image Diffusion Models with Structural Edge Guidance for Multi-Spectral Satellite Image Inpainting
creator: Mikolaj Czerkawski, Christos Tachtatzis
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Mikolaj Czerkawski, Christos Tachtatzis. The paper investigates the utility of text-to-image inpainting models for satellite image data. Two technical challenges of injecting structural guiding signals into the generative process as well as translating the inpainted RGB pixels to a wider set of MSI bands are addressed by introducing a novel inpainting framework based on StableDiffusion and ControlNet as well as a novel method for RGB-to-MSI translation.

title: Magnetic dipole moments of the Ω c ​ ( 3185 ) 0 \Omega_{c}(3185)^{0} and Ω c ​ ( 3327 ) 0 \Omega_{c}(3327)^{0} states from molecular perspective
creator: Ulaş Özdem
description: Abstract In this paper we study the magnetic dipole moments of the newly discovered Ω c ​ ( 3185 ) 0 \Omega_{c}(3185)^{0} and Ω c ​ ( 3327 ) 0 \Omega_{c}(3327)^{0} , assuming that Ω c ​ ( 3185 ) 0 \Omega_{c}(3185)^{0} and Ω c ​ ( 3327 ) 0 \Omega_{c}(3327)^{0} are S S -wave D ​ Ξ D\Xi and

title: Optimal symplectic positions for the mean width
creator: Jonghyeon Ahn, Ely Kerman
description: Abstract . In this work we study convex bodies in ℝ 2 ​ n {\mathbb{R}}^{2n} with the property that their mean width can not be decreased by the action of natural classes of symplectomorphisms. We also study the relationship between their mean widths and various symplectic invariants.

title: Phase mixing of propagating Alfvén waves in a single-fluid partially ionized solar plasma
creator: M. McMurdo, I. Ballai, G. Verth, A. Alharbi, V. Fedun
description: Abstract Phase mixing of Alfvén waves is one of the most promising mechanisms for heating of the solar atmosphere. The damping of waves in this case requires small transversal scales, relative to the magnetic field direction. Here this requirement is achieved by considering a transversal inhomogeneity in the equilibrium plasma density profile.

title: Full Grid Lattice Polygons with Maximal Sum of Squares of Edge-Lengths
creator: Oliver Mantas Ališauskas, Giedrius Alkauskas, Valdas Dičiūnas
description: Abstract . Consider a subset [ 1 , 2 , … , n ] × [ 1 , 2 , … , n ] [1,2,\ldots,n]\times[1,2,\ldots,n] of the plane integer lattice. Take any non self-intersecting n 2 n^{2} -gon built on it (straight angles are allowed). The square of a side length is a positive integer.

title: Parameter Estimation for Open Clusters using an Artificial Neural Network with a QuadTree-based Feature Extractor
creator: Lorenzo Cavallo, Lorenzo Spina, Giovanni Carraro, Laura Magrini, Eloisa Poggio, Tristan Cantat-Gaudin, Mario Pasquato, Sara Lucatello, Sergio Ortolani, Jose Schiappacasse-Ulloa
description: Abstract With the unprecedented increase of known star clusters, quick and modern tools are needed for their analysis. In this work, we develop an artificial neural network trained on synthetic clusters to estimate the age, metallicity, extinction, and distance of Gaia open clusters.

title: Detecting agreement in multi-party dialogue: evaluating speaker diarisation versus a procedural baseline to enhance user engagement.
creator: Angus Addlesee, Daniel Denley, Andy Edmondson, Nancie Gunson, Daniel Hernandez Garcia, Alexandre Kha, Oliver Lemon, James Ndubuisi, Neil O’Reilly, Lia Perochaud, Raphaël Valeri, Miebaka Worika
description: Abstract Conversational agents participating in multi-party interactions face significant challenges in dialogue state tracking, since the identity of the speaker adds significant contextual meaning. It is common to utilise diarisation models to identify the speaker. However, it is not clear if these are accurate enough to correctly identify specific conversational events such as agreement or disagreement during a real-time interaction.

title: Quantum distribution functions in systems with an arbitrary number of particles
creator: Yu.M. Poluektov, A.A. Soroka
description: Abstract Expressions for the entropy and equations for the quantum distribution functions in systems of non-interacting fermions and bosons with an arbitrary, including small, number of particles are obtained in the paper. Key words : distribution function, fermions, bosons, entropy, quantum dot, factorial, gamma function, Bose-Einstein condensation pacs 05.30.– d, 05.30.Ch, 05.30.Fk, 05.30.Jp, 64.60.an, 68.65.

title: Transient RFI environment of LOFAR-LBA at 72-75 MHz
creator: B. K. Gehlot ,, L. V. E. Koopmans, S. A. Brackenhoff, E. Ceccotti, S. Ghosh, C. Höfer, F. G. Mertens, M. Mevius, S. Munshi A. R. Offringa, V. N. Pandey, A. Rowlinson, A. Shulevski, R. A. M. J. Wijers, S. Yatawatta, S. Zaroubi
description: Abstract Context. Measurement of the highly redshifted and faint 21-cm signal of neutral hydrogen from the Cosmic Dawn and Epoch of Reionisation promises to unveil a wealth of information about the astrophysical processes that governed the structure formation and evolution of the universe during the first billion years of its evolution. Aims.

title: COLA: COarse-LAbel multi-source LiDAR semantic segmentation for autonomous driving
creator: Jules Sanchez, Jean-Emmanuel Deschaud, François Goulette
description: Abstract LiDAR semantic segmentation for autonomous driving has been a growing field of interest in recent years. Datasets and methods have appeared and expanded very quickly, but methods have not been updated to exploit this new data availability and rely on the same classical datasets.

title: Janus microswimmers are poor hydrodynamic mixers
creator: Maximilian R. Bailey, Dmitry A. Fedosov, Federico Paratore, Fabio Grillo, Gerhard Gompper, Lucio Isa
description: Abstract The generation of fluid flows by autophoretic microswimmers has been proposed as a mechanism to enhance mass transport and mixing at the micro- and nanoscale. Here, we experimentally investigate the ability of model 2-D “active baths” of photocatalytic silica-titania Janus microspheres to enhance the diffusivity of tracer particles at different microswimmer densities below the onset of collective behaviour.

title: Detecting Agreement in Multi-party Conversational AI
creator: Laura Schauer 1 , Jason Sweeney 1 , Charlie Lyttle 1 , Zein Said 1 , Áron Széles 1 , Cale Clark 1 , Katie McAskill 1 , Xander Wickham 1 , Tom Byars 1 , Daniel Hernandez Garcia 2 , Nancie Gunson 2 , Angus Addlesee 2 , Oliver Lemon 2
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Laura Schauer 1 , Jason Sweeney 1 , Charlie Lyttle 1 , Zein Said 1 , Áron Széles 1 , Cale Clark 1 , Katie McAskill 1 , Xander Wickham 1 , Tom Byars 1 , Daniel Hernandez Garcia 2 , Nancie Gunson 2 , Angus Addlesee 2 , Oliver Lemon 2. Today, conversational systems are expected to handle conversations in multi-party settings, especially within Socially Assistive Robots (SARs).

title: Canonical embedding of Lipschitz-free p p -spaces Thanks: Both authors were supported by the GAČR project 23-04776S
creator: Marek Cúth, Tomáš Raunig
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Marek Cúth, Tomáš Raunig. We find a new finite algorithm for evaluation of Lipschitz-free p p -space norm in finite-dimensional Lipschitz-free p p -spaces. We use this algorithm to deal with the problem of whether given p p -metric spaces 𝒩 ⊂ ℳ \mathcal{N}\subset\mathcal{M} , the canonical embedding of ℱ p ​ ( 𝒩 ) \mathcal{F}_{p}(\mathcal{N}) into ℱ p ​ ( ℳ ) \mathcal{F}_{p}(\mathcal{M}) is an isomorphism.

title: Tight upper bound on the clique size in the square of 2-degenerate graphs
creator: Seog-Jin Kim, Xiaopan Lian
description: Abstract The square of a graph G G , denoted G 2 G^{2} , has the same vertex set as G G and has an edge between two vertices if the distance between them in G G is at most 2 2 .

title: Obstacle- and Occlusion-Responsive Visual Tracking Control for Redundant Manipulators using Reachability Measure
creator: Mincheul Kang, Junhyoung Ha
description: Abstract A vision system attached to a manipulator excels at tracing a moving target object while effectively handling obstacles, overcoming limitations arising from the camera’s confined field of view and occluded line of sight. Meanwhile, the manipulator may encounter certain challenges, including restricted motion due to kinematic constraints and the risk of colliding with external obstacles.

title: On real analytic functions on closed subanalytic domains Thanks: Supported by FWF-Project P 32905-N
creator: Armin Rainer
description: Abstract . We show that a function f : X → ℝ f:X\to\mathbb{R} defined on a closed uniformly polynomially cuspidal set X X in ℝ n \mathbb{R}^{n} is real analytic if and only if f f is smooth and all its composites with germs of polynomial curves in X X are real analytic.

title: Variational Weighting for Kernel Density Ratios
creator: Sangwoong Yoon, Frank C. Park, Gunsu Yun, Iljung Kim, Yung-Kyun Noh
description: Abstract Kernel density estimation (KDE) is integral to a range of generative and discriminative tasks in machine learning. Drawing upon tools from the multidimensional calculus of variations, we derive an optimal weight function that reduces bias in standard kernel density estimates for density ratios, leading to improved estimates of prediction posteriors and information-theoretic measures.

title: Non deterministic Pseudorandom Generator for Quantum Key Distribution
creator: Lucy Sharma
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Lucy Sharma. Quantum Key Distribution(QKD) thrives to achieve perfect secrecy of Onetime Pad (OTP) through quantum processes. One of the crucial components of QKD are Quantum Random Number Generators(QRNG) for generation of keys. Unfortunately, these QRNG does not immediately produce usable bits rather it produces raw bits with high entropy but low uniformity which can be hardly used by any cryptographic system. A lot of pre-processing is required before the random numbers generated by QRNG to be usable.

title: Horizon-bound objects: Kerr–Vaidya solutions
creator: Pravin K. Dahal, Swayamsiddha Maharana, Fil Simovic, Daniel R. Terno
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Pravin K. Dahal, Swayamsiddha Maharana, Fil Simovic, Daniel R. Terno. Kerr–Vaidya metrics are the simplest dynamical axially-symmetric solutions, all of which violate the null energy condition and thus are consistent with the formation of a trapped region in finite time according to distant observers. We examine different classes of Kerr–Vaidya metrics, and find two which possess spherically-symmetric counterparts that are compatible with the finite formation time of a trapped region. These solutions describe evaporating black holes and expanding white holes.

title: Progress in the Partial-Wave Analysis Methods at COMPASS
creator: \firstname Florian Markus \lastname Kaspar \fnsep, \firstname Julien \lastname Beckers \fnsep, \firstname Jakob \lastname Knollmüller \fnsep for the COMPASS Collaboration
description: Abstract We study the excitation spectrum of light and strange mesons in diffractive scattering. We identify different hadron resonances through partial wave analysis, which inherently relies on analysis models. Besides statistical uncertainties, the model dependence of the analysis introduces dominant systematic uncertainties.

title: Validity problems in clinical machine learning by indirect data labeling using consensus definitions \titletag Thanks: This article is an extended version of Chapter 2.4.3 of Riezler and Hagmann 2021 .
creator: Michael Hagmann, Shigehiko Schamoni, Stefan Riezler
description: Abstract We demonstrate a validity problem of machine learning in the vital application area of disease diagnosis in medicine. It arises when target labels in training data are determined by an indirect measurement, and the fundamental measurements needed to determine this indirect measurement are included in the input data representation.

title: Topology Optimization for Microwave Control With Reconfigurable Intelligent Metasurfaces In Complex Media
creator: Theodosios D. Karamanos, Mathias Fink, Fabrice Lemoult
description: Abstract Reconfigurable intelligent metasurfaces have been proposed as an efficient solution for improving wireless telecommunication systems in multiple scattering or reverberating media. Concurrently, topology optimization has been successfully employed as an inverse design technique in many fields, and particularly in electromagnetics.

title: MixUp-MIL: A Study on Linear & Multilinear Interpolation-Based Data Augmentation for Whole Slide Image Classification
creator: Michael Gadermayr 1, Lukas Koller 1, Maximilian Tschuchnig 1, Lea Maria Stangassinger 2, Christina Kreutzer 3, Sebastien Couillard-Despres 3, Gertie Janneke Oostingh 2, Anton Hittmair 4
description: Abstract For classifying digital whole slide images in the absence of pixel level annotations, multiple instance learning methods are typically applied. Such methods are currently of very high interest in the research community due to the generic applicability, whereby the issue of data augmentation in this context is rarely explored.

title: Joint distributions of statistics over permutations avoiding two patterns of length 3
creator: Tian Han, Sergey Kitaev
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Tian Han, Sergey Kitaev. Finding distributions of permutation statistics over pattern-avoiding classes of permutations attracted much attention in the literature. In particular, Bukata et al. found distributions of ascents and descents on permutations avoiding any two patterns of length 3.

title: Grouping Local Process Models
creator: Viki Peeva, Wil M.P. van der Aalst
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Viki Peeva, Wil M.P. van der Aalst. In recent years, process mining emerged as a proven technology to analyze and improve operational processes. An expanding range of organizations using process mining in their daily operation brings a broader spectrum of processes to be analyzed. Some of these processes are highly unstructured, making it difficult for traditional process discovery approaches to discover a start-to-end model describing the entire process.

title: Cross-section of the Nb 95 {{}^{95\rm}\rm{Nb}} production on natural molybdenum at the bremsstrahlung end-point energy up to 95 MeV
creator: I.S. Timchenko 1,2,, O.S. Deiev 2 , S.M. Olejnik 2 , S.M. Potin 2 , V.A. Kushnir 2 , V.V. Mytrochenko 2,3 , S.A. Perezhogin 2
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by I.S. Timchenko 1,2,, O.S. Deiev 2 , S.M. Olejnik 2 , S.M. Potin 2 , V.A. Kushnir 2 , V.V. Mytrochenko 2,3 , S.A. Perezhogin 2. The photoproduction of 95m Nb on Mo nat {{}^{\rm nat}\rm{Mo}} was studied using the electron beam of the LUE-40 linac RDC ”Accelerator” NSC KIPT. Measurements were performed using activation and off-line γ \gamma -ray spectrometric techniques.

title: Zero-shot Bilingual App Reviews Mining with Large Language Models
creator: Jialiang Wei, Anne-Lise Courbis, Thomas Lambolais, Binbin Xu, Pierre Louis Bernard, Gérard Dray, [6pt] : EuroMov Digital Health in Motion, Univ Montpellier, IMT Mines Ales, Ales, France
description: Abstract App reviews from app stores are crucial for improving software requirements. A large number of valuable reviews are continually being posted, describing software problems and expected features. Effectively utilizing user reviews necessitates the extraction of relevant information, as well as their subsequent summarization. Due to the substantial volume of user reviews, manual analysis is arduous.

title: Byzantine Consensus in Abstract MAC Layer
creator: Lewis Tseng, Callie Sardina
description: Abstract This paper studies the design of Byzantine consensus algorithms in an asynchronous single-hop network equipped with the “abstract MAC layer” [DISC09], which captures core properties of modern wireless MAC protocols. Newport [PODC14], Newport and Robinson [DISC18], and Tseng and Zhang [PODC22] study crash-tolerant consensus in the model.

title: Coulomb impurities in graphene driven by ultrashort electromagnetic pulses: Excitation, ionization, and pair creation
creator: Saparboy Rakhmanov, Reinhold Egger, Davron Matrasulov
description: Abstract We provide a theory for electronic transitions induced by ultrashort electromagnetic pulses in two-dimensional artificial relativistic atoms which are created by a charged impurity in a gapped graphene monolayer. Using a non-perturbative sudden-perturbation approximation, we derive and discuss analytical expressions for the probabilities for excitation, ionization and electron-hole pair creation in this system.

title: Learned layered coding for Successive Refinement in the Wyner-Ziv Problem
creator: Boris Joukovsky ID, Brent De Weerdt ID, Nikos Deligiannis ID
description: Abstract We propose a data-driven approach to explicitly learn the progressive encoding of a continuous source, which is successively decoded with increasing levels of quality and with the aid of correlated side information. This setup refers to the successive refinement of the Wyner-Ziv coding problem.

title: Regularity for almost minimizers of a one-phase Bernoulli-type functional in Carnot Groups of step two Thanks: The authors are members of Gruppo Nazionale per l’Analisi Matematica, la Probabilitá e le loro Applicazioni (GNAMPA) of the Istituto Nazionale di Alta Matematica (INdAM): F.F. has been part
creator: Fausto Ferrari, Nicolò Forcillo, Enzo Maria Merlino
description: Abstract . We prove that nonnegative almost minimizers of the horizontal Bernoulli-type functional J ( u , Ω ) := ∫ Ω ( | ∇ 𝔾 u ( x ) | 2 + χ { u > 0 } ( x ) ) d x J(u,\Omega):=\int_{\Omega}\Big(|\nabla_{\mathbb{G}}u(x)|^{2}+\chi_{\{u>0\}}(x)\Big)\,dx are Lipschitz continuous with respect to the Carnot-Carathéodory distance.

title: Modelling cross-correlations of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays and galaxies
creator: Federico R. Urban a, Stefano Camera b , c {}^{b,\,c}, and David Alonso d
description: Abstract The astrophysical engines that power ultra-high-energy cosmic rays (UHECRs) remain to date unknown. Since the propagation horizon of UHECRs is limited to the local, anisotropic Universe, the distribution of UHECR arrival directions should be anisotropic. In this paper we expand the analysis of the potential for the angular, harmonic cross-correlation between UHECRs and galaxies to detect such anisotropies.

title: Statistical analysis of vortex condensate motion in two-dimensional turbulence
creator: Vladimir Parfenyev
description: Abstract An inverse turbulent cascade in a periodic square box produces a coherent system-sized vortex dipole. We study the statistics of its motion by carrying out direct numerical simulations performed for various bottom friction α \alpha , pumping intensity ε \varepsilon , and fluid hyperviscosity ν \nu .

title: Quantifying the value of information transfer in population-based SHM
creator: A.J. Hughes, J. Poole, N. Dervilis, P. Gardner & K. Worden
description: Abstract Abstract Population-based structural health monitoring (PBSHM), seeks to address some of the limitations associated with data scarcity that arise in traditional SHM. A tenet of the population-based approach to SHM is that information can be shared between sufficiently-similar structures in order to improve predictive models.

title: Inefficient acceleration of electrons in the shocked wind of the massive star Θ 1 \Theta^{1} Ori C within the Trapezium cluster Inefficient acceleration of electrons in the shocked wind of the massive star Θ 1 \Theta^{1} Ori C within the Trapezium cluster – References 2015
creator: W. Bednarek
description: Abstract Shocked winds of massive stars in young stellar clusters have been proposed as possible sites in which relativistic particles are accelerated. Electrons, accelerated in such an environment, are expected to efficiently comptonize optical radiation (from massive stars) and the infra-red radiation (re-scattered by the dust within the cluster) producing GeV-TeV gamma-rays.

title: SoK: Memorisation in Machine Learning
creator: Dmitrii Usynin 1,2 , Moritz Knolle 2,3 , Georgios Kaissis 1,2,3
description: Abstract Quantifying the impact of individual data samples on machine learning models is an open research problem. This is particularly relevant when complex and high-dimensional relationships have to be learned from a limited sample of the data generating distribution, such as in deep learning.

title: Bridging the gap between agent based models and continuous opinion dynamics
creator: Andrew Nugent, Susana N. Gomes, Marie-Therese Wolfram
description: Abstract There is a rich literature on microscopic models for opinion dynamics; most of them fall into one of two categories - agent-based models or differential equation models - with a general understanding that the two are connected in certain scaling limits. In this paper we show rigorously this is indeed the case.

title: On Preimages Question
creator: Yohsuke Matsuzawa, Kaoru Sano
description: Abstract . For a surjective self-morphism on a projective variety defined over a number field, we study the preimages question, which asks if the set of rational points on the iterated preimages of an invariant closed subscheme eventually stabilize. We prove the answer is positive for self-morphisms on ℙ 1 × ℙ 1 {\mathbb{P}}^{1}\times{\mathbb{P}}^{1} .

title: List of problems Thanks: The second author has been partially supported by the grant PID2019-104844GB-I00
creator: Martina Juhnke-Kubitzke, Rosa M. Miró-Roig
description: Abstract . The study of the Lefschetz properties of Artinian graded algebras was motivated by the hard Lefschetz theorem for a smooth complex projective variety, a breakthrough in algebraic topology and geometry. Over the last few years, this topic has attracted increasing attention from mathematicians in various areas.

title: Equivariance Is Not All You Need: Characterizing the Utility of Equivariant Graph Neural Networks for Particle Physics Tasks
creator: Savannah Thais, Daniel Murnane
description: Abstract Incorporating inductive biases into ML models is an active area of ML research, especially when ML models are applied to data about the physical world. Equivariant Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have recently become a popular method for learning from physics data because they directly incorporate the symmetries of the underlying physical system.

title: On regularized polynomial functional regression
creator: Markus Holzleitner, Sergei V. Pereverzyev
description: Abstract This article offers a comprehensive treatment of polynomial functional regression, culminating in the establishment of a novel finite sample bound. This bound encompasses various aspects, including general smoothness conditions, capacity conditions, and regularization techniques. In doing so, it extends and generalizes several findings from the context of linear functional regression as well.

title: Injecting Categorical Label and Syntactic Information into Biomedical NER
creator: Sumam Francis ∗1 and Marie-Francine Moens 1
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Sumam Francis ∗1 and Marie-Francine Moens 1. Biomedical Named Entity Recognition, Attribute Injection, Deep Learning, Text Classification Abstract. We present a simple approach to improve biomedical named entity recognition (NER) by injecting categorical labels and Part of Speech (POS) information into the model. We use two approaches, in the first approach, we first train a sequence-level classifier to classify the sentences into categories to obtain the sentence-level tags (categorical labels).

title: Unified Multi-modal Unsupervised Representation Learning for Skeleton-based Action Understanding Conference: Proceedings of the 31st ACM International Conference on Multimedia; October 29-November 3, 2023; Ottawa, ON, Canada Proceedings of the 31st ACM International Conference on Multimedia (MM ’23)
creator: Shengkai Sun, Daizong Liu, Jianfeng Dong, Xiaoye Qu, Junyu Gao, Xun Yang, Xun Wang, Meng Wang
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Shengkai Sun, Daizong Liu, Jianfeng Dong, Xiaoye Qu, Junyu Gao, Xun Yang, Xun Wang, Meng Wang. Unsupervised pre-training has shown great success in skeleton-based action understanding recently. Existing works typically train separate modality-specific models ( i.e. , joint, bone, and motion), then integrate the multi-modal information for action understanding by a late-fusion strategy. Although these approaches have achieved significant performance, they suffer from the complex yet redundant multi-stream model designs, each of which is also limited to the fixed input skeleton modality.

title: Analytical approximations of Lotka-Volterra integrals
creator: Niklas L.P. Lundström, Gunnar J. Söderbacka
description: Abstract In this note we derive simple analytical bounds for solutions of x − ln ⁡ x = y − ln ⁡ y x-\ln x=y-\ln y and use them for estimating trajectories following Lotka-Volterra-type integrals. We show how our results imply estimates for the Lambert W W function as well as for trajectories of general predator-prey systems, including e.g.

title: A survey and classification of face alignment methods based on face models
creator: Jagmohan Meher 1 , Hector Allende-Cid 2 3 , Torbjörn E. M. Nordling 1
description: Abstract A face model is a mathematical representation of the distinct features of a human face. Traditionally, face models were built using a set of fiducial points or landmarks, each point ideally located on a facial feature, i.e., corner of the eye, tip of the nose, etc.

title: Maximal Consistent Subsystems of Max-T Fuzzy Relational Equations
creator: Ismaïl Baaj
description: Abstract In this article, we study the inconsistency of a system of max − T \max-T fuzzy relational equations of the form A ​ □ T max ​ x = b A\Box_{T}^{\max}x=b , where T T is a t-norm among min \min , the product or Lukasiewicz’s t-norm.

title: Constraints on Dark Energy from the Gravitational Wave Background
creator: Jafar Khodagholizadeh
description: Abstract Current observational data indicate that dark energy (DE) is a cosmological constant without considering its conclusiveness evidence. Considering the dynamic nature of Λ \Lambda individually as a function of time and the scale factor, we review their effects on the gravitational waves.

title: Ignoring Time Dependence in Software Engineering Data. A Mistake
creator: Mikel Robredo, Nyyti Saarimäki, Rafael Peñaloza, Valentina Lenarduzzi
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Mikel Robredo, Nyyti Saarimäki, Rafael Peñaloza, Valentina Lenarduzzi. Researchers often delve into the connections between different factors derived from the historical data of software projects. For example, scholars have devoted their endeavors to the exploration of associations among these factors. However, a significant portion of these studies has failed to consider the limitations posed by the temporal interdependencies among these variables and the potential risks associated with the use of statistical methods ill-suited for analyzing data with temporal connections.

title: Charge and energy deposition in the McDipper framework
creator: Hannah Elfner
description: Abstract In this short note we present aspects of the energy and charge deposition within the McDipper , a novel 3D resolved model for the initial state of ultrarelativistic Heavy-Ion collisions based on the k ⟂ k_{\perp} -factorized Color Glass Condensate hybrid approach.

title: DRAUC: An Instance-wise Distributionally Robust AUC Optimization Framework
creator: Siran Dai Qianqian Xu Zhiyong Yang Xiaochun Cao Qingming Huang SKLOIS, Institute of Information Engineering, CAS School of Cyber Security, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences Key Lab. of Intelligent Information Processing, Institute of Computing Tech., CAS School of Computer Science and Tech.,
description: Abstract The Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC) is a widely employed metric in long-tailed classification scenarios. Nevertheless, most existing methods primarily assume that training and testing examples are drawn i.i.d. from the same distribution, which is often unachievable in practice.

title: The European Moon Rover System: a modular multipurpose rover for future complex lunar missions Thanks: The EMRS rover has been developed during European Moon Rover Sys-tem Pre-Phase A project fully funded by ESA under grant agreement No. 4000137474/22/NL/GLC. Seoane 1 , Iñaki Colmenarejo 1 , Steven Kay 2 , Angus Cameron 2 , Carmen Camañes 3 , Íñigo Sard 3 , Danel Juárez 3 , Alessandro Orlandi 4 , Federica Angeletti 4 , Vassilios Papantoniou 5 , Ares Papantoniou 5 , Sp

creator: Lucía Córdova, Miguel Correia, Alessandro Georgoudis, and Antoine Vuignier
description: Abstract We revisit the space of gapped quantum field theories with a global O(N) symmetry in two spacetime dimensions. Previous works using S-matrix bootstrap revealed a rich space in which integrable theories such as the non-linear sigma model appear at special points on the boundary, along with an abundance of unknown models hinting at a non conventional UV behaviour.

title: Algorithm 3
creator: Imminent collisions algorithm (v2)
description: Abstract Weight-sharing is ubiquitous in deep learning. Motivated by this, we propose a “weight-sharing regularization” penalty on the weights w ∈ ℝ d w\in\mathbb{R}^{d} of a neural network, defined as ℛ ⁡ ( w ) = 1 d − 1 ​ ∑ i > j d | w i − w j | \mathcal{R}(w)=\frac{1}{d-1}\sum_{i>j}^{d}|w_{i}-w_{j}| .

creator: Dzung Tri Tran, Thanh Huy Nguyen, Khiem Hong Phan
description: Abstract We present one-loop contributing for h → ℓ ​ ℓ ¯ ​ γ h\rightarrow\ell\bar{\ell}\gamma with ℓ = ν e , μ , τ , e , μ \ell=\nu_{e,\mu,\tau},e,\mu and e − ​ e + → h ​ γ e^{-}e^{+}\rightarrow h\gamma in U ​ ( 1 ) B − L U(1)_{B-L} extension of the standard models.

title: Incorporating basic RANS calibrations in existing machine-learned turbulence modeling
creator: Jiaqi J.L. Li, Yuanwei Bin, George P. Huang, Xiang I.A. Yang
description: Abstract This work aims to incorporate basic calibrations of Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes (RANS) models as part of machine learning (ML) frameworks. The ML frameworks considered are tensor-basis neural network (TBNN), physics-informed machine learning (PIML), and field inversion & machine learning (FIML) in J. Fluid Mech. , 2016, 807, 155-166, Phys. Rev. Fluids , 2017, 2(3), 034603 and J. Comp. Phys.

title: RELand: Risk Estimation of Landmines via Interpretable Invariant Risk Minimization
creator: Mateo Dulce Rubio, Siqi Zeng, Qi Wang, Didier Alvarado, Francisco Moreno, Hoda Heidari, Fei Fang
description: Abstract Landmines remain a threat to war-affected communities for years after conflicts have ended, partly due to the laborious nature of demining tasks. Humanitarian demining operations begin by collecting relevant information from the sites to be cleared, which is then analyzed by human experts to determine the potential risk of remaining landmines.

title: Architectural Sweet Spots for Modeling Human Label Variation by the Example of Argument Quality: It’s Best to Relate Perspectives!
creator: Philipp Heinisch, Matthias Orlikowski, Julia Romberg, Philipp Cimiano
description: Abstract Many annotation tasks in natural language processing are highly subjective in that there can be different valid and justified perspectives on what is a proper label for a given example. This also applies to the judgment of argument quality, where the assignment of a single ground truth is often questionable.

title: Using Shallow Neural Networks with Functional Connectivity from EEG signals for Early Diagnosis of Alzheimer’s and Frontotemporal Dementia
creator: Zaineb Ajra, Binbin Xu, Gérard Dray, Jacky Montmain, Stéphane Perrey
description: Abstract Introduction: Dementia is a neurological disorder associated with aging that can cause a loss of cognitive functions, impacting daily life. Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is the most common cause of dementia, accounting for 50–70% of cases, while frontotemporal dementia (FTD) affects social skills and personality. Electroencephalography (EEG) provides an effective tool to study the effects of AD on the brain.

title: Mathematical modeling of heat process in a cylindrical domain with nonlinear thermal coefficients and a heat source on the axis
creator: Julieta Bollati, Adriana C. Briozzo, Stanislav N. Kharin, Targyn A. Nauryz
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Julieta Bollati, Adriana C. Briozzo, Stanislav N. Kharin, Targyn A. Nauryz. A mathematical model of the heat process in one-dimensional domain governed by a cylindrical heat equation with a heat source on the axis z = 0 z=0 and nonlinear thermal coefficients is considered. The developed model is particularly applicable for analyzing temperature variations on electrical contact surfaces, where precise thermal management is crucial for ensuring optimal performance and preventing overheating.

title: SurfFlow : high-throughput surface energy calculations for arbitrary crystals
creator: Firat Yalcin, Michael Wolloch
description: Abstract We introduce SurfFlow , an open-source high-throughput workflow package designed for automated first-principles calculations of surface energies in arbitrary crystals. Our package offers a comprehensive solution capable of handling multi-element crystals, nonstoichiometric compositions, and asymmetric slabs, for all potential terminations.

title: Martingale approximation of non-stationary stochastic processes
creator: Dalibor Volný
description: Abstract We generalise the martingale-coboundary representation of discrete time stochastic processes to the non-stationary case and to random variables in Orlicz spaces. Related limit theorems (CLT, invariance principle, log log law, probabilities of large deviations) are studied. Classification: 60G10, 60G42, 28D05, 60F05 0. Introduction Let (\Omega,A,\mu) be a probability space and (X_{i})_{i\in\mathbb{Z}} a sequence of random variables.

title: Collision Avoidance using Iterative Dynamic and Nonlinear Programming with Adaptive Grid Refinements
creator: Rebecca Richter, Alberto De Marchi, Matthias Gerdts
description: Abstract Nonlinear optimal control problems for trajectory planning with obstacle avoidance present several challenges. While general-purpose optimizers and dynamic programming methods struggle when adopted separately, their combination enabled by a penalty approach is capable of handling highly nonlinear systems while overcoming the curse of dimensionality.

title: Persuasion and Matching: Optimal Productive Transport Thanks: Kolotilin : School of Economics, UNSW Business School. Corrao and Wolitzky : Department of Economics, MIT. This paper supercedes earlier papers titled “Persuasion with Non-Linear Preferences,” “Persuasion as Matching,” and “Assortative In
creator: Anton Kolotilin, Roberto Corrao, and Alexander Wolitzky
description: Abstract . We consider general Bayesian persuasion problems where the receiver’s utility is single-peaked in a one-dimensional action. We show that a signal that pools at most two states in each realization is always optimal, and that such pairwise signals are the only solutions under a non-singularity condition (the twist condition ).

title: Generalized integrals and point interactions
creator: Jan Dereziński 1, Christian Gaß 1 and Błażej Ruba 2
description: Abstract First we recall a method of computing scalar products of eigenfunctions of a Sturm-Liouville operator. This method is then applied to Macdonald and Gegenbauer functions, which are eigenfunctions of the Bessel, resp. Gegenbauer operators. The computed scalar products are well defined only for a limited range of parameters.

title: Tensor Golub Kahan based on Einstein product
creator: A. El Hachimi, K. Jbilou, M. Hached, A. Ratnani
description: Abstract The Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) of matrices is a widely used tool in scientific computing. In many applications of machine learning, data analysis, signal and image processing, the large datasets are structured into tensors, for which generalisations of SVD have already been introduced, for various types of tensor-tensor products.

title: GPTuner : A Manual-Reading Database Tuning System via GPT-Guided Bayesian Optimization
creator: Jiale Lao, Yibo Wang, Yufei Li, Jianping Wang, Yunjia Zhang, Zhiyuan Cheng, Wanghu Chen, Mingjie Tang, Jianguo Wang
description: Abstract . Modern database management systems (DBMS) expose hundreds of configurable knobs to control system behaviours. Determining the appropriate values for these knobs to improve DBMS performance is a long-standing problem in the database community. As there is an increasing number of knobs to tune and each knob could be in continuous or categorical values, manual tuning becomes impractical.

title: Controlling effective field contributions to laser-induced magnetization precession by heterostructure design
creator: J. Jarecki, M. Mattern, F.-C. Weber, J.-E. Pudell, X.-G. Wang, J.-C. Rojas Sánchez, M. Hehn, A. von Reppert, M. Bargheer
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by J. Jarecki, M. Mattern, F.-C. Weber, J.-E. Pudell, X.-G. Wang, J.-C. Rojas Sánchez, M. Hehn, A. von Reppert, M. Bargheer. Nanoscale heterostructure design can control laser-induced heat dissipation and strain propagation as well as their efficiency for driving magnetization precession. We use insulating MgO layers incorporated into metallic Pt-Cu-Ni heterostructures to block the propagation of hot electrons.

title: Recursive construction for expansions of tree Yang-Mills amplitudes from soft theorem
creator: Chang Hu ab , Kang Zhou c
description: Abstract In this paper, we have introduced a fundamentally different approach, based on a bottom-up methodology, to expand tree-level Yang-Mills (YM) amplitudes into Yang-Mills-scalar (YMS) amplitudes and Bi-adjoint-scalar (BAS) amplitudes. Our method relies solely on the intrinsic soft behavior of external gluons, eliminating the need for external aids such as Feynman rules or CHY rules.

title: Persistent Homology for High-dimensional Data Based on Spectral Methods
creator: Sebastian Damrich Philipp Berens Dmitry Kobak
description: Abstract Persistent homology is a popular computational tool for analyzing the topology of point clouds, such as the presence of loops or voids. However, many real-world datasets with low intrinsic dimensionality reside in an ambient space of much higher dimensionality.

title: Measurement of the energy of the 8.3-eV isomer of 229m Th with photoelectric effect.
creator: F. F. Karpeshin
description: Abstract It is proposed to use the photoelectric effect in the inner shells of the 229 Th atom to refine the energy of its 8.3-eV isomer. The calculation was performed using the Feinberg—Migdal shaking theory, which leads to the probability of isomer formation up to several units of 10 − 4 10^{-4} in the case of K K -shell.

title: LCPR: A Multi-Scale Attention-Based LiDAR-Camera Fusion Network for Place Recognition
creator: Zijie Zhou, Jingyi Xu, Guangming Xiong, Junyi Ma*
description: Abstract Place recognition is one of the most crucial modules for autonomous vehicles to identify places that were previously visited in GPS-invalid environments. Sensor fusion is considered an effective method to overcome the weaknesses of individual sensors. In recent years, multimodal place recognition fusing information from multiple sensors has gathered increasing attention.

title: Euclid’s Near-Infrared Spectrometer and Photometer ready for flight – review of final performance
creator: E. Medinaceli, L. Valenziano, N. Auricchio, E. Franceschi, F. Gianotti, P. Battaglia, R. Farinelli, A. Balestra, S. Dusini, C. Sirignano, E. Borsato, L. Stanco, A. Renzi, A. Troja, L. Gabarra, S. Ligori, V. Capobianco, L. Corcione, D. Bonino, G. Sirri, L. Patrizii, M. Tenti, D. Di Ferdinando, C. Val
description: Abstract ESA’s mission Euclid , while undertaking its final integration stage, is fully qualified. Euclid will perform an extra galactic survey ( 0 < z < 2 0<z<2 ) by observing in the visible and near-infrared wavelength range. To detect infrared radiation, it is equipped with the Near Infrared Spectrometer and Photometer (NISP) instrument, operating in the 0.9–2 µm range.

title: PainSeeker: An Automated Method for Assessing Pain in Rats Through Facial Expressions
creator: Liu Liu, Guang Li, Dingfan Deng, Jinhua Yu, and Yuan Zong
description: Abstract In this letter, we aim to investigate whether laboratory rats’ pain can be automatically assessed through their facial expressions. To this end, we began by presenting a publicly available dataset called RatsPain, consisting of 1,138 facial images captured from six rats that underwent an orthodontic treatment.

title: Stable Linear Subspace Identification: A Machine Learning Approach
creator: Loris Di Natale, Muhammad Zakwan, Bratislav Svetozarevic, Philipp Heer, Giancarlo Ferrari-Trecate, Colin N. Jones
description: Abstract Machine Learning (ML) and linear System Identification (SI) have been historically developed independently. In this paper, we leverage well-established ML tools — especially the automatic differentiation framework — to introduce SIMBa, a family of discrete linear multi-step-ahead state-space SI methods using backpropagation.

title: Fate of localization features in a one-dimensional non-Hermitian flat-band lattice with quasiperiodic modulations
creator: Zhihao Xu*
description: Abstract We investigate the influence of quasiperiodic modulations on one-dimensional non-Hermitian diamond lattices with an artificial magnetic flux θ \theta that possess flat bands. Our study shows that the symmetry of these modulations and the magnetic flux θ \theta play a pivotal role in shaping the localization properties of the system.

title: A contract negotiation scheme for safety verification of interconnected systems
creator: Xiao Tan, Antonis Papachristodoulou, Dimos V. Dimarogonas
description: Abstract This paper proposes a (control) barrier function synthesis and safety verification scheme for interconnected nonlinear systems based on assume-guarantee contracts (AGC) and sum-of-squares (SOS) techniques. It is well-known that the SOS approach does not scale well for barrier function synthesis for high-dimensional systems. In this paper, we show that compositional methods like AGC can mitigate this problem.

title: ONE-LOOP CORRECTION CONTRIBUTIONS IN THE DECOUPLING LIMIT OF GENERALIZED YUKAWA MODEL
creator: M.S. Dmytriiev, V.V. Skalozub
description: Abstract We consider the generalized Yukawa model consisting of two Dirac fermions and two scalar fields. One of the scalars is assumed to be much heavier than the other particles, so it decouples at low energies. Low-energy effective Lagrangian (EL) of the model is derived.

title: A two-site Kitaev chain in a two-dimensional electron gas
creator: Sebastiaan L.D. ten Haaf, Qingzhen Wang, A. Mert Bozkurt, Chun-Xiao Liu, Ivan Kulesh, Philip Kim, Di Xiao, Candice Thomas, Michael J. Manfra, Tom Dvir, Michael Wimmer, Srijit Goswami
description: Abstract Artificial Kitaev chains can be used to engineer Majorana bound states (MBSs) in superconductor-semiconductor hybrids Sau and Sarma 2012 ; Leijnse and Flensberg 2012 ; Ful 2013 ; Dvir et al. 2023 . In this work, we realize a two-site Kitaev chain in a two-dimensional electron gas by coupling two quantum dots through a region proximitized by a superconductor.

title: Robust poor man’s Majorana zero modes using Yu-Shiba-Rusinov states
creator: Francesco Zatelli, David van Driel, Di Xu, Guanzhong Wang, Chun-Xiao Liu, Alberto Bordin, Bart Roovers, Grzegorz P. Mazur, Nick van Loo, Jan C. Wolff, A. Mert Bozkurt, Ghada Badawy, Sasa Gazibegovic, Erik P. A. M. Bakkers, Michael Wimmer, Leo P. Kouwenhoven, Tom Dvir
description: Abstract The recent realization of a two-site Kitaev chain featuring “poor man’s Majorana” states demonstrates a path forward in the field of topological superconductivity. Harnessing the potential of these states for quantum information processing, however, requires increasing their robustness to external perturbations. Here, we form a two-site Kitaev chain using proximitized quantum dots hosting Yu-Shiba-Rusinov states.

title: A Basmajian-type inequality for Riemannian surfaces Thanks: The first author acknowledges support by the FSE/AEI/MICINN grant RYC-2016-19334 “Local and global systolic geometry and topology”. The second author acknowledges support by the Luxembourg National Research Fund PRIDE17/1224660/GPS. The fir
creator: Florent Balacheff, David Fisac
description: Abstract . We explore for compact Riemannian surfaces whose boundary consists of a single closed geodesic the relationship between orthospectrum and boundary length. More precisely, we etablish a uniform lower bound on the boundary length in terms of the orthospectrum when fixing a metric invariant of the surface related to the classical notion of volume entropy.

title: Mini Minds: Exploring Bebeshka and Zlata Baby Models
creator: Irina Proskurina, Guillaume Metzler, Julien Velcin
description: Abstract In this paper, we describe the University of Lyon 2 submission to the Strict-Small track of the BabyLM competition.
