Many approaches have been proposed to adapt neural networks for this task, but still, boosting and bagging of decision trees are the best-performing methods for this task.

title: Telecom band quantum dot technologies for long-distance quantum networks
creator: Ying Yu, Shunfa Liu, Chang-Min Lee, Peter Michler, Stephan Reitzenstein, Kartik Srinivasan, Edo Waks, Jin Liu
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Ying Yu, Shunfa Liu, Chang-Min Lee, Peter Michler, Stephan Reitzenstein, Kartik Srinivasan, Edo Waks, Jin Liu. A future quantum internet is expected to generate, distribute, store and process quantum bits (qubits) over the globe by linking different quantum nodes via quantum states of light. To facilitate the long-haul operations, quantum repeaters, the building blocks for a long-distance quantum network, have to be operated in the telecom wavelengths to take advantage of both the low-loss fiber network and the well-established technologies for optical communications.

title: Human-AI Collaboration in Thematic Analysis using ChatGPT: A User Study and Design Recommendations DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX CCS: Human-centered computing User studies CCS: Human-centered computing Collaborative interaction
creator: Lixiang Yan, Vanessa Echeverria, Gloria Fernandez Nieto, Yueqiao Jin, Zachari Swiecki, Linxuan Zhao, Dragan Gašević, Roberto Martinez-Maldonado
description: Abstract . Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) offers promising potential for advancing human-AI collaboration in qualitative research. However, existing works focused on conventional machine-learning and pattern-based AI systems, and little is known about how researchers interact with GenAI in qualitative research. This work delves into researchers’ perceptions of their collaboration with GenAI, specifically ChatGPT.

title: Quantum signal processing over SU(N)
creator: Lorenzo Laneve
description: Abstract Quantum signal processing (QSP) and the quantum singular value transformation (QSVT) are pivotal tools for simplifying the development of quantum algorithms. These techniques leverage polynomial transformations on the eigenvalues or singular values of block-encoded matrices, achieved with the use of just one control qubit.

title: Spectral functions of the strongly interacting 3D Fermi gas
creator: Christian H. Johansen, Bernhard Frank, Johannes Lang
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Christian H. Johansen, Bernhard Frank, Johannes Lang. Computing dynamical properties of strongly interacting quantum many-body systems poses a major challenge to theoretical approaches. Usually, one has to resort to numerical analytic continuation of results on imaginary frequencies, which is a mathematically ill-defined procedure. Here, we present an efficient method to compute the spectral functions of the two-component Fermi gas near the strongly interacting unitary limit directly in real frequencies.

title: CeCNN: Copula-enhanced convolutional neural networks in joint prediction of refraction error and axial length based on ultra-widefield fundus images
creator: Chong Zhong †, Yang Li †, Danjuan Yang, Meiyan Li, Xingtao Zhou, Bo Fu ‡, Catherine C. Liu ‡, A.H. Welsh
description: Abstract The ultra-widefield (UWF) fundus image is an attractive 3D biomarker in AI-aided myopia screening because it provides much richer myopia-related information. Though axial length (AL) has been acknowledged to be highly related to the two key targets of myopia screening, Spherical Equivalence (SE) measurement and high myopia diagnosis, its prediction based on the UWF fundus image is rarely considered.

title: Analytic and Monte Carlo Approximations to the Distribution of the First Passage Time of the Drifted Diffusion with Stochastic Resetting and Mixed Boundary Conditions Journal: arXiv
creator: Juan Magalang, Riccardo Turin, Javier Aguilar, Laetitia Colombani, Daniel Sanchez-Taltavull, Riccardo Gatto
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Juan Magalang, Riccardo Turin, Javier Aguilar, Laetitia Colombani, Daniel Sanchez-Taltavull, Riccardo Gatto. This article introduces two techniques for computing the distribution of the absorption or first passage time of the drifted Wiener diffusion subject to Poisson resetting times, to an upper hard wall barrier and to a lower absorbing barrier.

title: Structural Transition and Magnetic Anisotropy in α \alpha -RuCl 3
creator: Subin Kim, Ezekiel Horsley, Jacob P. C. Ruff, Beatriz D. Moreno, Young-June Kim
description: Abstract We report X-ray diffraction and magnetic susceptibility studies of the structural phase transition in α \alpha -RuCl 3 . By utilizing a single crystal sample with predominantly single twin domain, we show that α \alpha -RuCl 3 goes from high-temperature C2/m structure to a rhombohedral structure with R 3 ¯ \bar{3} symmetry at low temperature.

title: Non-singular word maps for linear groups
creator: Henry Bradford, Jakob Schneider, Andreas Thom
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Henry Bradford, Jakob Schneider, Andreas Thom. We study the word image of words with constants in GL ⁡ ( V ) \GL(V) and show that it is large provided the word satisfies some natural conditions on its length and its critical constants.

title: Exploring Jiu-Jitsu Argumentation for Writing Peer Review Rebuttals
creator: Sukannya Purkayastha Anne Lauscher Iryna Gurevych
description: Abstract In many domains of argumentation, people’s arguments are driven by so-called attitude roots , i.e., underlying beliefs and world views, and their corresponding attitude themes . Given the strength of these latent drivers of arguments, recent work in psychology suggests that instead of directly countering surface-level reasoning (e.g.

title: Topology Only Pre-Training: Towards Generalised Multi-Domain Graph Models
creator: Alex O. Davies, Riku Green, Nirav S. Ajmeri, Telmo M. Silva Filho
description: Abstract The principal benefit of unsupervised representation learning is that a pre-trained model can be fine-tuned where data or labels are scarce. Existing approaches for graph representation learning are domain specific, maintaining consistent node and edge features across the pre-training and target datasets. This has precluded transfer to multiple domains.

title: On the presentation of the Grothendieck-Witt group of symmetric bilinear forms over local rings
creator: Robert Rogers and Marco Schlichting
description:
A 2023 arXiv research paper by Robert Rogers and Marco Schlichting. We prove a Chain Lemma for inner product spaces over commutative local rings R R with residue field other than 𝔽 2 \mathbb{F}_{2} and use this to show that the usual presentation of the Grothendieck-Witt group of symmetric bilinear forms over R R as the zero-th Milnor-Witt K K -group holds provided the residue field of R R is not 𝔽 2 \mathbb{F}_{2} . 1991 Mathematics Subject Classification

title: On a conjecture of Ramírez Alfonsín and Skałba III
creator: Yuchen Ding and Takao Komatsu
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Yuchen Ding and Takao Komatsu. Let 1 < c < d 1<c<d be two relatively prime integers. For a non-negative integer ℓ \ell , let g ℓ ​ ( c , d ) g_{\ell}(c,d) be the largest integer n n such that n = c ​ x + d ​ y n=cx+dy has at most ℓ \ell non-negative solutions ( x , y ) (x,y) .

title: Dimension-independent weak value estimation via controlled SWAP operations
creator: Giulio Chiribella, Kyrylo Simonov, Xuanqiang Zhao
description: Abstract Weak values of quantum observables are a powerful tool for investigating quantum phenomena. Some methods for measuring weak values in the laboratory require weak interactions and postselection, while others are deterministic, but require statistics over a number of experiments that grows linearly with the dimension of the measured system in the worst case over all possible observables.

title: Only long edges can erase the subcritical annulus-crossing phase of weight-dependent random connection models
creator: Emmanuel Jacob
description: Abstract Abstract: This short note aims at complementing the results of the recent work [ 9 ] , where Jahnel and Lüchtrath investigate the question of existence of a subcritical percolation phase for the annulus-crossing probabilities in a large class of continuum percolation models, namely the classical or generalized weight-dependent random connection models.

title: Analyzing Film Adaptation through Narrative Alignment
creator: Tanzir Pial, Shahreen Salim, Charuta Pethe, Allen Kim, Steven Skiena
description: Abstract Novels are often adapted into feature films, but the differences between the two media usually require dropping sections of the source text from the movie script. Here we study this screen adaptation process by constructing narrative alignments using the Smith-Waterman local alignment algorithm coupled with SBERT embedding distance to quantify text similarity between scenes and book units.

title: General relativistic stochastic thermodynamics
creator: Tao Wang, Yifan Cai, Long Cui, Liu Zhao
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Tao Wang, Yifan Cai, Long Cui, Liu Zhao. Based on the recent work [ 1 , 2 ] , we formulate the first law and the second law of stochastic thermodynamics in the framework of general relativity.

title: Coronal Models and Detection of Open Magnetic Field Journal: Astrophysical Journal
creator: Eleanna Asvestari, Manuela Temmer, Ronald M. Caplan, Jon A. Linker, Stephan G. Heinemann, Rui F. Pinto, Carl J. Henney, Charles N. Arge, Mathew J. Owens, Maria S. Madjarska, Jens Pomoell, Stefan J. Hofmeister, Camilla Scolini, Evangelia Samara
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Eleanna Asvestari, Manuela Temmer, Ronald M. Caplan, Jon A. Linker, Stephan G. Heinemann, Rui F. Pinto, Carl J. Henney, Charles N. Arge, Mathew J. Owens, Maria S. Madjarska, Jens Pomoell, Stefan J. Hofmeister, Camilla Scolini, Evangelia Samara. A plethora of coronal models, from empirical to more complex magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) ones, are being used for reconstructing the coronal magnetic field topology and estimating the open magnetic flux.

title: The conjugacy problem for Out ⁡ ( F 3 ) \operatorname{Out}(F_{3}) .
creator: François Dahmani, Stefano Francaviglia, Armando Martino, Nicholas Touikan
description: Abstract . We present a solution to the Conjugacy Problem in the group of outer-automorphisms of F 3 F_{3} , a free group of rank 3. We distinguish according to several computable invariants, such as irreducibility, subgroups of polynomial growth, and subgroups carrying the attracting lamination.

title: Extracting human interpretable structure-property relationships in chemistry using XAI and large language models
creator: Geemi P. Wellawatte, Philippe Schwaller
description: Abstract Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) is an emerging field in AI that aims to address the opaque nature of machine learning models. Furthermore, it has been shown that XAI can be used to extract input-output relationships, making them a useful tool in chemistry to understand structure-property relationships.

title: Causal Discovery Under Local Privacy
creator: Ruta Binkyte, Carlos Pinzón, Szilvia Lestyán, Kangsoo Jung, Héber H. Arcolezi, Catuscia Palamidessi
description: Abstract Differential privacy is a widely adopted framework designed to safeguard the sensitive information of data providers within a data set. It is based on the application of controlled noise at the interface between the server that stores and processes the data, and the data consumers.

title: A quantum central path algorithm for linear optimization
creator: Brandon Augustino, Jiaqi Leng, Giacomo Nannicini, Tamás Terlaky, Xiaodi Wu
description: Abstract We propose a novel quantum algorithm for solving linear optimization problems by quantum-mechanical simulation of the central path. While interior point methods follow the central path with an iterative algorithm that works with successive linearizations of the perturbed KKT conditions, we perform a single simulation working directly with the nonlinear complementarity equations.

title: Analyzing Near-Infrared Hyperspectral Imaging for Protein Content Regression and Grain Variety Classification Using Bulk References and Varying Grain-to-Background Ratios
creator: Ole-Christian Galbo Engstrøm, Erik Schou Dreier, Birthe Møller Jespersen, Kim Steenstrup Pedersen
description: Abstract Based on previous work, we assess the use of NIR-HSI images for calibrating models on two datasets, focusing on protein content regression and grain variety classification. Limited reference data for protein content is expanded by subsampling and associating it with the bulk sample.

title: Multivariate quantile-based permutation tests with application to functional data
creator: Zdeněk Hlávka, Daniel Hlubinka, Šárka Hudecová
description: Abstract . Permutation tests enable testing statistical hypotheses in situations when the distribution of the test statistic is complicated or not available. In some situations, the test statistic under investigation is multivariate, with the multiple testing problem being an important example.

title: KPI Extraction from Maintenance Work Orders — A comparison of Expert Labeling, Text Classification and AI-Assisted Tagging for Computing Failure Rates of Wind Turbines
creator: Marc-Alexander Lutz, Bastian Schäfermeier *, Rachael Sexton, Michael Sharp, Alden Dima, Stefan Faulstich, Jagan Mohini Aluri
description: Abstract Maintenance work orders are commonly used to document information about wind turbine operation and maintenance. This includes details about proactive and reactive wind turbine downtimes, such as preventative and corrective maintenance. However, the information contained in maintenance work orders is often unstructured and difficult to analyze, presenting challenges for decision-makers wishing to use it for optimizing operation and maintenance.

title: Distances and isoperimetric inequalities in random triangulations of high genus
creator: Thomas Budzinski, Guillaume Chapuy, Baptiste Louf
description: Abstract We prove that uniform random triangulations whose genus is proportional to their size n n have diameter of order log ⁡ n \log n with high probability. We also show that in such triangulations, the distances between most pairs of points differ by at most an additive constant.

title: Effects of Renormalon Scheme and Perturbative Scale Choices on Determinations of the Strong Coupling from e + ​ e − e^{+}e^{-} Event Shapes Preprint: LA-UR-23-26138 Preprint: SI-HEP-2023-24
creator: Guido Bell, Christopher Lee, Yiannis Makris, Jim Talbert, Bin Yan
description: Abstract We study the role of renormalon cancellation schemes and perturbative scale choices in extractions of the strong coupling constant α s ​ ( m Z ) \alpha_{s}(m_{Z}) and the leading non-perturbative shift parameter Ω 1 \Omega_{1} from resummed predictions of the e + ​ e − e^{+}e^{-} event shape thrust.

title: mmFUSION: Multimodal Fusion for 3D Objects Detection
creator: Javed Ahmad, Alessio Del Bue
description: Abstract Multi-sensor fusion is essential for accurate 3D object detection in self-driving systems. Camera and LiDAR are the most commonly used sensors, and usually, their fusion happens at the early or late stages of 3D detectors with the help of regions of interest (RoIs).

title: Expressivity of ReLU-Networks under Convex Relaxations
creator: Maximilian Baader, Mark Niklas Müller, Yuhao Mao, Martin Vechev
description: Abstract Convex relaxations are a key component of training and certifying provably safe neural networks. However, despite substantial progress, a wide and poorly understood accuracy gap to standard networks remains, raising the question of whether this is due to fundamental limitations of convex relaxations. Initial work investigating this question focused on the simple and widely used IBP relaxation.

title: Neural Appearance Model for Cloth Rendering Volume: 43 Issue: 4
creator: G. Y. Soh and Z. Montazeri University of Manchester, United Kingdom
description: Abstract The realistic rendering of woven and knitted fabrics has posed significant challenges throughout many years. Previously, fiber-based micro-appearance models have achieved considerable success in attaining high levels of realism. However, rendering such models remains complex due to the intricate internal scatterings of hundreds of fibers within a yarn, requiring vast amounts of memory and time to render.

title: Can CLIP Help Sound Source Localization?
creator: Sooyoung Park, Arda Senocak, Joon Son Chung
description: Abstract Large-scale pre-trained image-text models demonstrate remarkable versatility across diverse tasks, benefiting from their robust representational capabilities and effective multimodal alignment. We extend the application of these models, specifically CLIP, to the domain of sound source localization. Unlike conventional approaches, we employ the pre-trained CLIP model without explicit text input, relying solely on the audio-visual correspondence.

title: Discordance Minimization-based Imputation Algorithms for Missing Values in Rating Data
creator: Young Woong Park, Jinhak Kim, Dan Zhu
description: Abstract Ratings are frequently used to evaluate and compare subjects in various applications, from education to healthcare, because ratings provide succinct yet credible measures for comparing subjects. However, when multiple rating lists are combined or considered together, subjects often have missing ratings, because most rating lists do not rate every subject in the combined list.

title: On singular foliations tangent to a given hypersurface
creator: Michael Francis
description: Abstract We consider a class of singular foliations in the sense of Androulidakis and Skandalis that we call transverse order k k foliations. These have a finite number of leaves: one hypersurface (the singular leaf) together with the components of its complement (open leaves).

title: Do LLMs exhibit human-like response biases? A case study in survey design
creator: Lindia Tjuatja, Valerie Chen , Sherry Tongshuang Wu, Ameet Talwalkar, Graham Neubig {lindiat,vchen2,sherryw,atalwalk,gneubig}@andrew.cmu.edu
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Lindia Tjuatja, Valerie Chen , Sherry Tongshuang Wu, Ameet Talwalkar, Graham Neubig {lindiat,vchen2,sherryw,atalwalk,gneubig}@andrew.cmu.edu. As large language models (LLMs) become more capable, there is growing excitement about the possibility of using LLMs as proxies for humans in real-world tasks where subjective labels are desired, such as in surveys and opinion polling.

title: Learning Super-Resolution Ultrasound Localization Microscopy from Radio-Frequency Data Thanks: This work is funded by the Hasler Foundation under project number 22027. ⋆ Corresponding author email: christopher.hahne [ät] unibe.ch
creator: Christopher Hahne ⋆ \star, Georges Chabouh, Olivier Couture, Raphael Sznitman
description: Abstract Ultrasound Localization Microscopy (ULM) enables imaging of vascular structures in the micrometer range by accumulating contrast agent particle locations over time. Precise and efficient target localization accuracy remains an active research topic in the ULM field to further push the boundaries of this promising medical imaging technology.

title: Augmenting Lane Perception and Topology Understanding with Standard Definition Navigation Maps
creator: Katie Z Luo, Xinshuo Weng, Yan Wang, Shuang Wu, Jie Li, Kilian Q Weinberger, Yue Wang, Marco Pavone
description: Abstract Autonomous driving has traditionally relied heavily on costly and labor-intensive High Definition (HD) maps, hindering scalability. In contrast, Standard Definition (SD) maps are more affordable and have worldwide coverage, offering a scalable alternative. In this work, we systematically explore the effect of SD maps for real-time lane-topology understanding.

title: Quantum reaction-limited reaction-diffusion dynamics of noninteracting Bose gases
creator: Shiphrah Rowlands, Igor Lesanovsky, Gabriele Perfetto
description: Abstract We investigate quantum reaction-diffusion systems in one-dimension with bosonic particles that coherently hop in a lattice, and when brought in range react dissipatively. Such reactions involve binary annihilation ( A + A → ∅ A+A\to\emptyset ) and coagulation ( A + A → A A+A\to A ) of particles at distance d d .

creator: E. Masha, L. Barbieri, J. Skowronski, M. Aliotta, C. Ananna, F. Barile, D. Bemmerer, A. Best, A. Boeltzig, C. Broggini, C.G. Bruno, A. Caciolli, M. Campostrini, F. Casaburo, F. Cavanna, G.F. Ciani, A. Ciapponi, P. Colombetti, A. Compagnucci, P. Corvisiero, L. Csedreki, T. Davinson, R. Depalo, A. Di
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by E. Masha, L. Barbieri, J. Skowronski, M. Aliotta, C. Ananna, F. Barile, D. Bemmerer, A. Best, A. Boeltzig, C. Broggini, C.G. Bruno, A. Caciolli, M. Campostrini, F. Casaburo, F. Cavanna, G.F. Ciani, A. Ciapponi, P. Colombetti, A. Compagnucci, P. Corvisiero, L. Csedreki, T. Davinson, R. Depalo, A. Di .

title: Spin-Flavor Oscillations of Relic Neutrinos in Primordial Magnetic Field
creator: Ashutosh Kumar Alok, Trambak Jyoti Chall, Neetu Raj Singh Chundawat, Arindam Mandal
description: Abstract The neutrino magnetic moment operator clasps a tiny but non-zero value within the standard model (SM) of particle physics and rather enhanced values in various new physics models. This generation of the magnetic moment ( μ ν \mu_{\nu} ) is through quantum loop corrections which can exhibit spin-flavor oscillations in the presence of an external magnetic field.

title: Imitation learning for sim-to-real adaptation of robotic cutting policies based on residual Gaussian process disturbance force model
creator: Jamie Hathaway, Rustam Stolkin, Alireza Rastegarpanah
description: Abstract Robotic cutting, a crucial task in applications such as disassembly and decommissioning, faces challenges due to uncertainties in real-world environments. This paper presents a novel approach to enhance sim-to-real transfer of robotic cutting policies, leveraging a hybrid method integrating Gaussian process (GP) regression to model disturbance forces encountered during cutting tasks.

title: Interactive Semantic Map Representation for Skill-based Visual Object Navigation
creator: Tatiana Zemskova, Aleksei Staroverov, Kirill Muravyev, Dmitry Yudin, Aleksandr Panov
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Tatiana Zemskova, Aleksei Staroverov, Kirill Muravyev, Dmitry Yudin, Aleksandr Panov. Visual object navigation using learning methods is one of the key tasks in mobile robotics. This paper introduces a new representation of a scene semantic map formed during the embodied agent interaction with the indoor environment. It is based on a neural network method that adjusts the weights of the segmentation model with backpropagation of the predicted fusion loss values during inference on a regular (backward) or delayed (forward) image sequence.

title: Personality Style Recognition via Machine Learning: Identifying Anaclitic and Introjective Personality Styles from Patients’ Speech
creator: Semere Kiros Bitew \email semerekiros.bitew@ugent.be, Vincent Schelstraete \email vincent@techwolf.be, Klim Zaporojets \email klim.zaporojets@ugent.be, Kimberly Van Nieuwenhove \email kimberly.vannieuwenhove@ugent.be, Reitske Meganck \email reitske.meganck@ugent.be, Chris Develder \email chris.devel
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Semere Kiros Bitew \email semerekiros.bitew@ugent.be, Vincent Schelstraete \email vincent@techwolf.be, Klim Zaporojets \email klim.zaporojets@ugent.be, Kimberly Van Nieuwenhove \email kimberly.vannieuwenhove@ugent.be, Reitske Meganck \email reitske.meganck@ugent.be, Chris Develder \email chris.devel. In disentangling the heterogeneity observed in psychopathology, personality of the patients is considered crucial.

title: Holographic renormalization of Horndeski gravity
creator: Nicolás Cáceres, Cristóbal Corral, Felipe Díaz, Rodrigo Olea
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Nicolás Cáceres, Cristóbal Corral, Felipe Díaz, Rodrigo Olea. We study the renormalization of a particular sector of Horndeski theory. In particular, we focus on the nonminimal coupling of a scalar field to the Gauss-Bonnet term and its kinetic coupling to the Einstein tensor. Adopting a power expansion on the scalar function that couples the Gauss-Bonnet term, we find specific conditions on their coefficients such that the action and charges are finite. To accomplish the latter, we add a finite set of intrinsic boundary terms.

title: Revisiting Loop Corrections in Single Field USR Inflation
description: Abstract We revisit the one-loop corrections on CMB scale perturbations induced from small scale modes in single field models which undergo a phase of ultra slow-roll inflation. There were concerns that large loop corrections are against the notion of the decoupling of scales and they are cancelled out once the boundary terms are included in Hamiltonian.

title: Stable partitions for proportional generalized claims problems Thanks: We gratefully acknowledge financial support from the Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF) through Project 100018 _ \_ 192583. Oihane Gallo gratefully acknowledges additional financial support from the Spanish Government throu
creator: Oihane Gallo, Bettina Klaus
description: Abstract We consider a set of agents who have claims on an endowment that is not large enough to cover all claims. Agents can form coalitions but a minimal coalition size θ \theta is required to have positive coalitional funding that is proportional to the sum of the claims of its members.

title: On the Post-Lie Structure in SISO Affine Feedback Control Systems
creator: Kurusch Ebrahimi-Fard, W. Steven Gray, Venkatesh G. S
description: Abstract . The main objective of this work is to show that the single-input, single-output (SISO) affine feedback group, a transformation group in the context of the affine feedback interconnection of Chen–Fliess series, is a post-group in the sense of Bai, Guo, Sheng and Tang. 1.

title: Ramsey Quantifiers in Linear Arithmetics CCS: Theory of computation Logic and verification CCS: Theory of computation Automated reasoning CCS: Theory of computation Program verification CCS: Theory of computation Complexity classes CCS: Theory of computation Verification by model checking CCS: Theor
creator: Pascal Bergsträßer, Moses Ganardi, Anthony W. Lin, Georg Zetzsche
description: Abstract . We study Satisfiability Modulo Theories (SMT) enriched with the so-called Ramsey quantifiers, which assert the existence of cliques (complete graphs) in the graph induced by some formulas. The extended framework is known to have applications in proving program termination (in particular, whether a transitive binary predicate is well-founded), and monadic decomposability of SMT formulas.

title: Carroll geodesics
creator: Luca Ciambelli, Daniel Grumiller
description: Abstract Using effective field theory methods, we derive the Carrollian analog of the geodesic action. We find that it contains both “electric” and “magnetic” contributions that are in general coupled to each other. The equations of motion descending from this action are the Carrollian pendant of geodesics, allowing surprisingly rich dynamics.

title: Exact fluctuation and long-range correlations in a single-file model under resetting
creator: Saikat Santra 1 and Prashant Singh 2
description: Abstract Resetting is a renewal mechanism in which a process is intermittently repeated after a random or fixed time. This simple act of stop and repeat profoundly influences the behaviour of a system as exemplified by the emergence of non-equilibrium properties and expedition of search processes.

title: Unveiling Safety Vulnerabilities of Large Language Models
creator: George Kour, Marcel Zalmanovici, Naama Zwerdling, Esther Goldbraich
description: Abstract As large language models become more prevalent, their possible harmful or inappropriate responses are a cause for concern. This paper introduces a unique dataset containing adversarial examples in the form of questions, we call AttaQ , designed to provoke such harmful or inappropriate responses.

title: On finite permutation groups of rank three
creator: Hong Yi Huang, Cai Heng Li, Yan Zhou Zhu
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Hong Yi Huang, Cai Heng Li, Yan Zhou Zhu. The classification of the finite primitive permutation groups of rank 3 3 was completed in the 1980s and this landmark achievement has found a wide range of applications. In the general transitive setting, a classical result of Higman shows that every finite imprimitive rank 3 3 permutation group G G has a unique non-trivial block system ℬ \mathcal{B} and this provides a natural way to partition the analysis of these groups.

title: Dynamics of Carrollian Scalar Fields
creator: Luca Ciambelli
description: Abstract Adopting an intrinsic Carrollian viewpoint, we show that the generic Carrollian scalar field action is a combination of electric and magnetic actions, found in the literature by taking the Carrollian limit of the relativistic scalar field. This leads to non-trivial dynamics: even a single particle with non-vanishing energy can move in Carrollian physics.

title: Observation of the distribution of nuclear magnetization in a molecule
creator: S. G. Wilkins 1,∗,† , S. M. Udrescu 1,∗,‡ , M. Athanasakis-Kaklamanakis 2,3 , R. F. Garcia Ruiz 1,§ , M. Au 4,5 , I. Belos̆ević 6 , R. Berger 7 , M. L. Bissell 8 , A. A. Breier 9 , A. J. Brinson 1 , K. Chrysalidis 4 , T. E. Cocolios 3 , R. P. de Groote 3 , A. Dorne 3 , K. T. Flanagan 8,10 , S. Franc
description: Abstract Rapid progress in the experimental control and interrogation of molecules, combined with developments in precise calculations of their structure, are enabling new opportunities in the investigation of nuclear and particle physics phenomena. Molecules containing heavy, octupole-deformed nuclei such as radium are of particular interest for such studies, offering an enhanced sensitivity to the properties of fundamental particles and interactions.

title: A study of the One-Dimensional Heat-Conduction Equation with Radiation
creator: Mihai Halic
description: Abstract . We consider a boundary value problem (BVP) modelling one-dimensional heat-conduction with radiation, which is derived from the Stefan-Boltzmann law. The problem strongly depends on the parameters, making difficult to estimate the solution. In here we apply an analytical approach to determine upper and lower bounds to the exact solution of the BVP, which allows estimating the latter.

title: Dynamics and Scaling of Internally Cooled Convection Journal: Communications in Nonlinear Science and Numerical Simulation
creator: Lokahith Agasthya, Caroline Jane Muller
description: Abstract Our goal is to investigate fundamental properties of the system of internally cooled convection. The system consists of an upward thermal flux at the lower boundary, a mean temperature lapse-rate and a constant cooling term in the bulk with the bulk cooling in thermal equilibrium with the input heat flux.

title: SPIRAL: An Efficient Algorithm for the Integration of the Equation of Rotational Motion Journal: the Journal of Computational Physics
creator: Carlos Andrés del Valle, Vasileios Angelidakis, Sudeshna Roy, José Daniel Muñoz, Thorsten Pöschel
description: Abstract We introduce Spiral , a third-order integration algorithm for the rotational motion of extended bodies. It requires only one force calculation per time step, does not require quaternion normalization at each time step, and can be formulated for both leapfrog and synchronous integration schemes, making it compatible with many particle simulation codes.

title: A Categorical Model for Retrosynthetic Reaction Analysis
creator: Ella Gale, Leo Lobski, Fabio Zanasi
description: Abstract We introduce a mathematical framework for retrosynthetic analysis, an important research method in synthetic chemistry. Our approach represents molecules and their interaction using string diagrams in layered props – a recently introduced categorical model for partial explanations in scientific reasoning.

title: Search for a CP-odd Higgs boson decaying into a heavy CP-even Higgs boson and a Z Z boson in the ℓ + ​ ℓ − ​ t ​ t ¯ \ell^{+}\ell^{-}t\bar{t} and ν ​ ν ¯ ​ b ​ b ¯ \nu\bar{\nu}b\bar{b} final states using 140 fb -1 of data collected with the ATLAS detector
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by . A search for a heavy CP-odd Higgs boson, A A , decaying into a Z Z boson and a heavy CP-even Higgs boson, H H , is presented. It uses the full LHC Run 2 dataset of p ​ p pp collisions at s = 13 \sqrt{s}=13 TeV collected with the ATLAS detector, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 140 140 fb -1 .

title: Computability in Dynamical Systems Thanks: Burr was partially supported by grants from the National Science Foundation (CCF-1527193 and DMS-1913119). Thanks: Wolf was partially supported by grants from the Simons Foundation (#637594 to Christian Wolf) and PSC-CUNY (TRADB-51-63715 to Christian Wolf).
creator: Michael Burr, Christian Wolf
description: Abstract . In this paper we present an introduction to the area of computability in dynamical systems. This is a fairly new field which has received quite some attention in recent years. One of the central questions in this area is if relevant dynamical objects can be algorithmically presented by a Turing machine.

title: Towards Interpretable Sequence Continuation: Analyzing Shared Circuits in Large Language Models
creator: Michael Lan, Philip Torr, Fazl Barez
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Michael Lan, Philip Torr, Fazl Barez. While transformer models exhibit strong capabilities on linguistic tasks, their complex architectures make them difficult to interpret. Recent work has aimed to reverse engineer transformer models into human-readable representations called circuits that implement algorithmic functions. We extend this research by analyzing and comparing circuits for similar sequence continuation tasks, which include increasing sequences of Arabic numerals , number words , and months .

title: Enhanced power spectra from multi-field inflation
creator: Jinn-Ouk Gong
description: Abstract We investigate the enhancement of the power spectra large enough to produce primordial black holes in models with multiple scalar fields. We present analytic solutions for the perturbations in the case of constant turns without the need for an effective field theory for the first time and clarify the role of the Hubble friction that has been overlooked previously.

title: Benchmarking a Neutral-Atom Quantum Computer
creator: N. Wagner, C. Poole, T. M. Graham, M. Saffman
description: Abstract In this study, we simulated the algorithmic performance of a small neutral atom quantum computer and compared its performance when operating with all-to-all versus nearest-neighbor connectivity. This comparison was made using a suite of algorithmic benchmarks developed by the Quantum Economic Development Consortium.

title: Contactless Fingerprint Biometric Anti-Spoofing: An Unsupervised Deep Learning Approach
creator: Banafsheh Adami, Nima Karimian
description: Abstract Contactless fingerprint recognition offers a higher level of user comfort and addresses hygiene concerns more effectively. However, it is also more vulnerable to presentation attacks such as photo paper, paper-printout, and various display attacks, which makes it more challenging to implement in biometric systems compared to contact-based modalities.

title: Galaxy Spectra neural Network (GaSNet). II. Using Deep Learning for Spectral Classification and Redshift Predictions 2023 Galaxy Spectra neural Network (GaSNet). II. Using Deep Learning for Spectral Classification and Redshift Predictions – 31
creator: Fucheng Zhong, Nicola R. Napolitano, Caroline Heneka, Rui Li, Franz Erik Bauer, Nicolas Bouche, Johan Comparat, Young-Lo Kim, Jens-Kristian Krogager, Marcella Longhetti, Jonathan Loveday, Boudewijn F. Roukema, Benedict L. Rouse, Mara Salvato, Crescenzo Tortora, Roberto J. Assef, Letizia P. Cassarà,
description: Abstract The size and complexity reached by the large sky spectroscopic surveys require efficient, accurate, and flexible automated tools for data analysis and science exploitation. We present the Galaxy Spectra Network/GaSNet-II, a supervised multi-network deep learning tool for spectra classification and redshift prediction. GaSNet-II can be trained to identify a customized number of classes and optimize the redshift predictions.

title: Purcell modified Doppler cooling of quantum emitters inside optical cavities
creator: J. Lyne, N. S. Bassler, S. Park, G. Pupillo, C. Genes
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by J. Lyne, N. S. Bassler, S. Park, G. Pupillo, C. Genes. Standard cavity cooling of atoms or dielectric particles is based on the action of dispersive optical forces in high-finesse cavities. We investigate here a complementary regime characterized by large cavity losses, resembling the standard Doppler cooling technique. For a single two-level emitter a modification of the cooling rate is obtained from the Purcell enhancement of spontaneous emission in the large cooperativity limit.

title: Time-Efficient Reinforcement Learning with Stochastic Stateful Policies
creator: Firas Al-Hafez, Guoping Zhao, Jan Peters, Davide Tateo
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Firas Al-Hafez, Guoping Zhao, Jan Peters, Davide Tateo. Stateful policies play an important role in reinforcement learning, such as handling partially observable environments, enhancing robustness, or imposing an inductive bias directly into the policy structure. The conventional method for training stateful policies is Backpropagation Through Time (BPTT) , which comes with significant drawbacks, such as slow training due to sequential gradient propagation and the occurrence of vanishing or exploding gradients.

title: High-fidelity 3D Reconstruction of Plants using Neural Radiance Field
creator: Kewei Hu, Ying Wei, Yaoqiang Pan, Hanwen Kang, Chao Chen
description: Abstract Accurate reconstruction of plant phenotypes plays a key role in optimising sustainable farming practices in the field of Precision Agriculture (PA). Currently, optical sensor-based approaches dominate the field, but the need for high-fidelity 3D reconstruction of crops and plants in unstructured agricultural environments remains challenging.

title: Enhancing LLM Intelligence with ARM-RAG: Auxiliary Rationale Memory for Retrieval Augmented Generation
creator: Eric Melz
description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) are smart but forgetful. Recent studies, (e.g., Bubeck et al. 2023 ) on modern LLMs have shown that they are capable of performing amazing tasks typically necessitating human-level intelligence. However, unlike humans, frozen LLMs do not improve over time; they neither acquire new knowledge nor learn from their successes or failures.

title: Black-Box Prompt Optimization: Aligning Large Language Models without Model Training
creator: Jiale Cheng, Xiao Liu, Kehan Zheng, Pei Ke, Hongning Wang , Yuxiao Dong , Jie Tang , Minlie Huang
description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) have shown impressive success in various applications. However, these models are often not well aligned with human intents, which calls for additional treatments on them; that is, the alignment problem. To make LLMs better follow user instructions, existing alignment methods primarily focus on further training them.

title: Characterization of Singular Arcs in Spacecraft Trajectory Optimization
creator: Andrea C. Morelli, Carmine Giordano, Riccardo Bonalli , and Francesco Topputo
description: Abstract Low-thrust engines for interplanetary spacecraft transfers allow cost-effective space missions with flexible launch and arrival dates. To find fuel-optimal trajectories, an optimal control problem is to be solved. Pontryagin’s Maximum Principle shows that the structure of the optimal control is bang-bang with the possibility of singular arcs.

title: Physics PhD student perspectives on the importance and difficulty of finding a research group
creator: Mike Verostek, Casey W. Miller, Benjamin M. Zwickl
description: Abstract Joining a research group is one of the most important events on a graduate student’s path to becoming an independent physics researcher and earning a PhD. However, graduate students’ perspectives on the experience of finding a research group are not well-documented in the literature.

title: The early evolution of young massive clusters
creator: M. Stoop, A. Derkink, L. Kaper, A. de Koter, C. Rogers, M. C. Ramírez-Tannus, D. Guo, N. Azatyan
description: Abstract Context. Characterising the outcome of the star formation process is key to understand and predict the evolution of stellar populations. Especially the fraction of massive stars in young stellar clusters is of importance as they are the dominant sources of both mechanical and radiative feedback, strongly influencing the thermal and dynamical state of their birth environments, and beyond.

title: The role of sign indefinite invariants in shaping turbulent cascades
creator: Michal Shavit, Oliver Bühler and Jalal Shatah
description: Abstract We highlight a non-canonical yet natural choice of variables for an efficient derivation of a kinetic equation for the energy density in non-isotropic systems, including internal gravity waves on a vertical plane, inertial and Rossby waves. The existence of a second quadratic invariant simplifies the kinetic equation and leads to extra conservation laws for resonant interactions.

title: Random Natural Gradient
creator: Ioannis Kolotouros, Petros Wallden
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Ioannis Kolotouros, Petros Wallden. Hybrid quantum-classical algorithms appear to be the most promising approach for near-term quantum applications. An important bottleneck is the classical optimization loop, where the multiple local minima and the emergence of barren plateaux make these approaches less appealing. To improve the optimization, the Quantum Natural Gradient (QNG) method [Quantum 4, 269 (2020)] was introduced – a method that uses information about the local geometry of the quantum state-space.

title: Laser-driven ion and electron acceleration from near-critical density gas targets: towards high-repetition rate operation in the 1 PW, sub-100 fs laser interaction regime
creator: V. Ospina-Bohórquez, C. Salgado-López, M. Ehret, S. Malko, M. Salvadori, T. Pisarczyk, T. Chodukowski, Z. Rusiniak, M. Krupka, P. Guillon, M. Lendrin, G. Pérez-Callejo, C. Vlachos, F. Hannachi, M. Tarisien, F. Consoli, C. Verona, G. Prestopino, J. Dostal, R. Dudzak, J. L. Henares, J. I. Apiñaniz, D.
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by V. Ospina-Bohórquez, C. Salgado-López, M. Ehret, S. Malko, M. Salvadori, T. Pisarczyk, T. Chodukowski, Z. Rusiniak, M. Krupka, P. Guillon, M. Lendrin, G. Pérez-Callejo, C. Vlachos, F. Hannachi, M. Tarisien, F. Consoli, C. Verona, G. Prestopino, J. Dostal, R. Dudzak, J. L. Henares, J. I. Apiñaniz, D.. Ion acceleration from gaseous targets driven by relativistic-intensity lasers was demonstrated as early as the late 90s, yet most of the experiments conducted to date have involved picosecond-duration, Nd:glass lasers operating at low repetition rate.

title: Fate of Chiral Symmetries in the Quark-Gluon Plasma from an Instanton-Based Random Matrix Model of QCD
creator: Tamás G. Kovács
description: Abstract We propose a new way of understanding how chiral symmetry is realized in the high temperature phase of QCD. Based on the finding that a simple free instanton gas precisely describes the details of the lowest part of the spectrum of the lattice overlap Dirac operator, we propose an instanton-based random matrix model of QCD with dynamical quarks.

description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Franz Lehner, Kamil Szpojankowski. title: Multi-band description of the upper critical field of bulk FeSe
creator: M. Bristow, A. Gower, J. C. A. Prentice, M. D. Watson, Z. Zajicek, S. J. Blundell, A. A. Haghighirad, A. McCollam, A. I. Coldea
description: Abstract The upper critical field of multi-band superconductors can be an essential quantity to unravel the nature of superconducting pairing and its interplay with the electronic structure. Here we experimentally map out the complete upper critical field phase diagram of FeSe for different magnetic field orientations at temperatures down to 0.3 0.3\, K using both resistivity and torque measurements.

title: Resource analysis of quantum algorithms for coarse-grained protein folding models
creator: Hanna Linn, Isak Brundin, Laura García-Álvarez, Göran Johansson
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Hanna Linn, Isak Brundin, Laura García-Álvarez, Göran Johansson. Protein folding processes are a vital aspect of molecular biology that is hard to simulate with conventional computers. Quantum algorithms have been proven superior for certain problems and may help tackle this complex life science challenge. We analyze the resource requirements for simulating protein folding on a quantum computer, assessing this problem’s feasibility in the current and near-future technological landscape.

title: A Bayesian Approach for Simultaneously Radial Kernel Parameter Tuning in the Partition of Unity Method
creator: Roberto Cavoretto, Alessandra De Rossi, Sandro Lancellotti, Federico Romaniello
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Roberto Cavoretto, Alessandra De Rossi, Sandro Lancellotti, Federico Romaniello. In this paper, Bayesian optimisation is used to simultaneously search the optimal values of the shape parameter and the radius in radial basis function partition of unity interpolation problem.

title: q q -Independence of the C ∗ C^{*} -algebra of ”Continuous Functions” on a Quantum 2 × 2 2\times 2 -Matrix Ball
creator: Olof Giselsson
description: Abstract For 0 < q < 1 , 0<q<1, let Pol ​ ( Mat 2 ) q \mathrm{Pol}(\mathrm{Mat}_{2})_{q} be the q q -analogue of regular functions on the open matrix ball of 2 × 2 2\times 2 -matrices introduced by L. Vaksman.

title: Harnessing excitons at the nanoscale - photoelectrical platform for quantitative sensing and imaging
creator: Zhurun Ji, Mark E. Barber, Ziyan Zhu, Carlos R. Kometter, Jiachen Yu, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Mengkun Liu, Thomas P. Devereaux, Benjamin E. Feldman, Zhixun Shen
description: Abstract Excitons — quasiparticles formed by the binding of an electron and a hole through electrostatic attraction — hold promise in the fields of quantum light confinement and optoelectronic sensing. Atomically thin transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) provide a versatile platform for hosting and manipulating excitons, given their robust Coulomb interactions and exceptional sensitivity to dielectric environments.

title: Minimal triangulations of circle bundles
creator: Gaiane Panina, Maksim Turevskii
description: Abstract . A triangulation of a circle bundle E → 𝜋 B E\xrightarrow[\text{}]{\pi}B is a triangulation of the total space E E and the base B B such that the projection π \pi is a simplicial map. In the paper we address the following questions: Which circle bundles can be triangulated over a given triangulation of the base?

title: Software Architecture Challenges in Integrating Hybrid Classical-Quantum Systems
creator: Vlad Stirbu, Tommi Mikkonen
description: Abstract The emergence of quantum computing proposes a revolutionary paradigm that can radically transform numerous scientific and industrial application domains. The ability of quantum computers to scale computations exponentially imply better performance and efficiency for certain algorithmic tasks than current computers provide.

title: Polyregular functions on unordered trees of bounded height Conference: …; …; … CCS: Theory of computation Transducers CCS: Theory of computation Tree languages CCS: Theory of computation Logic
creator: Mikołaj Bojańczyk, Bartek Klin
description: Abstract . We consider injective first-order interpretations that input and output trees of bounded height. The corresponding functions have polynomial output size, since a first-order interpretation can use a k k -tuple of input nodes to represent a single output node. We prove that the equivalence problem for such functions is decidable, i.e.

title: Spatio-Temporal Anomaly Detection with Graph Networks for Data Quality Monitoring of the Hadron Calorimeter
creator: Mulugeta Weldezgina Asres, Christian Walter Omlin, Long Wang, David Yu, Pavel Parygin, Jay Dittmann, Georgia Karapostoli, Markus Seidel, Rosamaria Venditti, Luka Lambrecht, Emanuele Usai, Muhammad Ahmad, Javier Fernandez Menendez, Kaori Maeshima, The CMS-HCAL Collaboration
description: Abstract The compact muon solenoid (CMS) experiment is a general-purpose detector for high-energy collision at the large hadron collider (LHC) at CERN. It employs an online data quality monitoring (DQM) system to promptly spot and diagnose particle data acquisition problems to avoid data quality loss.

title: Solvable Polynomial Ideals: The Ideal Reflection for Program Analysis CCS: Theory of computation Logic and verification CCS: Theory of computation Automated reasoning CCS: Theory of computation Abstraction CCS: Mathematics of computing Gröbner bases and other special bases
creator: John Cyphert, Zachary Kincaid
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by John Cyphert, Zachary Kincaid. This paper presents a program analysis method that generates program summaries involving polynomial arithmetic. Our approach builds on prior techniques that use solvable polynomial maps for summarizing loops. These techniques are able to generate all polynomial invariants for a restricted class of programs, but cannot be applied to programs outside of this class—for instance, programs with nested loops, conditional branching, unstructured control flow, etc. There currently lacks approaches to apply these prior methods to the case of general programs.

title: Wearable data from subjects playing Super Mario, sitting university exams, or performing physical exercise help detect acute mood episodes via self-supervised learning
creator: Filippo Corponi, Bryan M. Li, Gerard Anmella, Clàudia Valenzuela-Pascual, [0.5mm] Ariadna Mas Isabella Pacchiarotti Marc Valentí Iria Grande, [0.5mm] Antonio Benabarre Marina Garriga Eduard Vieta Allan H Young, [0.5mm] Stephen M. Lawrie Heather C. Whalley Diego Hidalgo-Mazzei Antonio Vergari, [2mm]
description: Abstract Personal sensing, leveraging data passively and near-continuously collected with wearables from patients in their ecological environment, is a promising paradigm to monitor mood disorders (MDs), a major determinant of worldwide disease burden. However, collecting and annotating wearable data is very resource-intensive. Studies of this kind can thus typically afford to recruit only a couple dozens of patients.

[ 2 ] . A brief discussion of the earlier proposed “solutions” of the flavour problem and their drawbacks is given, e.g.

title: MELEP: A Novel Predictive Measure of Transferability in Multi-Label ECG Diagnosis
creator: Cuong V. Nguyen, Hieu Minh Duong, Cuong D. Do
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Cuong V. Nguyen, Hieu Minh Duong, Cuong D. Do. In practical electrocardiography (ECG) interpretation, the scarcity of well-annotated data is a common challenge. Transfer learning techniques are valuable in such situations, yet the assessment of transferability has received limited attention. To tackle this issue, we introduce MELEP, which stands for Muti-label Expected Log of Empirical Predictions , a measure designed to estimate the effectiveness of knowledge transfer from a pre-trained model to a downstream multi-label ECG diagnosis task.

title: Elliptic units for complex cubic fields (On Eisenstein’s Jugendtraum)
creator: Nicolas Bergeron, Pierre Charollois, Luis E. García
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Nicolas Bergeron, Pierre Charollois, Luis E. García. We propose a conjecture extending the classical construction of elliptic units to complex cubic number fields K \displaystyle K . The conjecture concerns special values of the elliptic gamma function, a holomorphic function of three complex variables arising in mathematical physics whose transformation properties under SL 3 ​ ( 𝐙 ) \displaystyle\mathrm{SL}_{3}(\mathbf{Z}) were studied by Felder and Varchenko in the early 2000s.

title: Exploring Best Practices for ECG Pre-Processing in Machine Learning
creator: Amir Salimi 1 , Sunil Vasu Kalmady 2 , Abram Hindle. 1,2 , Osmar Zaiane, Padma Kaul
description: Abstract In this work we search for best practices in pre-processing of Electrocardiogram (ECG) signals in order to train better classifiers for the diagnosis of heart conditions. State of the art machine learning algorithms have achieved remarkable results in classification of some heart conditions using ECG data, yet there appears to be no consensus on pre-processing best practices.

title: Fractional quantum anomalous Hall effects in rhombohedral multilayer graphene in the moiréless limit
creator: Boran Zhou, Hui Yang, Ya-Hui Zhang
description: Abstract The standard theoretical framework for fractional quantum anomalous Hall effect (FQAH) assumes an isolated flat Chern band in the single particle level. In this paper we challenges this paradigm for the FQAH recently observed in the pentalayer rhombohedral stacked graphene aligned with hexagon boron nitride (hBN).

title: Distributed Agent-Based Collaborative Learning in Cross-Individual Wearable Sensor-Based Human Activity Recognition
creator: Ahmad Esmaeili, Zahra Ghorrati, Eric T. Matson
description: Abstract The rapid growth of wearable sensor technologies holds substantial promise for the field of personalized and context-aware Human Activity Recognition. Given the inherently decentralized nature of data sources within this domain, the utilization of multi-agent systems with their inherent decentralization capabilities presents an opportunity to facilitate the development of scalable, adaptable, and privacy-conscious methodologies.

title: Island myriads in periodic potentials
creator: Matheus J. Lazarotto, Iberê L. Caldas, Yves Elskens
description: Abstract A phenomenon of emergence of stability islands in phase-space is reported for two periodic potentials with tiling symmetries, one square and the other hexagonal, inspired by bidimensional Hamiltonian models of optical lattices. The structures found, here termed as island myriads, resemble web-tori with notable fractality and arise at energy levels reaching that of unstable equilibria.

title: A Modulation-Format Dependent Closed-form Expression for the Gaussian Noise Model in the Presence of Raman Amplification
creator: H. Buglia (1), M. Jarmolovičius (1), L. Galdino (2), R.I. Killey (1), and P. Bayvel (1)
description: Abstract 1 Introduction Raman amplification (RA) has attracted considerable attention in recent years because of its potential to achieve increased data rates in optical fibre transmission systems [ 1 ] . For ultra-wideband (UWB) systems, this technique can be used in combination with lumped amplification (e.g.

title: DDPET-3D: Dose-aware Diffusion Model for 3D Ultra Low-dose PET Imaging
creator: Huidong XieYale University huidong.xie@yale.edu, Weijie GanWashington University in St. Louis weijie.gan@wustl.edu Bo ZhouYale University bo.zhou@yale.edu Xiongchao ChenYale University xiongchao.chen@yale.edu Qiong LiuYale University qiong.liu@yale.edu Xueqi GuoYale University xueqi.guo@yale.edu Lia
description: Abstract As PET imaging is accompanied by substantial radiation exposure and cancer risk, reducing radiation dose in PET scans is an important topic. Recently, diffusion models have emerged as the new state-of-the-art generative model to generate high-quality samples and have demonstrated strong potential for various tasks in medical imaging.

title: Environmental-Impact Based Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
creator: Farinaz Alamiyan-Harandi, Pouria Ramazi
description: Abstract To promote cooperation and strengthen the individual impact on the collective outcome in social dilemmas, we propose the Environmental-impact Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (EMuReL) method where each agent estimates the “environmental impact” of every other agent, that is, the difference in the current environment state compared to the hypothetical environment in the absence of that other agent.

title: Stringlet Excitation Model of the Boson Peak
creator: Cunyuan Jiang, Matteo Baggioli, Jack F. Douglas
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Cunyuan Jiang, Matteo Baggioli, Jack F. Douglas. The boson peak (BP), a low-energy excess in the vibrational density of states over the Debye contribution, is often identified as a characteristic of amorphous solid materials. Despite decades of efforts, its microscopic origin still remains a mystery. Recently, it has been proposed, and corroborated with simulations, that the BP might stem from intrinsic localized modes involving one-dimensional (1D) string-like excitations (“stringlets”).

title: Can LLMs Follow Simple Rules?
creator: Norman Mu, Sarah Chen, Zifan Wang, Sizhe Chen, David Karamardian, Lulwa Aljeraisy, Dan Hendrycks, David Wagner
description: Abstract As Large Language Models (LLMs) are deployed with increasing real-world responsibilities, it is important to be able to specify and constrain the behavior of these systems in a reliable manner. Model developers may wish to set explicit rules for the model, such as “do not generate abusive content”, but these may be circumvented by jailbreaking techniques.

title: Computing Approximate ℓ p \ell_{p} Sensitivities Thanks: Authors listed alphabetically. A preliminary version of this paper was first published in NeurIPS 2023.
creator: Swati Padmanabhan, David P. Woodruff, Qiuyi (Richard) Zhang
description: Abstract Recent works in dimensionality reduction for regression tasks have introduced the notion of sensitivity, an estimate of the importance of a specific datapoint in a dataset, offering provable guarantees on the quality of the approximation after removing low-sensitivity datapoints via subsampling.

title: Kindness in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
creator: Farinaz Alamiyan-Harandi, Mersad Hassanjani, Pouria Ramazi
description: Abstract In human societies, people often incorporate fairness in their decisions and treat reciprocally by being kind to those who act kindly. They evaluate the kindness of others’ actions not only by monitoring the outcomes but also by considering the intentions. This behavioral concept can be adapted to train cooperative agents in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL).

title: Deep Hashing via Householder Quantization
creator: Lucas R. Schwengber, Lucas Resende †, Paulo Orenstein, Roberto I. Oliveira
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Lucas R. Schwengber, Lucas Resende †, Paulo Orenstein, Roberto I. Oliveira. Hashing is at the heart of large-scale image similarity search, and recent methods have been substantially improved through deep learning techniques. Such algorithms typically learn continuous embeddings of the data.

title: Centralizers of non-elliptic univalent self-maps and the embeddability problem in the unit disc Thanks: This research was supported in part by Ministerio de Innovación y Ciencia, Spain, project PID2022-136320NB-I00, and Junta de Andalucía, project P20_00664.
creator: Manuel D. Contreras †, Santiago Díaz-Madrigal †, Pavel Gumenyuk ‡
description: Abstract . The embeddability problem is a very old and hard problem in discrete holomorphic iteration which deals with determining general conditions on a given univalent self-map φ \varphi of the unit disc 𝔻 \mathbb{D} in order to be contained in a continuous one-parameter semigroup.

title: Reentrant supersolidity
creator: Leo Radzihovsky
description: Abstract A “supersolid” – a crystal that exhibits an off-diagonal long-range order and a superflow – has been a subject of much research since its first proposal AndreevLifshitz69 , but has not been realized as a ground state of short-range interacting bosons in a continuum.

title: Localised Gravity and Resolved Braneworlds
creator: Rahim Leung
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Rahim Leung. Deriving an effective massless field theory for fluctuations about a braneworld spacetime requires analysis of the transverse-space-wavefunction’s second-order differential equation. There can be two strikingly different types of effective theory. For a supersymmetric braneworld, one involves a technically consistent embedding of a supergravity theory on the worldvolume; the other can produce, in certain situations, a genuine localisation of gravity near the worldvolume but not via a technically consistent embedding.

title: mPLUG-Owl2: Revolutionizing Multi-modal Large Language Model with Modality Collaboration
creator: Qinghao Ye Haiyang Xu Jiabo Ye Ming Yan Anwen Hu
description: Abstract Multi-modal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have demonstrated impressive instruction abilities across various open-ended tasks. However, previous methods primarily focus on enhancing multi-modal capabilities. In this work, we introduce a versatile multi-modal large language model, mPLUG-Owl2, which effectively leverages modality collaboration to improve performance in both text and multi-modal tasks.

title: Stochastic quantization of two-dimensional P ⁡ ( Φ ) P(\Phi) Quantum Field Theory
creator: Paweł Duch, Wojciech Dybalski, Azam Jahandideh
description: Abstract We give a simple and self-contained construction of of the P ⁡ ( Φ ) P(\Phi) Euclidean Quantum Field Theory in the plane and verify the Osterwalder-Schrader axioms: translational and rotational invariance, reflection positivity and regularity. In the intermediate steps of the construction we study measures on spheres.

title: A Milky Way-like barred spiral galaxy at a redshift of 3
creator: Luca Costantin, Pablo G. Pérez-González, Yuchen Guo, Chiara Buttitta, Shardha Jogee, Micaela B. Bagley, Guillermo Barro, Jeyhan S. Kartaltepe, Anton M.
