description: Abstract Although it’s widely believed that gravity should have a quantum nature like every other force, the conceptual obstacles to constructing a quantum theory of gravity compel us to explore other perspectives. Gravity is not like any other force. It alone defines a universal space-time geometry, upon which quantum fields evolve. We feel gravity because matter causes space-time to bend.

title: Probing the Galactic Diffuse Continuum Emission with COSI
creator: Christopher M. Karwin, Thomas Siegert, Jacqueline Beechert, John A. Tomsick, Troy A. Porter, Michela Negro, Carolyn Kierans, Marco Ajello, Israel Martinez Castellanos, Albert Shih, Andreas Zoglauer, Steven E. Boggs
description: Abstract In 2016 the Compton Spectrometer and Imager (COSI) had a successful 46-day flight onboard NASA’s Super Pressure Balloon platform. In this work we report measurements of the Galactic diffuse continuum emission (GDCE) observed towards the inner Galaxy during the flight, which in the COSI energy band ( 0.2 − 5 0.2-5 MeV) is primarily generated from inverse Compton radiation.

title: Theory of moiré magnetism in twisted bilayer α \alpha -RuCl 3
creator: Muhammad Akram, Jesse Kapeghian, Jyotirish Das, Roser Valentí, Antia S. Botana, Onur Erten
description: Abstract Twisted heterostructures of van der Waals materials have received much attention for their many remarkable properties. Here, we present a comprehensive theory of the long-range ordered magnetic phases of twisted bilayer α \alpha -RuCl 3 via a combination of first-principles calculations and atomistic simulations.

title: Fast Parameter Inference on Pulsar Timing Arrays with Normalizing Flows
creator: David Shih, Marat Freytsis, Stephen R. Taylor, Jeff A. Dror, Nolan Smyth
description: Abstract Pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) perform Bayesian posterior inference with expensive MCMC methods. Given a dataset of ∼ 10 ​ – ​ 100 \sim 10\text{--}100 pulsars and 𝒪 ⁡ ( 10 3 ) {\mathcal{O}}(10^{3}) timing residuals each, producing a posterior distribution for the stochastic gravitational wave background (SGWB) can take days to a week.

title: Fermi-Bose crossover using engineered disorder potential
creator: Madhuparna Karmakar, Rajesh Narayanan
description: Abstract We present the first instance of a disorder tuned Fermi-Bose crossover that could be realized in superconducting systems. More specifically, harnessing a non perturbative numerical technique we analyze the ground state behavior of a two-dimensional attractive Hubbard model subjected to spin selective disorder potential.

title: Amplification of electromagnetic waves by a rotating body
creator: M.C. Braidotti, A. Vinante, M. Cromb, A. Sandakumar, D. Faccio, H. Ulbricht
description: Abstract In 1971, Zel’dovich predicted the amplification of electromagnetic (EM) waves scattered by a rotating metallic cylinder, gaining mechanical rotational energy from the body.Since then, this phenomenon has been believed to be unobservable with electromagnetic fields due to technological difficulties in meeting the condition of amplification, that is, the cylinder must rotate faster than the frequency of the incoming radiation.

title: Solution to the conflict between the resolved and unresolved galaxy stellar mass estimation from the perspective of JWST
creator: Jie Song, GuanWen Fang, Zesen Lin, Yizhou Gu, Xu Kong
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Jie Song, GuanWen Fang, Zesen Lin, Yizhou Gu, Xu Kong. By utilizing the spatially-resolved photometry of galaxies at 0.2 < z < 3.0 0.2<z<3.0 in the CEERS field, we estimate the resolved and unresolved stellar mass via spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting to study the discrepancy between them. We first compare M ∗ M_{\ast} derived from photometry with and without the JWST wavelength coverage and find that M ∗ M_{\ast} can be overestimated by up to 0.2 dex when lacking rest-frame NIR data.

title: Super-early JWST galaxies, outflows and Ly α \alpha visibility in the EoR
creator: Andrea Ferrara
description: Abstract The overabundance of super-early (redshift z > 10 z>10 ), luminous ( M UV < − 20 M_{\rm UV}<-20 ), and blue galaxies detected by JWST has been explained ( Ferrara et al. 2023 ) as due to negligible dust attenuation in these systems.

title: On integrability of the one-dimensional Hubbard model
creator: A. Melikyan
description: Abstract We find a family of solutions to Zamolodchikov’s tetrahedral algebra corresponding to the fermionic R R -operator for the free fermion model of the difference type in one of the spectral parameters, construct an extension of the R R -operator for a system of two spins satisfying the Yang-Baxter equation, and find the local charges.

title: Dissipationless Nonlinearity in Quantum Material Josephson Diodes
creator: Constantin Schrade, Valla Fatemi
description: Abstract Dissipationless nonlinearities for three-wave mixing are a key component of many superconducting quantum devices, such as amplifiers and bosonic qubits. So far, such third-order nonlinearities have been primarily achieved with circuits of concatenated Josephson tunnel junctions. In this work, we theoretically develop an alternative approach to realize third-order nonlinearities from gate-tunable and intrinsically symmetry-broken quantum material Josephson junctions.

title: Search for dark matter particles in \PWp \PWm events with transverse momentum imbalance in proton-proton collisions at s = 13 ​ \TeV \sqrt{s}=13\TeV
creator: The CMS Collaboration
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by The CMS Collaboration. A search for dark matter particles is performed using events with a pair of \PW bosons and large missing transverse momentum. Candidate events are selected by requiring one or two leptons ( \Pell = \Pell= electrons or muons). The analysis is based on proton-proton collision data collected at a center-of-mass energy of 13 \TeV by the CMS experiment at the LHC and corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 138 \fbinv .

title: First-principles study of the magnetic anisotropy of ultrathin B-, C-, and N-doped FeCo films
creator: Joanna Marciniak, Mirosław Werwiński, Justyna Rychły-Gruszecka
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Joanna Marciniak, Mirosław Werwiński, Justyna Rychły-Gruszecka. Iron-based layered systems are of great interest because of their ability to tune effective material parameters such as magnetic anisotropy energy (MAE). The influence of the crystallographic structure of Fe, its thickness, and the presence of other layers above and below the Fe layer on magnetic parameters, such as the MAE of the studied system, is an intriguing and important topic from an application point of view.

title: An almost dark galaxy with the mass of the Small Magellanic Cloud
creator: Mireia Montes, Ignacio Trujillo, Ananthan Karunakaran, Raúl Infante-Sainz, Kristine Spekkens, Giulia Golini, Michael Beasley, Maria Cebrián, Nushkia Chamba, Mauro D’Onofrio, Lee Kelvin, Javier Román
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Mireia Montes, Ignacio Trujillo, Ananthan Karunakaran, Raúl Infante-Sainz, Kristine Spekkens, Giulia Golini, Michael Beasley, Maria Cebrián, Nushkia Chamba, Mauro D’Onofrio, Lee Kelvin, Javier Román. Almost Dark Galaxies are objects that have eluded detection by traditional surveys such as the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS).

title: Direct Neural Machine Translation with Task-level Mixture of Experts models
creator: Isidora Chara Tourni, Subhajit Naskar
description: Abstract Direct neural machine translation (direct NMT) is a type of NMT system that translates text between two non-English languages. Direct NMT systems often face limitations due to the scarcity of parallel data between non-English language pairs. Several approaches have been proposed to address this limitation, such as multilingual NMT and pivot NMT (translation between two languages via English).

title: LATIS: The Stellar Mass-Metallicity Relation of Star-forming Galaxies at z ∼ 2.5 z\sim 2.5 NumPy ( Harris et al. 2020 ) , Matplotlib ( Hunter 2007 ) , Astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2013 ; Astropy Collaboration et al. 2018 ; Astropy Collaboration et al. 2022 ) , PyMultiNest ( Buchner et al.
creator: Nima Chartab, Andrew B. Newman, Gwen C. Rudie, Guillermo A. Blanc, Daniel D. Kelson
description: Abstract We present the stellar mass - stellar metallicity relation for 3491 star-forming galaxies at 2 ≲ z ≲ 3 2\lesssim z\lesssim 3 using rest-frame far-ultraviolet (FUV) spectra from the Ly α \alpha Tomography IMACS Survey (LATIS). We fit stellar population synthesis models from the Binary Population And Spectral Synthesis code (BPASS v 2.2.1 2.2.

title: Dynamical Friction Models for Black-Hole Binary Formation in AGN Disks Journal: ApJ IAS15 ( Rein & Spiegel 2015 ) , Matplotlib ( Hunter 2007 ) , NumPy ( van der Walt et al. 2011 ) , Rebound ( Rein & Liu 2012 ) , SciPy ( Virtanen et al. 2020 )
creator: Kecheng Qian, Jiaru Li, Dong Lai
description: Abstract Stellar-mass black holes (sBH) embedded in gaseous disks of active galactic nuclei (AGN) can be important sources of detectable gravitational radiation for LIGO/Virgo when they form binaries and coalesce due to orbital decay. In this paper, we study the effect of gas dynamical friction (DF) on the formation of BH binaries in AGN disks using N N -body simulations.

title: Subaru High- z z Exploration of Low-luminosity Quasars (SHELLQs). XVII. Black Hole Mass Distribution at 𝒛 ∼ 𝟔 z\sim 6 Estimated via Spectral Comparison with Low- 𝒛 z Quasars
creator: Ayumi Takahashi, Yoshiki Matsuoka, Masafusa Onoue, Michael A. Strauss, Nobunari Kashikawa, Yoshiki Toba, Kazushi Iwasawa, Masatoshi Imanishi, Masayuki Akiyama, Toshihiro Kawaguchi, Akatoki Noboriguchi, Chien-Hsiu Lee
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Ayumi Takahashi, Yoshiki Matsuoka, Masafusa Onoue, Michael A. Strauss, Nobunari Kashikawa, Yoshiki Toba, Kazushi Iwasawa, Masatoshi Imanishi, Masayuki Akiyama, Toshihiro Kawaguchi, Akatoki Noboriguchi, Chien-Hsiu Lee. We report the distribution of black hole (BH) masses and Eddingont ratios estimated for a sample of 131 low luminosity quasars in the early cosmic epoch ( 5.6 < z < 7.0 5.6<z<7.0 ).

title: Revamp : Automated Simulations of Adversarial Attacks on Arbitrary Objects in Realistic Scenes
creator: Matthew Hull, Zijie J. Wang, Duen Horng (Polo) Chau
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Matthew Hull, Zijie J. Wang, Duen Horng (Polo) Chau. Deep Learning models, such as those used in an autonomous vehicle are vulnerable to adversarial attacks where an attacker could place an adversarial object in the environment, leading to mis-classification. Generating these adversarial objects in the digital space has been extensively studied, however successfully transferring these attacks from the digital realm to the physical realm has proven challenging when controlling for real-world environmental factors.

title: Mechanisms of scrambling and unscrambling of quantum information in the ground state in spin chains: domain-walls, spin-flips and scattering phase shifts
creator: Samudra Sur 1 and Diptiman Sen 1,2
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Samudra Sur 1 and Diptiman Sen 1,2. The spatiotemporal evolution of the out-of-time-order correlator (OTOC) measures the propagation and scrambling of local quantum information. For the transverse field Ising model with open boundaries, the local operator σ x \sigma^{x} shows an interesting picture of the ground state OTOC where the local information gets scrambled throughout the entire system and, more strikingly, starts ‘unscrambling’ upon reflection at the other end.

title: Searching for Mass Concentrations with Precision Pulsar Timing
creator: John M. LoSecco
description: Abstract This papers searches for evidence of mass concentrations along the path of radio pulses in the PPTA2 survey data release. Radio pulse travel times are influenced via gravitational fields along the path from the source to the observer. Transient time delays in transit are a useful measure of the matter distribution along the path.

title: InferDPT : Privacy-preserving Inference for Black-box Large Language Models This work was supported in part by the National Natural Science Foundation of China under Grant U2436601, 62472398, U2336206, and 62121002 , and by the Open Foundation of Key Laboratory of Cyberspace Security, Ministry of Ed
creator: Meng Tong, Kejiang Chen, Jie Zhang, Yuang Qi, Weiming Zhang, Nenghai Yu, Tianwei Zhang, Zhikun Zhang
description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs), represented by ChatGPT, have greatly simplified text generation tasks. However, they have also raised concerns about privacy risks such as data leakage and unauthorized information collection. Existing solutions for privacy-preserving inference face practical challenges related to computational time and communication costs.

title: Superconductivity in the Two-Orbital Hubbard Model of Infinite-Layer Nickelates
creator: Zhihui Luo, Dao-Xin Yao, Wéi Wú
description: Abstract The pairing symmetry in infinite-layer nickelate superconductors has been an intriguing problem under heated debates. In this work, we study a two-orbital Hubbard model with one strongly correlated 3 ​ d 3d orbital and one more itinerant 5 ​ d 5d orbital, by using an eight-site cellular dynamic mean field theory study.

title: Variations of Interstellar Gas-to-Dust Ratios at High Galactic Latitudes
creator: J. Michael Shull, Georgia V. Panopoulou
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by J. Michael Shull, Georgia V. Panopoulou. Interstellar dust at high Galactic latitudes can influence astronomical foreground subtraction, produce diffuse scattered light, and soften the ultraviolet spectra of quasars. In a sample of 94 sight lines toward quasars at high latitude and low extinction, we evaluate the interstellar “gas-to-dust ratio” N H / E ⁡ ( B − V ) N_{\rm H}/E(B-V) , using hydrogen column densities (H I and H 2 ) and far-infrared estimates of dust reddening.

title: Comparing first-principles density functionals plus corrections for the lattice dynamics of YBa 2 Cu 3 O 6
creator: Jinliang Ning, Christopher Lane, Bernardo Barbiellini, Robert S. Markiewicz, Arun Bansil, Adrienn Ruzsinszky, John P. Perdew, Jianwei Sun
description: Abstract The enigmatic mechanism underlying unconventional high-temperature superconductivity, especially the role of lattice dynamics, has remained a subject of debate. Theoretical insights have long been hindered due to the lack of an accurate first-principles description of the lattice dynamics of cuprates.

title: Mapping Physical Conditions in Neighboring Hot Cores: NOEMA Studies of W3( H 2 ​ O \text{H}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}}\text{O} ) and W3(OH) Astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2013 ; Astropy Collaboration et al. 2018 ; Astropy Collaboration et al. 2022 )
creator: Morgan M. Giese, Will E. Thompson, Dariusz C. Lis, Susanna L. Widicus Weaver
description: Abstract The complex chemistry that occurs in star-forming regions can provide insight into the formation of prebiotic molecules at various evolutionary stages of star formation. To study this process, we present millimeter-wave interferometric observations of the neighboring hot cores W3( H 2 ​ O \text{H}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}}\text{O} ) and W3(OH) carried out using the NOEMA interferometer.

title: Optimizing edge-state transfer in a Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain via hybrid analog-digital strategies
creator: Sebastián V. Romero, Xi Chen, Gloria Platero, Yue Ban
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Sebastián V. Romero, Xi Chen, Gloria Platero, Yue Ban. The Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chain, which serves as a paradigmatic model for comprehending topological phases and their associated edge states, plays an essential role in advancing our understanding of quantum materials and quantum information processing and technology. In this paper, we introduce a hybrid analog-digital protocol designed for the nonadiabatic yet high-fidelity transfer of edge states in an SSH chain, featuring two sublattices, A and B.

title: The p − p- parabolicity under a decay assumption on the Ricci curvature
creator: L. S. Priebe, R. B. Soares
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by L. S. Priebe, R. B. Soares. We prove that, given α > 0 \alpha>0 , if M M is a complete Riemannian manifold which Ricci curvature satisfies. title: On the positivity of the hypergeometric Veneziano amplitude
description: Abstract Recently, an infinite family of one-parameter generalisations of the Veneziano amplitude were bootstrapped using as input assumptions an integer mass spectrum, crossing symmetry, high-energy boundedness, and exchange of finite spins. This new result was dubbed the hypergeometric Veneziano amplitude, with a real-valued deformation parameter r.

title: On the Space Usage of Approximate Distance Oracles with Sub-2 Stretch Thanks: This work is partially supported by Israel Science Foundation (ISF) grant no. 1926/19 and by United States - Israel Binational Science Foundation (BSF) grant no. 2018364. Contact: kopelot.biu@gmail.com, korinariel10@gmail.
creator: Tsvi Kopelowitz, Ariel Korin, Liam Roditty Bar-Ilan University, Ramat Gan, Israel
description: Abstract For an undirected unweighted graph G = ( V , E ) G=(V,E) with n n vertices and m m edges, let d ⁡ ( u , v ) d(u,v) denote the distance from u ∈ V u\in V to v ∈ V v\in V in G G .

title: Does Quarkonia Suppression serve as a probe for the deconfinement in small systems?
creator: Partha Bagchi, Arpan Das, Ananta P. Mishra
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Partha Bagchi, Arpan Das, Ananta P. Mishra. In high multiplicity proton-proton ( p − p ) (p-p) collisions, the formation of a deconfined state of quarks and gluons akin to Heavy Ion Collisions (HIC) has been a subject of significant interest.

title: Walraswap: a solution to uniform price batch auctions
creator: Sergio Andrés Yuhjtman, Flashbots
description: Abstract Consider a finite set of trade orders and automated market makers (AMMs) at some state. We propose a solution to the problem of finding an equilibrium price vector to execute all the orders jointly with corresponding optimal AMMs swaps. The solution is based on Brouwer’s fixed-point theorem. We discuss computational aspects relevant for realistic situations in public blockchain activity.

title: Statistical Mechanics of Exponentially Many Low Lying States
creator: Swapnamay Mondal
description: Abstract It has recently been argued that for near-extremal black holes, the entropy and the energy above extremality respectively receive a l ​ o ​ g ​ T logT and a T T -linear correction, where T T is the temperature.

title: Spectral theory of p p -adic unitary operator
creator: Zhao Tianhong
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Zhao Tianhong. The p p -adic unitary operator U U is defined as an invertible operator on p p -adic ultrametric Banach space such that | U | = | U − 1 | = 1 \left|U\right|=\left|U^{-1}\right|=1 . We point out U U has a spectral measure valued in projection functors , which can be explained as the measure theory on the formal group scheme. The spectrum decomposition of U U is complete when ψ \psi is a p p -adic wave function.

title: An Image is Worth Multiple Words: Learning Object Level Concepts using Multi-Concept Prompt Learning
creator: Chen Jin, Ryutaro Tanno, Amrutha Saseendran, Tom Diethe, Philip Teare
description: Abstract Textural Inversion, a prompt learning method, learns a singular embedding for a new “word” to represent image style and appearance, allowing it to be integrated into natural language sentences to generate novel synthesised images. However, identifying and integrating multiple object-level concepts within one scene poses significant challenges even when embeddings for individual concepts are attainable.

title: Emergent Symmetries and Interactions in High Dimensions: An Isolated Fixed Point Versus A Manifold of Strongly Interacting Fixed Points
creator: Fei Zhou
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Fei Zhou. In this article, we explore conditions of continuous emergent symmetries in gapless states, either as topological quantum critical points (TQCPs) or a stable phase with protecting symmetries and connections to smooth deformations of the gapped states around.

title: Weakly-Popular and Super-Popular Matchings with Ties and Their Connection to Stable Matchings
creator: Gergely Csáji (HUN-REN KRTK KTI)
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Gergely Csáji (HUN-REN KRTK KTI). In this paper, we study a slightly different definition of popularity in bipartite graphs G = ( U , W , E ) G=(U,W,E) with two-sided preferences, when ties are present in the preference lists.

title: Channel Estimation via Loss Field: Accurate Site-Trained Modeling for Shadowing Prediction
creator: Jie Wang 1, Meles G. Weldegebriel, Neal Patwari
description: Abstract Future mobile ad hoc networks will share spectrum between many users. Channels will be assigned on the fly to guarantee signal and interference power requirements for requested links. Channel losses must be re-estimated between many pairs of users as they move and as environmental conditions change.

title: Towards Simpler Sorting Networks and Monotone Circuits for Majority
creator: Natalia Dobrokhotova-Maikova, Alexander Kozachinskiy, Vladimir Podolskii
description: Abstract In this paper, we study the problem of computing the majority function by low-depth monotone circuits and a related problem of constructing low-depth sorting networks. We consider both the classical setting with elementary operations of arity 2 2 and the generalized setting with operations of arity k k , where k k is a parameter.

title: Enhancing the Performance of Automated Grade Prediction in MOOC using Graph Representation Learning Thanks: † These authors have an affiliation with Data Science and Applications Lab at Utah State University.
creator: Soheila Farokhi †, Aswani Yaramal †, Jiangtao Huang, Muhammad Fawad Akbar Khan †, Xiaojun Qi, Hamid Karimi †
description: Abstract In recent years, Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs) have gained significant traction as a rapidly growing phenomenon in online learning. Unlike traditional classrooms, MOOCs offer a unique opportunity to cater to a diverse audience from different backgrounds and geographical locations. Renowned universities and MOOC-specific providers, such as Coursera, offer MOOC courses on various subjects.

title: Fact-based Agent modeling for Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
creator: Baofu Fang, Caiming Zheng, Hao Wang
description: Abstract In multi-agent systems, agents need to interact and collaborate with other agents in environments. Agent modeling is crucial to facilitate agent interactions and make adaptive cooperation strategies. However, it is challenging for agents to model the beliefs, behaviors, and intentions of other agents in non-stationary environment where all agent policies are learned simultaneously.

title: Quantum teleportation implies symmetry-protected topological order
creator: Yifan Hong, David T. Stephen, Aaron J. Friedman
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Yifan Hong, David T. Stephen, Aaron J. Friedman. We constrain a broad class of teleportation protocols using insights from locality. In the “standard” teleportation protocols we consider, all outcome-dependent unitaries are Pauli operators conditioned on linear functions of the measurement outcomes. We find that all such protocols involve preparing a “resource state” exhibiting symmetry-protected topological (SPT) order with Abelian protecting symmetry 𝒢 k = ( ℤ 2 × ℤ 2 ) k \mathcal{G}_{k}=(\mathbb{Z}^{\,}_{2}\times\mathbb{Z}^{\,}_{2})^{k} .

title: Coincidences between intervals in two partial orders on complex reflection groups
creator: Joel Brewster Lewis, Jiayuan Wang
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Joel Brewster Lewis, Jiayuan Wang. In a finite real reflection group, the reflection length of each element is equal to the codimension of its fixed space, and the two coincident functions determine a partial order structure called the absolute order. In complex reflection groups, the reflection length is no longer always equal to the codimension of fixed space, and the two functions give rise to two different partial orders on the group.

title: Multi-domain analysis and prediction of the light emitted by an inductively coupled plasma jet
creator: Lorenzo Capponi, Alberto Padovan, Gregory S. Elliott, Marco Panesi, Daniel J. Bodony, Francesco Panerai
description: Abstract Inductively coupled plasma wind tunnels are crucial for replicating hypersonic flight conditions in ground testing. Achieving the desired conditions (e.g., stagnation-point heat fluxes and enthalpies during atmospheric reentry) requires a careful selection of operating inputs, such as mass flow, gas composition, nozzle geometry, torch power, chamber pressure, and probing location along the plasma jet.

title: Smooth Symmetric Transonic Isothermal Flows with Nonzero Angular Velocity
creator: Na Zhang
description: Abstract In this paper, the steady inviscid flows with radial symmetry for the isothermal Euler system are studied in an annulus. We present a complete classification of transonic radially symmetric flow patterns in term of physical boundary conditions at the inner and outer circle.

title: A characterization of 4-connected graphs with no K 3 , 3 + v K_{3,3}+v -minor
creator: Linsong Wei, Yuqi Xu, Weihua Yang, Yunxia Zhang
description: Abstract Abstract: Among graphs with 13 edges, there are exactly three internally 4-connected graphs which are Oct^{+} , cube+e and K_{3,3}+v . A complete characterization of all 4-connected graphs with no Oct^{+} -minor is given in [John Maharry, An excluded minor theorem for the octahedron plus an edge, Journal of Graph Theory 57(2) (2008) 124-130].

title: Symbolic Defect of Monomial Ideals
creator: Benjamin Oltsik
description: Abstract . Given a monomial ideal I I , we study two functions that quantify ways to measure the difference between symbolic powers and usual powers of I I . In many cases we determine the asymptotic growth rate of these two functions. We also perform explicit computations by using the symbolic polyhedron.

title: On the topology of conormal complexes and posets of matroids
creator: Anastasia Nathanson, Ethan Partida
description: Abstract . We introduce the poset of biflats of a matroid M M , a Lagrangian analog of the lattice of flats of M M , and study the topology of its order complex, which we call the biflats complex.

title: Generalized time-reversal symmetry and effective theories for nonequilibrium matter
creator: Xiaoyang Huang, Jack H. Farrell, Aaron J. Friedman, Isabella Zane, Paolo Glorioso, Andrew Lucas
description: Abstract The past decade has witnessed the development of systematic effective theories for dissipative thermal systems. Here, we describe an analogous effective theory framework that applies to the classical stochastic dynamics of nonequilibrium systems. We illustrate this approach using a range of examples, including nonreciprocal (predator-prey) dynamics, dissipative and driven rigid-body motion, and active chiral fluids and solids.

title: Topologies for geometric flows and continuous dependence on parameters
creator: Andrew D. Lewis, Yanlei Zhang
description: Abstract We study time- and parameter-dependent ordinary differential equations in the geometric setting of vector fields and their flows. Various degrees of regularities in state are considered, including Lipschitz, finitely diferentiable, smooth, and holomorphic. A suitable topology for the space of flows is derived using geometric descriptions of suitable topologies for vector fields.

title: Instantaneous Frequency Estimation in Unbalanced Systems Using Affine Differential Geometry Thanks: A. Alshawabkeh, G. Tzounas and F. Milano are with the School of Electrical and Electronic Engineering, University College Dublin, Dublin, D04V1W8, Ireland. Á. Molina-García is with the Department of E
creator: Ali Alshawabkeh, Georgios Tzounas, Ángel Molina-García
description: Abstract The paper discusses the relationships between electrical and affine differential geometry quantities, establishing a link between frequency and time derivatives of voltage, through the utilization of affine geometric invariants. Based on this link, a new instantaneous frequency estimation formula is proposed, which is particularly suited for unbalanced and single-phase systems.

title: Adjoint-based inversion for stress and frictional parameters in earthquake modeling
creator: Vidar Stiernström, Martin Almquist, Eric M. Dunham
description: Abstract We present an adjoint-based optimization method to invert for stress and frictional parameters used in earthquake modeling. The forward problem is linear elastodynamics with nonlinear rate-and-state frictional faults. The misfit functional quantifies the difference between simulated and measured particle displacements or velocities at receiver locations. The misfit may include windowing or filtering operators.

title: Well-posedness and trend to equilibrium for the Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck system with a confining potential
creator: Gayrat Toshpulatov
description: Abstract We study well-posedness and long time behavior of the nonlinear Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck system with an external confining potential. The system describes the time evolution of particles (e.g. in a plasma) undergoing diffusion, friction and Coulomb interaction. We prove existence and uniqueness of mild solutions in a weighted Sobolev space.

title: Real-Variable Theory for New Herz-Type Hardy Spaces Associated with Ball Quasi-Banach Function Spaces 0 0 footnotetext: 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification . Primary 42B30; Secondary 42B35, 46E30. Key words and phrases. Herz-type Hardy space, ball quasi-Banach function space, maximal function, a
creator: Aiting Wang, Wenhua Wang, Mingquan Wei
description: Abstract Abstract Let X be a ball quasi-Banach function space, \alpha\in\mathbb{R} and q\in(0,\infty) . In this paper, the authors first introduce the new Herz-type Hardy spaces \mathcal{H\dot{K}}_{X}^{\alpha,\,q}({\mathbb{R}}^{n}) and \mathcal{HK}_{X}^{\alpha,\,q}({\mathbb{R}}^{n}) associated with ball quasi-Banach function space X , via the non-tangential grand maximal function.

title: Crossing beyond scattering amplitudes
creator: Simon Caron-Huot, Mathieu Giroux, Holmfridur S. Hannesdottir, Sebastian Mizera
description: Abstract We find that different asymptotic measurements in quantum field theory can be related to one another through new versions of crossing symmetry . Assuming analyticity, we conjecture generalized crossing relations for multi-particle processes and the corresponding paths of analytic continuation. We prove them to all multiplicity at tree-level in quantum field theory and string theory.

title: Overview of the EUSO-SPB2 Target of Opportunity program using the Cherenkov Telescope
creator: Tonia M. Venters
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Tonia M. Venters. During the Extreme Universe Space Observatory on a Super Pressure Balloon 2 (EUSO-SPB2) mission, we planned Target of Opportunity (ToO) operations to follow up on possible sources of ≳ 10 ​ PeV \gtrsim 10\,{\rm PeV} neutrinos. The original plan before flight was to point the onboard Cherenkov Telescope (CT) to catch the source’s path on the sky just below Earth’s horizon.

title: Twisted bilayer graphene revisited: minimal two-band model for low-energy bands
creator: Daniel Bennett, Daniel T. Larson, Louis Sharma, Stephen Carr, Efthimios Kaxiras
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Daniel Bennett, Daniel T. Larson, Louis Sharma, Stephen Carr, Efthimios Kaxiras. An accurate description of the low-energy electronic bands in twisted bilayer graphene (tBLG) is of great interest due to their relation to correlated electron phases such as superconductivity and Mott-insulator behavior at half-filling.

title: Sobolev orthogonal polynomials: Connection formulae
creator: Roberto S. Costas-Santos
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Roberto S. Costas-Santos. This contribution aims to obtain several connection formulae for the polynomial sequence, which is orthogonal with respect to the discrete Sobolev inner product ⟨ f , g ⟩ n = ⟨ 𝐮 , f ​ g ⟩ + ∑ j = 1 M μ j ​ f ( ν j ) ​ ( c j ) ​ g ( ν j ) ​ ( c j ) , \langle f,g\rangle_{n}=\langle{\bf u},fg\rangle+\sum_{j=1}^{M}\mu_{j}f^{(\nu_{j})}(c_{j})g^{(\nu_{j})}(c_{j}), where 𝐮 {\bf u} is a classical linear functional, c

title: Tight upper bound of genuine four party Svetlichny type nonlocality with and without local filtering
creator: Sk Sahadat Hossain, Biswajit Paul, Indrani Chattopadhyay, Debasis Sarkar
description: Abstract Identifying the nonlocality of a multiparty quantum state is an important task in quantum mechanics. Seevinck and Svetlichny [Phys. Rev. Lett. 89, 060401 (2002)], and independently, Collins and co-workers [Phys. Rev. Lett. 88, 170405 (2002)] have generalized the tripartite notion of Svetlichny nonlocality to n-parties.

title: Conditions for the existence of positive operator valued measures
creator: Maximilian Schumacher, Gernot Alber
description: Abstract Sufficient and necessary conditions are presented for the existence of ( N , M ) (N,M) -positive operator valued measures ( ( N , M ) (N,M) -POVMs) valid for arbitrary-dimensional quantum systems. A sufficient condition for the existence of ( N , M ) (N,M) -POVMs is presented.

title: A Unifying Framework for Learning Argumentation Semantics
creator: Zlatina Mileva, Antonis Bikakis, Fabio Aurelio D’Asaro, Mark Law, Alessandra Russo
description: Abstract Argumentation is a very active research field of Artificial Intelligence concerned with the representation and evaluation of arguments used in dialogues between humans and/or artificial agents. Acceptability semantics of formal argumentation systems define the criteria for the acceptance or rejection of arguments.

title: Micro-seismic Elastic Reflection Full Waveform Inversion with An Equivalent Source
creator: Hanchen Wang, Qiang Guo, Tariq Alkhalifah
description: Abstract In micro-seismic event measurements, pinpointing the passive source’s exact spatial and temporal location is paramount. This research advocates for the combined use of both P- and S-wave data, captured by geophone monitoring systems, to improve source inversion accuracy. Drawing inspiration from the secondary source concept in Elastic Reflection Full Waveform Inversion (ERFWI), we introduce an equivalent source term.

title: Gravitational form factors of light nuclei: Impulse approximation
creator: Fangcheng He, Ismail Zahed
description: Abstract The gravitational form factors of light nuclei are evaluated up to momenta of the order of the nucleon mass, using the impulse approximation. The nucleon gravitational form factors are reduced non-relativistically, and used to derive the gravitational form factors of light nuclei. The deuteron gravitational form factors are analysed using the Reid soft core potential.

title: RZ Piscium Hosts a Compact and Highly Perturbed Debris Disk Facilities: Spitzer (IRAC), WISE, ALMA, IRSA, AAVSO
creator: Kate Y. L. Su, Grant M. Kennedy, G. H. Rieke, A. Meredith Hughes, Yu-Chia Lin, Jamar Kittling, Alan P. Jackson, Ramya M. Anche, Hauyu Baobab Liu
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Kate Y. L. Su, Grant M. Kennedy, G. H. Rieke, A. Meredith Hughes, Yu-Chia Lin, Jamar Kittling, Alan P. Jackson, Ramya M. Anche, Hauyu Baobab Liu. RZ Piscium (RZ Psc) is well-known in the variable star field because of its numerous, irregular optical dips in the past five decades, but the nature of the system is heavily debated in the literature.

title: Studies of new Higgs boson interactions through nonresonant H ​ H HH production in the b ​ b ¯ ​ γ ​ γ b\bar{b}\gamma\gamma final state in p ​ p pp collisions at s = 13 \sqrt{s}=13 TeV with the ATLAS detector
creator: The ATLAS Collaboration
description: Abstract A search for nonresonant Higgs boson pair production in the b ​ b ¯ ​ γ ​ γ b\bar{b}\gamma\gamma final state is performed using 140 fb -1 of proton–proton collisions at a centre-of-mass energy of 13 TeV recorded by the ATLAS detector at the CERN Large Hadron Collider.

title: Rotating Black Hole in Kalb-Ramond Gravity: Constraining Parameters by Comparison with EHT Observations of Sgr A* and M87*
creator: M. Zubair, Muhammad Ali Raza, Eiman Maqsood
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by M. Zubair, Muhammad Ali Raza, Eiman Maqsood. This article deals with the study of some properties of the static and rotating black holes in Kalb-Ramond gravity in four dimensional spacetime. First, we discuss the action of the corresponding theory and the static black hole metric. Then we investigate the light sphere for the static black hole by using the Hamiltonian formalism and the corresponding linear radius of the shadow, angular velocity and Lyapunov exponent. For the rotating black hole, we discuss the horizon structure.

title: AGN Selection and Demographics: A New Age with JWST/MIRI Journal: ApJ
creator: Jianwei Lyu (吕建伟), Stacey Alberts, George H. Rieke, Irene Shivaei, Pablo G. Pérez-González, Fengwu Sun, Kevin N. Hainline, Stefi Baum, Nina Bonaventura, Andrew J. Bunker, Eiichi Egami, Daniel J. Eisenstein, Michael Florian, Zhiyuan Ji, Benjamin D. Johnson, Jane Morrison, Marcia Rieke, Brant Robertso
description: Abstract Understanding the co-evolution of supermassive black holes (SMBHs) and their host systems requires a comprehensive census of active galactic nuclei (AGN) behavior across a wide range of redshift, luminosity, obscuration level and galaxy properties. We report significant progress with JWST towards this goal from the Systematic Mid-infrared Instrument Legacy Extragalactic Survey (SMILES).

title: Soccer on Social Media
creator: Mehdi Houshmand Sarkhoosh, Sayed Mohammad Majidi Dorcheh, Sushant Gautam, Cise Midoglu, Saeed Shafiee Sabet, Pål Halvorsen
description: Abstract Comparative Analysis of Social Media Strategies Used by European Soccer Leagues and Teams keywords soccer/association football, multimedia, social media strategy, followers, visitor engagement, content cadence, website traffic Abstract In the era of digitalization, social media has become an integral part of our lives, serving as a significant hub for individuals and businesses to share information, communicate, and engage.

title: The JADES Origins Field: A New JWST Deep Field in the JADES Second NIRCam Data Release
creator: Daniel J. Eisenstein, Benjamin D. Johnson, Brant Robertson, Sandro Tacchella, Kevin Hainline, Peter Jakobsen, Roberto Maiolino, Nina Bonaventura, Andrew J. Bunker, Alex J. Cameron, Phillip A. Cargile, Emma Curtis-Lake, Ryan Hausen, Dávid Puskás, Marcia Rieke, Fengwu Sun, Christopher N. A. Willmer, C
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Daniel J. Eisenstein, Benjamin D. Johnson, Brant Robertson, Sandro Tacchella, Kevin Hainline, Peter Jakobsen, Roberto Maiolino, Nina Bonaventura, Andrew J. Bunker, Alex J. Cameron, Phillip A. Cargile, Emma Curtis-Lake, Ryan Hausen, Dávid Puskás, Marcia Rieke, Fengwu Sun, Christopher N. A. Willmer, C. We summarize the properties and initial data release of the JADES Origins Field (JOF), which will soon be the deepest imaging field yet observed with the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST).

title: Some applications of Gröbner-Shirshov bases to Lie algebras
creator: Luis Mendonça
description: Abstract . We show that if a countably generated Lie algebra H H does not contain isomorphic copies of certain finite-dimensional nilpotent Lie algebras A A and B B (satisfying some mild conditions), then H H embeds into a quotient of A ∗ B A\ast B that is at the same time hopfian and cohopfian.

title: Upper bound for the grand canonical free energy of the Bose gas in the Gross-Pitaevskii limit for general interaction potentials
creator: Marco Caporaletti, Andreas Deuchert
description: Abstract We consider a homogeneous Bose gas in the Gross–Pitaevskii limit at temperatures that are comparable to the critical temperature for Bose–Einstein condensation. Recently, an upper bound for the grand canonical free energy was proved in [ 13 ] capturing two novel contributions.

title: Parisi’s hypercube, Fock-space fluxes, and the microscopics of near-AdS 2 /near-CFT 1 duality
creator: Micha Berkooz, Yiyang Jia, Navot Silberstein
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Micha Berkooz, Yiyang Jia, Navot Silberstein. Parisi’s hypercube model describes a charged particle hopping on a d d -dimensional hypercube with disordered background fluxes in the large d d limit. It was noted previously [Jia and Verbaarschot, J. 11 (2020) 154] that the hypercube model at leading order in 1 / d 1/d has the same spectral density as the double-scaled Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (DS-SYK) model.

title: Price dispersion across online platforms: Evidence from hotel room prices in London (UK) Thanks: The authors are grateful to Frank Verboven, Jan De Loecker, Jo Van Biesebroeck, Luis Vasconcelos, for invaluable help, advice, and encouragement. We sincerely thank the editor and the two anonymous refer
creator: Debashrita Mohapatra, Debi Prasad Mohapatra, Ram Sewak Dubey
description: Abstract This paper studies the widespread price dispersion of homogeneous products across different online platforms, even when consumers can easily access price information from comparison websites. We collect data for the 200 most popular hotels in London (UK) and document that prices vary widely across booking sites while making reservations for a hotel room.

title: New Environment Adaptation with Few Shots for OFDM Receiver and mmWave Beamforming
creator: Ouya Wang, Shenglong Zhou, Geoffrey Ye Li
description: Abstract Few-shot learning (FSL) enables adaptation to new tasks with only limited training data. In wireless communications, channel environments can vary drastically; therefore, FSL techniques can quickly adjust transceiver accordingly. In this paper, we develop two FSL frameworks that fit in wireless transceiver design.

title: VisGrader : Automatic Grading of D3 Visualizations
creator: Matthew Hull, Vivian Pednekar, Hannah Murray, Nimisha Roy, Emmanuel Tung, Susanta Routray, Connor Guerin, Justin Chen, Zijie J. Wang, Seongmin Lee, Mahdi Roozbahani, and Duen Horng Chau
description: Abstract Manually grading D3 data visualizations is a challenging endeavor, and is especially difficult for large classes with hundreds of students. Grading an interactive visualization requires a combination of interactive, quantitative, and qualitative evaluation that are conventionally done manually and are difficult to scale up as the visualization complexity, data size, and number of students increase.

title: Equipping Federated Graph Neural Networks with Structure-aware Group Fairness
creator: Nan Cui, Xiuling Wang, Wendy Hui Wang, Violet Chen, Yue Ning
description: Abstract Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have been widely used for various types of graph data processing and analytical tasks in different domains. Training GNNs over centralized graph data can be infeasible due to privacy concerns and regulatory restrictions. Thus, federated learning (FL) becomes a trending solution to address this challenge in a distributed learning paradigm.

title: Developing 3D Virtual Safety Risk Terrain for UAS Operations in Complex Urban Environments Journal: Transportation Research Part C: Emerging Technologies
creator: Zhenyu Gao, John-Paul Clarke, Javid Mardanov, and Karen Marais
description: Abstract Unmanned Aerial Systems (UAS), an integral part of the Advanced Air Mobility (AAM) vision, are capable of performing a wide spectrum of tasks in urban environments. The societal integration of UAS is a pivotal challenge, as these systems must operate harmoniously within the constraints imposed by regulations and societal concerns.

title: knn-seq : Efficient, Extensible k k NN-MT Framework
creator: Hiroyuki Deguchi Hayate Hirano Tomoki Hoshino, Yuto Nishida Justin Vasselli Taro Watanabe
description: Abstract k k -nearest-neighbor machine translation ( k k NN-MT) Khandelwal et al. 2021 boosts the translation quality of a pre-trained neural machine translation (NMT) model by utilizing translation examples during decoding. Translation examples are stored in a vector database, called a datastore, which contains one entry for each target token from the parallel data it is made from.

title: Rational Catalan Numbers for Complex Reflection Groups
creator: Weston Miller
description: Abstract . Assuming standard conjectures, we show that the canonical symmetrizing trace evaluated at powers of a Coxeter element produces rational Catalan numbers for irreducible spetsial complex reflection groups. This extends a technique used by Galashin, Lam, Trinh, and Williams to uniformly prove the enumeration of their noncrossing Catalan objects for finite Coxeter groups. 1. Introduction 1.1.

title: Self-switching random walks on Erdös-Rényi random graphs feel the phase transition
creator: G. Iacobelli, G. Ost, D. Y. Takahashi
description: Abstract We study random walks on Erdös-Rényi random graphs in which, every time the random walk returns to the starting point, first an edge probability is independently sampled according to a priori measure μ \mu , and then an Erdös-Rényi random graph is sampled according to that edge probability.

title: Large Language Models for Code Analysis: Do LLMs Really Do Their Job?
creator: Chongzhou Fang, Ning Miao, Shaurya Srivastav, Jialin Liu, Ruoyu Zhang, Ruijie Fang, Asmita, Ryan Tsang, Najmeh Nazari, Han Wang, and Houman Homayoun
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Chongzhou Fang, Ning Miao, Shaurya Srivastav, Jialin Liu, Ruoyu Zhang, Ruijie Fang, Asmita, Ryan Tsang, Najmeh Nazari, Han Wang, and Houman Homayoun. Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated significant potential in the realm of natural language understanding and programming code processing tasks. Their capacity to comprehend and generate human-like code has spurred research into harnessing LLMs for code analysis purposes.

title: Van der Waals chain: a simple model for Casimir forces in dielectrics
creator: Helmut Hörner 1 , Lukas M. Rachbauer 1 , Stefan Rotter 1 , and Ulf Leonhardt 2
description: Abstract The Casimir force between dielectric bodies is well–understood, but not the Casimir force inside a dielectric, in particular its renormalization. We develop and analyse a simple model for the Casimir forces inside a medium that is completely free of renormalization and show then how renormalization emerges.

title: Retrieve-Cluster-Summarize: An Alternative to End-to-End Training for Query-specific Article Generation Conference: ; 2023; Internet arXiv CCS: Information systems Information retrieval CCS: Information systems Retrieval tasks and goals CCS: Information systems Summarization
creator: Connor Lennox, Sumanta Kashyapi, Laura Dietz
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Connor Lennox, Sumanta Kashyapi, Laura Dietz. Query-specific article generation is the task of, given a search query, generate a single article that gives an overview of the topic. We envision such articles as an alternative to presenting a ranking of search results. While generative Large Language Models (LLMs) like chatGPT also address this task, they are known to hallucinate new information, their models are secret, hard to analyze and control.

title: REMARK-LLM: A R obust and E fficient Water mark ing Framework for Generative Large Language Models
creator: Ruisi Zhang, Shehzeen Samarah Hussain, Paarth Neekhara, Farinaz Koushanfar
description: Abstract We present REMARK-LLM, a novel efficient, and robust watermarking framework designed for texts generated by large language models (LLMs). Synthesizing human-like content using LLMs necessitates vast computational resources and extensive datasets, encapsulating critical intellectual property (IP). However, the generated content is prone to malicious exploitation, including spamming and plagiarism.

title: GRI: Graph-based Relative Isomorphism of Word Embedding Spaces
creator: Muhammad Asif Ali, Yan Hu, Jianbin Qin, Di Wang
description: Abstract Automated construction of bilingual dictionaries using monolingual embedding spaces is a core challenge in machine translation. The end performance of these dictionaries relies upon the geometric similarity of individual spaces, i.e., their degree of isomorphism. Existing attempts aimed at controlling the relative isomorphism of different spaces fail to incorporate the impact of semantically related words in the training objective.

title: Property-Aware Multi-Speaker Data Simulation: A Probabilistic Modelling Technique for Synthetic Data Generation
creator: Tae Jin Park, He Huang, Coleman Hooper, Nithin Koluguri, Kunal Dhawan, Ante Jukić, Jagadeesh Balam and Boris Ginsburg
description: Abstract We introduce a sophisticated multi-speaker speech data simulator, specifically engineered to generate multi-speaker speech recordings. A notable feature of this simulator is its capacity to modulate the distribution of silence and overlap via the adjustment of statistical parameters. This capability offers a tailored training environment for developing neural models suited for speaker diarization and voice activity detection.

title: On groups occurring as absolute centers of finite groups
creator: Georgiana Fasolă, Marius Tărnăuceanu
description: Abstract Given a construction f f on groups, we say that a group G G is f f -realisable if there is a group H H such that G ≅ f ⁡ ( H ) G\cong f(H) , and completely f f -realisable if there is a group H H such that G ≅ f ⁡ ( H ) G\cong

title: Free weakly Novikov metabelian algebra of infinite rank
creator: Iritan Ferreira dos Santos, Alexey M. Kuz’min
description: Abstract . An explicit base with multiplication table is obtained for the free weakly Novikov metabelian algebra of infinite rank over an arbitrary field of characteristic ≠ 2 \neq 2 . Keywords: Right symmetric algebra, metabelian algebra, Novikov algebra, free algebra of variety. MSC 2020: 17A30, 17A50, 17D25, 17D99. 1. Introduction Weakly Novikov rings appeared in papers by E.

title: Isomorphism Classes of Idempotent Evolution Algebras Thanks: Keywords: Idempotent evolution algebra, finite field, isomorphism class, counting formula Thanks: MSC2010: primary 17D92, secondary 05A05 Thanks: * Corresponding author. Email: ymzou@uwm.edu
creator: Yangjiang Wei, Yi Ming Zou ∗
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Yangjiang Wei, Yi Ming Zou ∗. We showed that isomorphism classes of idempotent evolution algebras are in bijection with the orbits of the semidirect product group of the symmetric group and the torus, considered the combinatoric problem of enumeration of isomorphism classes for these algebras over arbitrary finite fields, derived a general counting formula, and obtained explicit formulas for the numbers of isomorphism classes in dimensions 2 2 , 3 3 , and 4 4 over any finite field.

title: The CHiME-7 Challenge: System Description and Performance of NeMo Team’s DASR System
creator: Tae Jin Park, He Huang, Ante Jukić, Kunal Dhawan, Krishna C. Puvvada, Nithin Koluguri, Nikolay Karpov, Aleksandr Laptev, Jagadeesh Balam and Boris Ginsburg
description: Abstract We present the NVIDIA NeMo team’s multi-channel speech recognition system for the 7th CHiME Challenge Distant Automatic Speech Recognition (DASR) Task, focusing on the development of a multi-channel, multi-speaker speech recognition system tailored to transcribe speech from distributed microphones and microphone arrays.

title: Nearly Optimal Bounds for Sample-Based Testing and Learning of k k -Monotone Functions
creator: Hadley Black
description: Abstract We study monotonicity testing of functions f : { 0 , 1 } d → { 0 , 1 } f\colon\{0,1\}^{d}\to\{0,1\} using sample-based algorithms, which are only allowed to observe the value of f f on points drawn independently from the uniform distribution. A classic result by Bshouty-Tamon (J.

title: Solving Hard Analogy Questions with Relation Embedding Chains
creator: Nitesh Kumar, Steven Schockaert
description: Abstract Modelling how concepts are related is a central topic in Lexical Semantics. A common strategy is to rely on knowledge graphs (KGs) such as ConceptNet, and to model the relation between two concepts as a set of paths. However, KGs are limited to a fixed set of relation types, and they are incomplete and often noisy.

title: Refutation of K2-256b and Rejection of 130 Unconfirmed Transiting Planet Candidates with Gaia DR3 NSS Note: Draft Version; not for circulation
creator: Thomas W. Tarrants, Elvis O. Mendes
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Thomas W. Tarrants, Elvis O. Mendes. Much of the exoplanet discovery efforts over the next several years are largely tasked with finding candidates for the upcoming Ariel mission. This is a role that TESS is well-suited for. Radial velocity follow-up is needed to confirm the planetary nature of these systems, as many of its planet candidates turn out to be eclipsing binary systems with small stellar secondaries. Focused Doppler follow-up to obtain these radial velocities is expensive.

title: Online Learning and Planning in Cognitive Hierarchies
creator: Bernhard Hengst, Maurice Pagnucco, David Rajaratnam
description: Abstract Complex robot behaviour typically requires the integration of multiple robotic and Artificial Intelligence (AI) techniques and components. Integrating such disparate components into a coherent system, while also ensuring global properties and behaviours, is a significant challenge for cognitive robotics. Using a formal framework to model the interactions between components can be an important step in dealing with this challenge.

title: Field theory for mechanical criticality in disordered fiber networks
creator: Sihan Chen 1,2,3,4 , Tomer Markovich 2,5,6 , Fred C. MacKintosh 1,2,7,8,9
description: Abstract Strain-controlled criticality governs the elasticity of jamming and fiber networks. While the upper critical dimension of jamming is believed to be d u = 2 d_{u}=2 , non-mean-field exponents are observed in numerical studies of 2D and 3D fiber networks. The origins of this remains unclear.

title: An O ⁡ ( log ⁡ n ) O(\log n) -Competitive Posted-Price Algorithm for Online Matching on the Line Thanks: Supported in part by NSF grants CCF-1907673, CCF-2036077, CCF-2209654 and an IBM Faculty Award.
creator: Stephen Arndt, Josh Ascher, Kirk Pruhs
description: Abstract Motivated by demand-responsive parking pricing systems, we consider posted-price algorithms for the online metric matching problem. We give an O ⁡ ( log ⁡ n ) O(\log n) -competitive posted-price randomized algorithm in the case that the metric space is a line. In particular, in this setting we show how to implement the ubiquitous guess-and-double technique using prices.

title: Countable modular groups of infinite type surfaces
creator: Rogelio Niño Hernández
description:
A 2023 arXiv research paper by Rogelio Niño Hernández. We prove that every connected, orientable infinite type surface S S without boundary and finite genus has a Riemann surface structure such that its modular group of quasiconformal homeomorphisms is countable. 1
